title: 嘉靖二十二年江西鄉試錄
text:
學正黃〔嘉樂〕□□〔自然〕教諭廖
〔芝〕劉〔三正〕金〔棌〕祝〔永順〕陳〔震〕

士三千六百有奇鎖院三試
之遵
制額掄其儁九十五人與其所爲
文二十篇以

地養萬物聖人養賢以及萬

學正黃〔嘉樂〕、□□〔自然〕，教諭廖〔芝〕、劉〔三正〕、金〔棌〕、祝〔永順〕、陳〔震〕、葉〔繼善〕、李〔資深〕、梁〔相〕、曁〔表〕，皆以徵至。届期，提調則左布政使陳〔煥〕、左參議王〔梴〕，監試則副使鄒〔守愚〕、僉事鄭〔世威〕。官方定物，展采錯事，井井理矣。乃合提學副使陸〔時雍〕所論士三千六百有奇，鎖院三試之。遵制額，掄其儁九十五人，與其所爲文二十篇以獻。
已事，〔表〕乃言曰：「順之彖曰：『天地養萬物，聖人養賢以及萬
translation_en:
…Huang Jiale, an Instructor, and □□ Ziran [?]; and the county-school Instructors Liao Zhi, Liu Sanzheng, Jin Cai, Zhu Yongshun, Chen Zhen, Ye Jishan, Li Zishen, Liang Xiang, and Ji Biao all arrived in response to summons. When the appointed time came, the Proctors were Left Administration Commissioner Chen Huan and Left Assistant Administration Commissioner Wang Chan; examination supervision was entrusted to Surveillance Vice Commissioner Zou Shouyu and Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Zheng Shiwei. Officials were assigned their duties and requisite provisions arranged; responsibilities were discharged and tasks apportioned, all in orderly fashion. They then assembled the more than 3,600 candidates assessed by Lu Shiyong, Surveillance Vice Commissioner for Education, sealed the examination compound, and examined them in three sessions. In accordance with the imperially prescribed quota, they selected ninety-five outstanding candidates and submitted their names together with twenty of their essays to the throne.
When the work was finished, Biao said: “The Commentary on the Judgment for the hexagram Shun [?; apparently Yi, ‘Nourishment’] says: ‘Heaven and earth nourish the myriad things; the sage nourishes the worthy, thereby extending nourishment to the myriad…

title: 嘉靖二十二年江西鄉試錄
text:
民鼎之彖曰聖人亨以享上
帝而大亨以養聖賢夫養賢
以及萬民所以體天地之仁
也享上帝以養聖賢所以報
天地之德也始之體仁與終
之報德拳拳焉惟聖賢之圖
嗟夫聖人之情見矣我
===
國家開基垂二百年養士之道
旣隆且備矣逮我
皇上天縱聖神嗣大歷服二十有
二年于兹
敬一有箴開天下以體仁之路
大享有禮示天下以報德之誠所
以養士之道愈隆愈備矣不
punctuated:
民」。鼎之彖曰：「聖人亨以享上帝，而大亨以養聖賢。」夫養賢以及萬民，所以體天地之仁也；享上帝以養聖賢，所以報天地之德也。始之體仁與終之報德，拳拳焉惟聖賢之圖。嗟夫！聖人之情見矣！
我國家開基垂二百年，養士之道旣隆且備矣。逮我皇上，天縱聖神，嗣大歷服二十有二年于兹。敬一有箴，開天下以體仁之路；大享有禮，示天下以報德之誠。所以養士之道愈隆愈備矣。不
translation_en:
…the myriad people.” The Commentary on the Judgment of the hexagram Ding (The Cauldron) says: “The sage cooks offerings to present to the Lord on High, and holds great feasts to nourish sages and worthies.” Nourishing worthies and thereby extending nourishment to the myriad people is the means of embodying the benevolence of Heaven and Earth; offering sacrifice to the Lord on High and nourishing sages and worthies is the means of repaying the beneficence of Heaven and Earth. From embodying benevolence at the outset to repaying beneficence at the end, the earnest concern throughout is for sages and worthies alone. Ah! Here the sage’s true feelings are revealed!
Nearly two hundred years have passed since our dynasty laid its foundations, and its provisions for nurturing scholars have become both generous and comprehensive. Now our Emperor, endowed by Heaven with sagacity and spiritual insight, has held the great imperial mandate for twenty-two years. His Admonition on Reverence for the One opens to all under Heaven the path to embodying benevolence; the rites of the Great Sacrifice demonstrate to all under Heaven his sincerity in repaying beneficence. Thus the provisions for nurturing scholars have become ever more generous and comprehensive. I do not…

title: 嘉靖二十二年江西鄉試錄
text:
知士之自養未有卓然以聖
賢自奮者乎昔者周公有曰
吾執贄而見者十人所還贄
相見者三十人貌執者百餘
人欲言而請畢事者千餘人
亦云廣矣而說者猶病其狹
焉至宋人所稱科目取士非
===
敢望拔十得五得一二足矣
何其待天下太薄也豈科目
之得人固難哉大江之西彭
蠡停涵庄廬出雲冲氣所鍾
盜之菁莪棫樸實望海內令
日所舉豈無卓然以聖賢自
奮者乎即觀爾科目之文竑
punctuated: 知士之自養，未有卓然以聖賢自奮者乎？昔者周公有曰：「吾執贄而見者十人，所還贄相見者三十人，貌執者百餘人，欲言而請畢事者千餘人。」亦云廣矣，而說者猶病其狹焉。至宋人所稱「科目取士，非敢望拔十得五，得一二足矣」，何其待天下太薄也！豈科目之得人固難哉？大江之西，彭蠡停涵，庄廬出雲，冲氣所鍾，盜之菁莪棫樸，實望海內。令日所舉，豈無卓然以聖賢自奮者乎？即觀爾科目之文，竑
translation_en:
…I wonder whether, in their self-cultivation, there are scholars who stand out in striving to become sages and worthies. Long ago, the Duke of Zhou said: “There were ten men whom I visited bearing introductory gifts; thirty whose gifts I returned when meeting them; more than a hundred whom I received with formal courtesy [?]; and more than a thousand who wished to speak and requested that I finish my business first.” This may indeed be called extensive, yet commentators still faulted it as narrow. As for the saying of men of the Song, “In selecting scholars through the examinations, we dare not hope to obtain five worthy men out of ten selected; one or two will suffice,” how little they expected of the men of the realm! Can it really be inherently difficult for the examinations to find worthy men?
West of the great river, the waters of Pengli gather, and clouds issue from Zhuanglu [?]. Here harmonious vital energies concentrate; its flourishing scholars, evoked by the luxuriant mugwort and clustered oaks of the Odes [?], are truly esteemed throughout the realm. Among those recommended today [?], can there be none who stand out in striving to become sages and worthies? Looking just at your examination writings, their expansive…

title: 嘉靖二十二年江西鄉試錄
text:
議假設罔不上嘉姚姒下景
魯鄒游夏以降若無當心者
其卓然於聖賢之塗無疑也
異時或持左券有辭于爾曰
彼云十得一二固厚也於乎
可思哉昔陸贄得韓愈歐陽
脩得蘇軾蘇轍至于今猶不
朽若令日萬一得聖賢之士
豈唯可以仰慰
===
聖天子惓惓之情而亦彰丞獬者
有吐握之風焉豈唯御史洎
諸大夫有休而人亦指〔表曰〕
是無樹蔉藙者可與也〔表之〕
采縈囿楙矣願爾多士加志
punctuated: 議假設，罔不上嘉姚姒，下景魯鄒；游夏以降，若無當心者。其卓然於聖賢之塗，無疑也。異時或持左券，有辭于爾曰：「彼云十得一二，固厚也。」於乎，可思哉！昔陸贄得韓愈，歐陽脩得蘇軾、蘇轍，至于今猶不朽。若令日萬一得聖賢之士，豈唯可以仰慰聖天子惓惓之情，而亦彰丞獬者有吐握之風焉？豈唯御史洎諸大夫有休，而人亦指〔表曰〕：「是無樹蔉藙者，可與也。」〔表之〕采縈囿楙矣。願爾多士加志
translation_en:
…in their arguments and hypothetical discussions, all praise Yao and Si—the sage rulers Shun and Yu—of high antiquity, and revere the masters of Lu and Zou, Confucius and Mencius, of later times. From Ziyou and Zixia onward, none seem to satisfy their aspirations. There is no doubt that they stand resolutely upon the path of the sages and worthies. Yet someday someone may hold the left half of a contract—as proof of a claim—and have grounds to say to you: “That statement about finding one or two out of ten was generous indeed.” Ah, this merits reflection!

In former times, Lu Zhi selected Han Yu, and Ouyang Xiu selected Su Shi and Su Zhe; their fame remains undying to this day. If today we should, by even the slightest chance, find men of sagely worth, would this not only console our sage Son of Heaven in his earnest concern, but also demonstrate that those described as ‘cheng xie’ [?] possess the spirit of one who spits out his food and grasps his unbound hair to welcome worthy men? Would this not only bring honor to the censor and the other officials, but also lead people to point them out 〔and declare〕: “These are men who do not plant ‘gun yi’ [?]; they deserve approval”? 〔Commend them〕 Their literary flourishing [?] is already abundant. May you, the many scholars, apply your resolve …

title: 嘉靖二十二年江西鄉試錄
text:
爲茲舉也若巡撫南贛僉都
御史虞〔守愚〕則宣謨揚休章
志貞教士習賴之若巡撫江
西僉都御史張〔岳〕雖新得代
而過化所遺彌彌嘉暢聞風
引領矣至於綜理要束則右
叅政王〔世爵〕左叅議岑〔萬〕副
===
使任〔轍〕僉事繆〔宗周〕李〔時達〕
襄翊周防則都指揮僉事方
〔恩〕時〔序〕若按察使陳〔嘉言〕以
初至左叅政何〔鼇〕右叅政趙
〔鏜〕僉事孫〔濟〕以祇役副使薛
〔甲〕楊〔本仁〕石〔遷高〕以兵政皆
雅志文致可稽也若以
punctuated: 爲茲舉也。若巡撫南贛僉都御史虞〔守愚〕，則宣謨揚休，章志貞教，士習賴之。若巡撫江西僉都御史張〔岳〕，雖新得代，而過化所遺，彌彌嘉暢，聞風引領矣。至於綜理要束，則右叅政王〔世爵〕、左叅議岑〔萬〕、副使任〔轍〕、僉事繆〔宗周〕、李〔時達〕；襄翊周防，則都指揮僉事方〔恩〕、時〔序〕。若按察使陳〔嘉言〕以初至，左叅政何〔鼇〕、右叅政趙〔鏜〕、僉事孫〔濟〕以祇役，副使薛〔甲〕、楊〔本仁〕、石〔遷高〕以兵政，皆雅志文致可稽也。若以
translation_en:
…in undertaking this examination. Yu Shouyu, Grand Coordinator of Nan-Gan and Assistant Censor-in-chief, promulgated plans and advanced good governance, made his aspirations manifest and rectified instruction; the scholarly community benefited from his efforts. Zhang Yue, Grand Coordinator of Jiangxi and Assistant Censor-in-chief, has recently been replaced, yet the transforming influence he left wherever he went continues to spread abundantly and beneficially. Hearing of his reputation, people crane their necks in admiration.

Overall management and the enforcement of essential regulations fell to Wang Shijue, Right Administration Vice Commissioner; Cen Wan, Left Administration Assistant Commissioner; Ren Zhe, Surveillance Vice Commissioner; and Miao Zongzhou and Li Shida, Surveillance Assistant Commissioners. Assistance and comprehensive security fell to Fang En and Shi Xu, Assistant Regional Military Commissioners.

title: 嘉靖二十二年江西鄉試錄
text:
朝命至樂觀盛舉者則戶部員
外郞何〔思〕魏〔一〕〔恭〕主事董〔德〕
〔明〕丘〔玳〕兵部主事韓〔桂〕若左
布政使俞〔夔〕按察使姚〔文〕〔炤〕
僉事楊〔伊〕〔志〕又皆緒正有勞
近雖代去法得備書云
直隸松江府儒學教授翟〔表〕
謹序
punctuated:
朝命至，樂觀盛舉者，則戶部員外郞何〔思〕、魏〔一〕〔恭〕，主事董〔德〕〔明〕、丘〔玳〕，兵部主事韓〔桂〕。若左布政使俞〔夔〕、按察使姚〔文〕〔炤〕、僉事楊〔伊〕〔志〕，又皆緒正有勞，近雖代去，法得備書云。
直隸松江府儒學教授翟〔表〕謹序。
translation_en:
…those who arrived on imperial orders and gladly witnessed this grand undertaking were He Si and Wei Yigong, Vice Directors in the Ministry of Revenue; Dong Deming and Qiu Dai, Secretaries in that ministry; and Han Gui, a Secretary in the Ministry of War. As for Yu Kui, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner; Yao Wenzhao, Provincial Surveillance Commissioner; and Yang Yizhi, Assistant Provincial Surveillance Commissioner, all likewise rendered meritorious service in organizing and setting matters in order [?]. Although they have recently been replaced and departed, established practice permits their names to be recorded here in full.
This preface is respectfully composed by Zhai Biao, Professor of the Prefectural Confucian School of Songjiang, in the directly administered metropolitan region.

Jiangxi Provincial Examination of the Twenty-second Year of Jiajing (1543)

Supervising Official
Li Sui, Investigating Censor assigned to巡按巡inspection of Jiangxi, had the courtesy name Liangbo and was a native of Jiangling County, Huguang. He became a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) in the jichou year.

Proctors
Chen Huan, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner of the Jiangxi Provincial Administration Commission, had the courtesy name Ziwen and was a native of Yuyao County, Zhejiang. He became a metropolitan graduate in the dingchou year.
Wang Chan, Left Assistant Administration Commissioner of the Jiangxi Provincial Administration Commission, had the courtesy name Zichang and was a native of Xiangshan County, Zhejiang. He became a metropolitan graduate in the renchen year.

Examination Monitoring Officials
Zou Shouyu, Vice Commissioner of the Jiangxi Provincial Surveillance Commission, had the courtesy name Junzhe and was a native of Putian County, Fujian. He became a metropolitan graduate in the bingxu year.

title: 嘉靖二十二年江西鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
子曰若聖與仁則吾豈敢抑爲之不厭誨
人不倦則可謂云爾已矣公西華曰正
唯弟子不能學也
胡杰
同考試官教諭葉　批〔平易不可及〕
同考試官教諭廖　批〔文理俱優〕
同考試官學正黃　批〔晚獨得此篇親切有味〕
===
考試官教授葉　批〔善形容〕
考試官教授翟　批〔明潔〕
聖人遜仁聖而因道其所能賢者深嘆其難也
夫聖人之心無息也無息則與天爲一矣是豈
易能者哉此公西華所以仰窺而歎也昔夫子
之謙詞若曰道出於天不可得而盡也學至於
道不可得而止也彼固有以聖與仁易言者何
哉蓋聖也者大而化之之謂也非造位天德者
不與焉而我非其人也仁也者德全道備之謂
punctuated:
第壹場
四書
子曰：「若聖與仁，則吾豈敢？抑爲之不厭，誨人不倦，則可謂云爾已矣。」公西華曰：「正唯弟子不能學也。」
胡杰
同考試官教諭葉批〔平易不可及〕
同考試官教諭廖批〔文理俱優〕
同考試官學正黃批〔晚獨得此篇親切有味〕
考試官教授葉批〔善形容〕
考試官教授翟批〔明潔〕
聖人遜仁聖，而因道其所能，賢者深嘆其難也。
夫聖人之心無息也，無息則與天爲一矣，是豈易能者哉？此公西華所以仰窺而歎也。昔夫子之謙詞若曰：「道出於天，不可得而盡也；學至於道，不可得而止也。彼固有以聖與仁易言者，何哉？蓋聖也者，大而化之之謂也，非造位天德者不與焉，而我非其人也。仁也者，德全道備之謂
translation_en:
First Session
Four Books

The Master said: “As for sagehood and benevolence, how would I dare claim them? Yet working at them without growing weary and teaching others without tiring—this much may be said of me, and nothing more.” Gongxi Hua said: “It is precisely this that we disciples cannot learn.”

Hu Jie

Associate Examiner Ye, Instructor, comments: “Plain and accessible, yet beyond others’ reach.”
Associate Examiner Liao, Instructor, comments: “Both composition and reasoning are excellent.”
Associate Examiner Huang, School Instructor, comments: “Late in the proceedings, I found this one piece alone intimate and richly suggestive.” [?]
Examiner Ye, Professor, comments: “Skillful in giving expression to the subject.”
Examiner Zhai, Professor, comments: “Clear and clean.”

The sage declined to claim benevolence and sagehood, and thereby spoke of what he could do; the worthy disciple deeply marveled at its difficulty.

The sage’s heart never ceases its activity. Never ceasing, it becomes one with Heaven. How could this be easy to achieve? This is why Gongxi Hua gazed upward, glimpsed it, and sighed in admiration. Formerly, the Master’s modest words were as if to say: “The Way issues from Heaven and cannot be exhausted; learning directed toward the Way cannot come to a halt. Why, then, are there those who speak lightly of sagehood and benevolence? Sagehood means being great and transforming others through that greatness. Only those who have attained the station of Heaven’s virtue partake of it, and I am not such a person. Benevolence means possessing virtue in its entirety and the Way in its completeness …

title: 嘉靖二十二年江西鄉試錄
text:
也非守心安仁者不與焉而我非其人也如其
曰居之而不疑則我豈敢乎抑爲之也發憤忘
食樂以忘憂而維日孜孜爲說諸心雖終身匪
懈也何有於厭乎及其誨人也博之以文約之
以禮而循循善誘苟可以語雖兩端必竭也何
有於倦乎力行而自信則固止於是而已耳此
則夫子之心也亦蓋深識之而歎曰爲可能也
不厭不可能也誨可能也不倦不可能也成身
成性以爲功有以見至誠無息之體焉立人達
===
人以爲心有以見萬物一體之用焉蓋與天之
不已者同運矣是豈弟子之所可致力而能乎
繇此以觀非亦之精久而有得不能悟也然則
亦其賢矣哉抑以古今所稱數大聖人者至堯
舜禹湯文武而止矣然其猶有兢兢業業祗台
日新緝熙而執競云者顧豈有所加益於數大
聖人者而然邪不厭不倦聖學之要其在是乎
夫子嘗曰聖人吾不得而見之矣又曰我未見
好仁者獨於顏氏之子則庶乎之稱三月不違
punctuated: 也，非守心安仁者不與焉，而我非其人也。如其曰居之而不疑，則我豈敢乎？抑爲之也，發憤忘食，樂以忘憂，而維日孜孜，爲說諸心，雖終身匪懈也，何有於厭乎？及其誨人也，博之以文，約之以禮，而循循善誘，苟可以語，雖兩端必竭也，何有於倦乎？力行而自信，則固止於是而已耳。此則夫子之心也。亦蓋深識之而歎曰：「爲可能也，不厭不可能也；誨可能也，不倦不可能也。成身成性以爲功，有以見至誠無息之體焉；立人達人以爲心，有以見萬物一體之用焉。蓋與天之不已者同運矣，是豈弟子之所可致力而能乎？」繇此以觀，非亦之精久而有得不能悟也，然則亦其賢矣哉！抑以古今所稱數大聖人者，至堯舜禹湯文武而止矣。然其猶有「兢兢業業」、「祗台日新」、「緝熙」而「執競」云者，顧豈有所加益於數大聖人者而然邪？不厭不倦，聖學之要，其在是乎！夫子嘗曰：「聖人，吾不得而見之矣。」又曰：「我未見好仁者。」獨於顏氏之子，則「庶乎」之稱、「三月不違
translation_en:
…Only those who preserve their minds and rest secure in benevolence can partake of it, and I am not such a person. If it means abiding in it without doubt, how could I dare claim that? Yet in pursuing it, I become so intent that I forget to eat, and so joyful that I forget my cares. I apply myself diligently each day, finding delight in my heart. Even if I remain unremitting throughout my life, how could I grow weary of it? As for teaching others, I broaden their learning through cultural study and restrain them through ritual, guiding them skillfully, step by step. Whenever someone can be instructed, I exhaust both ends of the matter for them. How could I tire of this? What I earnestly practice and confidently claim amounts to no more than this.”

Such was the Master's heart. Gongxi Hua, too, evidently understood it deeply and sighed: “To pursue it is possible; never to weary of it is beyond us. To teach is possible; never to tire of it is beyond us. Taking the perfection of one's person and nature as one's task reveals the substance of utmost sincerity, which never ceases. Setting one's heart on establishing others and enabling them to attain fulfillment reveals the operation of forming one body with the myriad things. This moves in concert with Heaven's ceaseless activity. How could we disciples achieve such ability merely by exerting ourselves?” From this we see that without refined and sustained effort yielding insight [?], he could not have understood this. Was he not, then, indeed worthy?

Now, the several great sages acclaimed from antiquity to the present extend only to Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu. Yet even of them there are such sayings as “cautious and vigilant,” “reverently, I renew myself daily,” “continuing in brightness,” and “holding firm in strength.” Could this have been because anything remained to be added to the achievements of these great sages? Never wearying and never tiring—is this not where the essential principle of sagely learning lies?

The Master once said: “A sage I have not been able to see.” He also said: “I have never seen anyone who loves benevolence.” Yet of the son of the Yan family alone, he offered the praise “nearly there,” and “for three months did not depart from…

title: 嘉靖二十二年江西鄉試錄
text:
之稱求見其止之稱不一而足也其在欲罷不
能之際乎是故善學夫子者莫如顏子
詩曰不顯惟德百辟其刑之是故君子篤
恭而天下平
李九韶
同考試官教諭祝　批〔下學極功止於篤恭最難〕
形容求其體認真切者僅見此篇
同考試官學正陳　批　造理之言
考試官教授葉　批　精密
考試官教授翟　批　文有思致
===
中庸引詩而著君子德化之極其盛焉蓋聖人
德盛而民化也夫何爲哉下學之極功至此而
無以加矣子思子推言君子爲己謹獨之功而
馴致其盛也蓋曰德必期於盡神而後可以語
化民勸民威不足以盡之也烈文之詩不云乎
不顯惟德百辟其刑之蓋言德之所存者神故
化之所及者遠也是詩也其達天德矣乎是故
君子動靜兼體上達乎性命之原內外合一自
punctuated:
之稱、求見其止之稱，不一而足也。其在欲罷不能之際乎？是故善學夫子者，莫如顏子。

《詩》曰：「不顯惟德，百辟其刑之。」是故君子篤恭而天下平。

李九韶

同考試官教諭祝　批：〔下學極功止於篤恭，最難〕形容，求其體認真切者，僅見此篇。
同考試官學正陳　批：造理之言。
考試官教授葉　批：精密。
考試官教授翟　批：文有思致。

《中庸》引《詩》而著君子德化之極，其盛焉。蓋聖人德盛而民化也，夫何爲哉？下學之極功至此而無以加矣。子思子推言君子爲己謹獨之功，而馴致其盛也。蓋曰：德必期於盡神，而後可以語化民；勸民，威不足以盡之也。《烈文》之詩不云乎：「不顯惟德，百辟其刑之。」蓋言德之所存者神，故化之所及者遠也。是詩也，其達天德矣乎！是故君子動靜兼體，上達乎性命之原；內外合一，自
translation_en:
…the commendation, and the commendation that he sought to see where the Master came to rest [?]—these are more than can be enumerated. Was it not precisely when he wished to stop but could not? Thus, among those who excelled in learning from the Master, none equaled Master Yan.

The Book of Odes says: “How illustrious is virtue! All the lords take it as their model.” Thus the gentleman is deeply reverent, and all under Heaven is at peace.

Li Jiushao

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhu, Instructor: 〔The utmost achievement of learning below culminates in profound reverence, which is most difficult〕 to describe. In seeking a genuinely perceptive and heartfelt understanding of this, I have found only this essay.
Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: Words that penetrate principle.
Comment by Examiner Ye, Professor: Refined and meticulous.
Comment by Examiner Zhai, Professor: The writing displays thoughtful insight.

The Doctrine of the Mean quotes the Book of Odes to reveal the culmination of the gentleman’s transforming influence through virtue—how flourishing it is! When the sage’s virtue flourishes, the people are transformed: what action need he take? The utmost achievement of learning below reaches this point, and nothing can be added to it. Master Zisi elaborates upon the gentleman’s efforts to cultivate himself and remain vigilant when alone, showing how these gradually reach their fullest development. His meaning is that virtue must attain the fullest spiritual efficacy before one can speak of transforming the people. In encouraging the people, awe-inspiring authority alone cannot accomplish everything. Does not the ode “Illustrious” (Lie wen) say: “How illustrious is virtue! All the lords take it as their model”? This means that what resides in virtue is spiritually efficacious, and therefore its transforming influence reaches far. Does not this ode comprehend the virtue of Heaven!

Thus the gentleman embodies both activity and stillness, attaining an understanding of the source of human nature and Heaven’s mandate; he unifies the inner and the outer, and of himself …

title: 嘉靖二十二年江西鄉試錄
text:
得乎中和之極緝熙敬止但見其穆穆焉已耳
退藏於密一天命之不已也齋莊中正但見其
安安焉已耳清明在躬一玄德之淵涵也君子
之積盛則然矣夫何與於天下也然而體信以
達順立於此而動於彼誠精而神應發乎邇而
見乎遠至禮不讓而上下之恭敬一焉合同而
化有莫得其所以神之者至德無爲而四方之
風俗同焉大道爲公有莫知其所以先之者故
曰篤恭而天下平此可以見聖神功化之極焉
===
可以見聖學始終之要焉學者當知所從事矣
雖然由下學而篤恭至矣盡矣然而又賛其妙
極於無聲無臭而後已焉夫豈高遠難行者哉
亦不過善事其心盡性而至命焉耳學者自謹
獨而求之則致中和以位育盡性以參天地脩
己以安百姓皆是道也程子曰有天德便可語
王道其要只在謹獨斯言得之矣
予天民之先覺者也予將以斯道覺斯民
也非予覺之而誰也
punctuated:
得乎中和之極。緝熙敬止，但見其穆穆焉已耳；退藏於密，一天命之不已也。齋莊中正，但見其安安焉已耳；清明在躬，一玄德之淵涵也。君子之積盛則然矣，夫何與於天下也？然而體信以達順，立於此而動於彼；誠精而神應，發乎邇而見乎遠。至禮不讓，而上下之恭敬一焉；合同而化，有莫得其所以神之者。至德無爲，而四方之風俗同焉；大道爲公，有莫知其所以先之者。故曰：「篤恭而天下平。」此可以見聖神功化之極焉，可以見聖學始終之要焉。學者當知所從事矣。雖然，由下學而篤恭，至矣，盡矣；然而又賛其妙，極於無聲無臭而後已焉。夫豈高遠難行者哉？亦不過善事其心，盡性而至命焉耳。學者自謹獨而求之，則致中和以位育，盡性以參天地，脩己以安百姓，皆是道也。程子曰：「有天德便可語王道，其要只在謹獨。」斯言得之矣。

予，天民之先覺者也；予將以斯道覺斯民也。非予覺之而誰也？
translation_en:
…and attains for himself the utmost equilibrium and harmony. Continuing in luminous virtue and abiding in reverence, he appears only solemn and dignified; withdrawing into hidden depths, he is one with the ceaseless operation of Heaven’s mandate. Reverent, grave, centered, and upright, he appears only perfectly at ease; with clarity and brightness embodied in him, he is one with the profound depths of mysterious virtue. Such is the fullness of the gentleman’s accumulated virtue. What involvement does he have in the world? Yet by embodying trustworthiness he brings about harmony: established here, he moves others there. His sincerity is refined, and a spiritual response follows: issuing nearby, its effects appear far away. Perfect ritual requires no yielding, yet reverence is shared alike by those above and below. Through union and concord, transformation takes place, though none can grasp what makes it so wondrous. Perfect virtue acts without contrivance, yet customs throughout the four quarters become alike. The Great Way serves the common good, though none can know how he takes the lead in this. Thus it is said: “Through profound reverence, the world is brought to peace.” Here one may see the utmost achievement of the sage’s wondrous transforming influence, and the essential thread running through the learning of the sages from beginning to end. Students should know where to direct their efforts.

Nevertheless, to proceed from elementary learning to profound reverence is the highest and fullest attainment. Yet the text goes on to praise its subtlety, stopping only when it reaches the point of being “without sound or scent.” Can this really be something lofty, remote, and difficult to practice? It amounts only to tending one’s heart well, fully realizing one’s nature, and thereby reaching Heaven’s mandate. If students seek it through vigilance over themselves when alone, then bringing equilibrium and harmony to their utmost so that Heaven and Earth take their proper places and all things are nurtured, fully realizing their nature so as to participate with Heaven and Earth, and cultivating themselves so as to bring peace to the common people—all belong to this Way. Master Cheng said: “With the virtue of Heaven, one may speak of the kingly Way. The essential point lies simply in vigilance over oneself when alone.” These words grasp it indeed.

“I am one of Heaven’s people who has awakened first; I shall use this Way to awaken these people. If I do not awaken them, who will?”

title: 嘉靖二十二年江西鄉試錄
text:
吳桂芳
同考試官教諭梁　批　伊尹此言當在幡然之後
同考試官教諭李　批　善言伊尹自任之意
同考試官教諭金　批　簡明可錄
考試官教授葉　批　純正
考試官教授翟　批　典則
此作得之
觀古人力任覺民之責其志可知已夫以道覺
民而自任之力伊尹之志大矣而辱已爲甚孟
===
子曉萬章意蓋曰吾謂伊尹無辱已之事嘗于
其言徵之矣其言曰使先知覺後知使先覺覺
後覺斯天意也而今安𭔃哉予固天民之先覺
者也夫道原于天無物我也是故粹乎其固有
者天民之所同也而覺存乎人有先後焉是故
超然而先覺者則予之所獨也予爲先覺則天
既屬意於我而民亦有厚望焉予其容已哉故
將因吾之已覺而覺其所未覺必使萬邦作乂
而後天意可塞也啓其所當然而及其所以然
punctuated:
吳桂芳

同考試官教諭梁，批：「伊尹此言當在幡然之後。」
同考試官教諭李，批：「善言伊尹自任之意。」
同考試官教諭金，批：「簡明可錄。」
考試官教授葉，批：「純正。」
考試官教授翟，批：「典則。」
此作得之。

觀古人力任覺民之責，其志可知已。夫以道覺民而自任之力，伊尹之志大矣，而辱已爲甚？孟子曉萬章，意蓋曰：「吾謂伊尹無辱已之事，嘗于其言徵之矣。其言曰：『使先知覺後知，使先覺覺後覺，斯天意也，而今安𭔃哉？予固天民之先覺者也。夫道原于天，無物我也，是故粹乎其固有者，天民之所同也；而覺存乎人，有先後焉，是故超然而先覺者，則予之所獨也。予爲先覺，則天既屬意於我，而民亦有厚望焉，予其容已哉？故將因吾之已覺，而覺其所未覺，必使萬邦作乂，而後天意可塞也；啓其所當然而及其所以然，
translation_en:
Wu Guifang

Associate Examiner Liang, Instructor, comments: “These words of Yi Yin must have been spoken after his decisive change of mind.”
Associate Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: “It expresses well Yi Yin’s intention in taking this responsibility upon himself.”
Associate Examiner Jin, Instructor, comments: “Concise and clear; worthy of inclusion.”
Examiner Ye, Professor, comments: “Pure and orthodox.”
Examiner Zhai, Professor, comments: “Classical and exemplary.”
This composition grasps the point.

By observing how firmly a man of antiquity assumed responsibility for awakening the people, we can understand his aspirations. Yi Yin’s aspirations were indeed great: he would awaken the people through the Way and resolutely took this task upon himself. Why, then, would he demean himself [?]? In enlightening Wan Zhang, Mencius meant, in substance:

“I say that Yi Yin never demeaned himself, and I have sought confirmation of this in his own words. He said: ‘That those who know first should awaken those who come to know later, and that those who awaken first should awaken those who awaken later—this is Heaven’s intention. And in whom does it now rest [?]? I am indeed one of Heaven’s people who has awakened first. The Way originates in Heaven and makes no distinction between others and oneself. Thus, the purity of what they inherently possess is shared by all Heaven’s people. Awakening, however, depends on the individual, and some awaken earlier, others later. Thus, to rise above others and awaken first is what distinguishes me alone. Since I have awakened first, Heaven has already entrusted its intention to me, and the people likewise have great expectations of me. How could I permit myself to stop? Therefore, I shall use what I have already apprehended to awaken them to what they have not yet apprehended. Only when I have brought all the states into good order can Heaven’s intention be fulfilled. I shall illuminate what they ought to do and extend this to the reasons why it is so…’”

title: 嘉靖二十二年江西鄉試錄
text:
必使大道爲公而後民望不孤也是非我之果
於自用而以無道必天下也蓋斯民也聞道有
先於吾則猶有可諉也而今未見其人矣開來
之任其昌當之邪斯民也聞道既後於吾吾終
不忍其昧也況其具又在我矣立教之責舍我
而誰邪此予所以不能不覺之也夫承天意以
從事者畏天命也立人極以覺民者悲人窮也
尹之志如此而謂有割烹要君之辱哉攷之咸
有一德與說命長發所稱則尹者雖百世師可
===
也孟子稱其所願學則曰姑舍是何歟夫作法
於偏其敝難稽也萬章此問姑以探孟子之不
仕本無足辯而孟子諄諄焉者其亦所以覺天
下也夫
易
象曰上天下澤履君子以辯上下定民志
同考試官教諭葉　批
辨上下定民志講者多用浮
詞此作獨得之渾化無迹可誦可誦
賀涇
punctuated:
必使大道爲公，而後民望不孤也。是非我之果於自用，而以無道必天下也。蓋斯民也，聞道有先於吾，則猶有可諉也，而今未見其人矣。開來之任，其昌當之邪？斯民也，聞道既後於吾，吾終不忍其昧也，況其具又在我矣。立教之責，舍我而誰邪？此予所以不能不覺之也。夫承天意以從事者，畏天命也；立人極以覺民者，悲人窮也。尹之志如此，而謂有割烹要君之辱哉？攷之《咸有一德》與《說命》《長發》所稱，則尹者，雖百世師可也。孟子稱其所願學，則曰「姑舍是」，何歟？夫作法於偏，其敝難稽也。萬章此問，姑以探孟子之不仕，本無足辯，而孟子諄諄焉者，其亦所以覺天下也夫！

易
象曰：「上天下澤，履。君子以辯上下，定民志。」

同考試官教諭葉，批：辨上下、定民志，講者多用浮詞。此作獨得之，渾化無迹，可誦，可誦！

賀涇
translation_en:
…I must ensure that the Great Way is shared by all; only then will the people’s hopes not be disappointed. This is not a matter of my being headstrong and self-willed, seeking to compel all under Heaven without the Way. If there were anyone among these people who had heard the Way before me, I might still entrust the task to him; yet I have seen no such person. Who, then, should undertake the responsibility of opening the way for those to come [?]? Since these people have heard the Way later than I, I cannot bear to leave them in ignorance, especially when the means of enlightening them lie with me. Who but I should shoulder the responsibility of establishing instruction? This is why I cannot but awaken them.

To act in accordance with Heaven’s intention is to stand in awe of Heaven’s mandate; to establish the supreme standard for humanity and awaken the people is to grieve over their distress. Such was the resolve of Yi Yin. How, then, could he be accused of the disgrace of seeking a ruler’s favor by butchering and cooking? Judging by what is said in “All Possess the One Virtue,” “The Charge to Yue,” and “Long Continuance,” Yi Yin could indeed serve as a teacher for a hundred generations. Why, then, when Mencius spoke of whom he wished to emulate, did he say, “Let us set this aside for now”? When a precedent is established on a partial basis, its harmful consequences are difficult to check. Wan Zhang’s question merely sought to probe why Mencius did not take office, and originally required no debate. Yet Mencius explained the matter so earnestly: was this not also his means of awakening all under Heaven?

Book of Changes
The Commentary on the Images says: “Heaven above and the marsh below: Treading. Thus the gentleman distinguishes those above from those below and settles the people’s aspirations.”

Associate Examiner Ye, Instructor, comments: “In explaining ‘distinguishes those above from those below and settles the people’s aspirations,’ commentators often resort to empty words. This essay alone grasps its meaning, integrating it so completely that no trace of artifice remains. Worth reciting, worth reciting!”

He Jing

易有自然之禮聖人因之以理天下也蓋禮者
理也聖人以禮爲治亦法其自然者爾觀此可
以知聖人制禮之原矣且禮何自而始乎其始
於天地也故觀禮於履乾上而兊下則是天澤
定位而大分昭焉初非有所強設也卑高以陳
===
而禮制行焉殆非可以僞爲也是禮者天地之
經緯也上下之紀也聖人則之以和邦國以馭
庶官以馴兆民于是名以命之器以别之使祿
位各比其德而等級不淆者所以防其僭也類
以聚之群以分之俾四民各一其業而品式弗
紊者所以防其亂也則禮達而分定分定而民

易有自然之禮，聖人因之以理天下也。蓋禮者，理也。聖人以禮爲治，亦法其自然者爾。觀此，可以知聖人制禮之原矣。且禮何自而始乎？其始於天地也。故觀禮於履，乾上而兊下，則是天澤定位，而大分昭焉，初非有所強設也。卑高以陳，而禮制行焉，殆非可以僞爲也。是禮者，天地之經緯也，上下之紀也。聖人則之，以和邦國，以馭庶官，以馴兆民。于是名以命之，器以别之，使祿位各比其德而等級不淆者，所以防其僭也；類以聚之，群以分之，俾四民各一其業而品式弗紊者，所以防其亂也。則禮達而分定，分定而民知守。百辟承式，靖共乃位，罔敢作慝以自犯於王章矣，其衆志之徂洽乎！四國信度，恪勤乃事，罔即淫佚以自蹈于匪彝矣，其民生之奠麗乎！

Associate Examiner Liao, Instructor, comments: 〔Thoroughly assimilates Cheng Yi’s commentary; both expression and reasoning are fully adequate.〕
Associate Examiner Huang, Instructor, comments: 〔Deeply grasps the source of the institution of ritual.〕
Examiner Ye, Professor, comments: 〔Concise yet comprehensive.〕
Examiner Zhai, Professor, comments: 〔Clear and clean.〕
The Book of Changes contains the rites inherent in the natural order; the sages follow these to bring order to the world. For ritual is principle. When the sages govern through ritual, they likewise take its natural order as their model, and nothing more. From this we can understand the source from which the sages instituted ritual. Where, then, does ritual originate? It originates in Heaven and Earth. Thus, when we examine ritual in the hexagram Treading (Lü), Qian is above and Dui below: Heaven and the lake occupy their fixed positions, and the great distinctions are manifest. These were never forcibly imposed. With the low and the high arrayed in order, ritual institutions come into operation; surely these cannot be fabricated artificially. Ritual is therefore the warp and weft of Heaven and Earth and the ordering framework of superior and inferior. The sages model themselves upon it to harmonize the states, direct the officials, and guide the myriad people into obedience.
Accordingly, they assign titles to designate people’s standing and ceremonial objects to distinguish them, ensuring that stipends and ranks correspond to each person’s virtue and that hierarchical grades remain distinct: this prevents usurpation of status. They gather people by kind and divide them into groups, ensuring that each of the four occupations devotes itself to its own work and that ranks and prescribed forms remain orderly: this prevents disorder. Thus ritual prevails and social distinctions become settled; once these are settled, the people know what they must observe. The assembled lords uphold the rules, peacefully and respectfully attending to their positions, and none dares commit wrongdoing and thereby violate the king’s statutes. How harmonious the purposes of the multitude become! Throughout the four quarters, people trust the standards and diligently attend to their tasks; none resorts to wanton indulgence and thereby falls into conduct contrary to established norms. How securely settled the people’s livelihoods become!

Thus we know that when the sages instituted ritual, they established it in accord with Heaven and Earth without contradiction and put it into practice throughout the world with few errors. Through it they regulated and assisted the processes of transformation and guided the people: could their achievement have been small? Moreover, the Master said: “To govern a state without ritual is like a blind man having no guide: bewildered, he does not know where to go.” The Three Dynasties belonged to different ages and did not simply inherit one another’s rites. This was because, although the principles of ritual cannot be changed, additions and reductions suited to the times concern only its articulations, forms, measures, and numbers. Hence it is said: “Those who understand the essential nature of rites and music can create them; those who recognize their forms can transmit them.”

“The Changes is that by which the sages plumb the depths and investigate the incipient workings of things. title: 嘉靖二十二年江西鄉試錄
text:
易之功其至矣乎且易何以爲聖人之道也彼
辭占之至精曰深然非自爲深也所以闡幽而
知來者聖人也否則其深者不可得而極也象
變之至變曰幾然非自爲幾也所以通變而極
數者聖人也否則其幾者不可得而研也此則
聖人之精藴因易以示者矣是知舍辭占而言
深不可也則夫明得失之報以定天下之疑者
皆深之所爲也舍象變而言幾不可也則夫盡
出入之利而成天下之亹亹者皆幾之所爲也
===
舍幾深而言神不可也則夫通志也若啓之成
務也若翼至皆神之所爲也夫豈待疾而速行
而至乎吁語易而至於神至矣盡矣而其原出
於聖人故曰易有聖人之道者此也雖然微聖
人則易不可得而見乎天地設位而易行乎其
中矣聖人所以成其能也其深其幾其神皆其
心之精藴也故舍聖人而天地未嘗無易也舍
天地而吾心未嘗無易也故曰神而明之存乎
其人
punctuated:
易之功，其至矣乎！且易何以爲聖人之道也？彼辭占之至精曰深，然非自爲深也。所以闡幽而知來者，聖人也；否則其深者不可得而極也。象變之至變曰幾，然非自爲幾也。所以通變而極數者，聖人也；否則其幾者不可得而研也。此則聖人之精藴因易以示者矣。是知舍辭占而言深，不可也；則夫明得失之報，以定天下之疑者，皆深之所爲也。舍象變而言幾，不可也；則夫盡出入之利，而成天下之亹亹者，皆幾之所爲也。舍幾深而言神，不可也；則夫通志也若啓之，成務也若翼至，皆神之所爲也。夫豈待疾而速，行而至乎？吁！語易而至於神，至矣，盡矣！而其原出於聖人，故曰易有聖人之道者，此也。
雖然，微聖人，則易不可得而見乎？天地設位，而易行乎其中矣。聖人所以成其能也，其深、其幾、其神，皆其心之精藴也。故舍聖人而天地未嘗無易也，舍天地而吾心未嘗無易也。故曰：「神而明之，存乎其人。」
translation_en:
…the achievement of making the Changes—how consummate it is! Moreover, why does the Changes embody the Way of the sages? The utmost refinement of its statements and divinations is called depth. Yet this depth does not manifest itself unaided. It is the sages who disclose what is hidden and know what is to come; otherwise, its depths could not be fully fathomed. The utmost subtlety of change in its images and transformations is called incipience. Yet this incipience does not manifest itself unaided. It is the sages who comprehend transformations and exhaust their numerical patterns; otherwise, these incipient workings could not be thoroughly investigated. These, then, are the sages’ essential insights, revealed through the Changes. Thus we know that one cannot speak of depth apart from its statements and divinations. Everything that makes clear the consequences of gain and loss, thereby settling the doubts of all under Heaven, is the work of depth. One cannot speak of incipience apart from its images and transformations. Everything that fully realizes the advantages of going forth and coming in, thereby bringing to fruition the tireless endeavors of all under Heaven, is the work of incipience. One cannot speak of numinous efficacy apart from incipience and depth. Making intentions understood, as though opening them up, and bringing affairs to completion, as though borne to their destination on wings [?]—these are all the work of numinous efficacy. How could it need haste to be swift, or movement to arrive? Ah! When discussion of the Changes reaches numinous efficacy, it has reached its utmost limit and is complete! Yet its source lies in the sages. This is what is meant by saying that the Changes contains the Way of the sages.
Nevertheless, without the sages, could the Changes not be perceived? Heaven and Earth take their appointed places, and change operates between them. The sages bring its capacities to fulfillment: its depth, its incipient workings, and its numinous efficacy are all essential insights within their minds. Thus, apart from the sages, Heaven and Earth have never been without change; apart from Heaven and Earth, my own mind has never been without change. Hence it is said: “To apprehend it numinously and make it clear depends upon the person.”

The sage ruler seeks a minister to oversee the whole of government; once he finds the right man, he entrusts him with undivided responsibility. How deeply Shun worried that he might fail to secure Yu! Once he secured Yu, the affairs of the hundred offices could accordingly be put in order. How skilled Shun was at entrusting men with office! We may imagine his address to the Four Mountains as follows: “In governing, nothing comes before deliberating on appointments; in deliberating on appointments, nothing matters more than choosing someone to oversee the whole of government. All the affairs of the realm today are the undertakings of Emperor Yao, and the one who coordinates them is the head of the hundred offices. Among you assembled ministers, can there be no one fit to be entrusted with exerting himself in service and advancing these undertakings? If there is, recommend him and have him take charge of the hundred offices. The many affairs differ, but he is to be held responsible for directing them all clearly. Thus, although the various categories of affairs are diverse, through him they may be brought smoothly to completion.” At this time, Bo Yu’s worthiness commanded the confidence of all …

text:
也故僉曰伯禹作司空是蓋以朝廷之有人而
不必他求耳帝即俞而咨禹曰汝平水土惟時
懋哉蓋言平成之休可稽於舊績而百揆之職
尚懋於新功此爲天下得人雖兼命而不嫌也
時則伯禹之心不自滿假者也故拜手稽首讓
于稷契曁皐陶將謂巳德之罔克而謙讓未遑
耳帝復俞而命之曰汝往哉蓋言四岳同辭則
公在天下而百揆是懋則簡在朕心此爲國家
任賢雖專命而不疑也於此有以見虞廷薦賢
===
之公焉有以見帝舜知人之哲焉茲有虞之治
後世弗可及也巳抑因是而知舜之心矣四岳
之咨諄諄於熈載之一言是豈以受堯之禪爲
可樂哉故必得禹而後堯之托爲不孤而舜之
憂始釋也是故堯得舜以遺天下而堯之仁大
矣舜得禹以遺天下而舜之仁大矣堯舜之用
心蓋如此故曰爲天下得人謂之仁
皇建其有極歛時五福用敷錫厥庶民惟
時厥庶民于汝極錫汝保極
punctuated:
也。故僉曰：「伯禹作司空。」是蓋以朝廷之有人，而不必他求耳。帝即俞而咨禹曰：「汝平水土，惟時懋哉！」蓋言平成之休，可稽於舊績；而百揆之職，尚懋於新功。此爲天下得人，雖兼命而不嫌也。時則伯禹之心不自滿假者也，故拜手稽首，讓于稷、契曁皐陶，將謂巳德之罔克，而謙讓未遑耳。帝復俞而命之曰：「汝往哉！」蓋言四岳同辭，則公在天下；而百揆是懋，則簡在朕心。此爲國家任賢，雖專命而不疑也。於此有以見虞廷薦賢之公焉，有以見帝舜知人之哲焉。茲有虞之治，後世弗可及也巳。抑因是而知舜之心矣。四岳之咨，諄諄於熈載之一言，是豈以受堯之禪爲可樂哉？故必得禹，而後堯之托爲不孤，而舜之憂始釋也。是故堯得舜以遺天下，而堯之仁大矣；舜得禹以遺天下，而舜之仁大矣。堯舜之用心蓋如此，故曰：「爲天下得人謂之仁。」

皇建其有極，歛時五福，用敷錫厥庶民。惟時厥庶民于汝極，錫汝保極。
translation_en:
…Thus they all said, “Bo Yu serves as Minister of Works.” They meant that the court already possessed the right man, and there was no need to seek elsewhere. The emperor assented and addressed Yu: “You have brought order to the waters and the land; now exert yourself in this!” He meant that the excellence of Yu’s achievement in restoring order could be verified from his past accomplishments, while in the office of Chief Minister he should strive for new achievements. This was finding the right man for All under Heaven: even an appointment combining offices gave no cause for misgiving. At that time, Bo Yu’s heart was free of self-satisfaction and conceit. Thus he bowed with clasped hands and touched his forehead to the ground, yielding the appointment to Ji, Xie, and Gao Yao. He meant that his own virtue was inadequate to the task, and could scarcely finish his humble demurrals. The emperor again assented and commanded him: “Go!” He meant that the Four Mountains’ unanimous recommendation expressed the impartial judgment of All under Heaven, while his own heart had selected Yu to apply himself to the duties of Chief Minister. This was employing a worthy man for the state: even an exclusive appointment gave no cause for doubt.

Here we can see the impartiality with which the court of Yu recommended worthy men, and Emperor Shun’s wisdom in discerning men’s abilities. Such was the government of Yu that later ages could not equal it. Moreover, from this we can understand Shun’s heart. In consulting the Four Mountains, he dwelt earnestly on the single phrase “bringing achievement to flourishing completion.” Could he have regarded receiving Yao’s abdication as something merely to enjoy? Only after he secured Yu would Yao’s trust remain unbetrayed and Shun’s anxiety begin to lift. Thus Yao secured Shun to leave to All under Heaven, and great was Yao’s benevolence; Shun secured Yu to leave to All under Heaven, and great was Shun’s benevolence. Such were the intentions of Yao and Shun. Hence the saying: “Finding the right man for All under Heaven is called benevolence.”

The sovereign establishes his supreme standard, gathers these five blessings, and thereby distributes them widely among his common people. Then these common people conform to your standard, enabling you to preserve that standard.

君子於皇極之建，而必著其君民相與之盛焉。夫極一也，君錫於上，民保於下，極其可以不建乎？箕子告武王若曰：「朝廷爲四方之極，君身實萬化之原。疇之次五，固曰建用皇極矣。何言乎極之建也？必其立本以盡性，而顯諸動靜者足以端表正之體；經綸以盡倫，而章諸軌物者足以正大觀之儀，則極建矣。吾見精神洞達，而天心純佑，自申錫于無疆；和氣流暢，而諸福畢至，自昭受于有永。極之所建，其福之所集乎？然君之斂福，非徒厚其身也，蓋將公溥於民，以各足其分，同綏乎元吉之祉；敷施於下，以各遂其欲，共囿於容保之休。極之所不違者，亦福之所不遺也。是非錫福也乎？所謂君之與民，蓋如此。夫
translation_en:
Zhu Yingyuan

Associate Examiner Zhu, an Instructor, comments: “The interpretation of the interaction between ruler and people is sound.”
Associate Examiner Chen, a School Instructor, comments: “Careful in both phrasing and conception.”
Examiner Ye, a Professor, comments: “Pure and clean.”
Examiner Cheng, a Professor, comments: “Full-bodied and substantial.”

In discussing the establishment of the sovereign’s ultimate standard, the gentleman invariably brings out the flourishing interaction between ruler and people. The standard is one: the ruler above bestows blessings, and the people below uphold the standard. How could it fail to be established? Jizi’s instruction to King Wu may be expressed as follows: “The court is the standard for the four quarters, and the ruler’s own person is truly the source of all transformation. The fifth of the divisions indeed says, ‘Establish and employ the sovereign’s ultimate standard.’ What does establishing this standard mean? The ruler must establish the foundation so as fully to realize his nature, and what he manifests in movement and stillness must suffice to set right his embodiment of exemplary rectitude. He must order affairs so as fully to fulfill human relationships, and what he displays in rules and norms must suffice to set right the bearing that all look up to. Then the standard is established. I see his spiritual vitality penetrating everywhere, while Heaven’s heart grants unalloyed assistance, repeatedly bestowing blessings without limit; harmonious vital energy flows freely, and all blessings arrive together, manifestly received for all time. Is not the place where the standard is established also where blessings gather?

“Yet the ruler’s gathering of blessings is not merely to enrich himself. He intends to extend them impartially and universally to the people, so that each receives a sufficient share and all rest together in the blessing of supreme good fortune; to distribute them among those below, so that each fulfills his desires and all dwell within the beneficence of his encompassing protection. Those whom the standard does not pass over are likewise those whom blessings do not leave out. Is this not the bestowal of blessings? Such, then, is what is meant by the ruler’s part in his interaction with the people. Now, …

title: 嘉靖二十二年江西鄉試錄
text:
民之被福若無與於君也吾知不識不知懋昭
乎帝則之順惟恐自越於典常是訓是行相安
於大道之公無敢自外於彝憲福之所衣被者
極之所無斁也是非保極也乎所謂民之與君
又如此夫以君民相與之盛信乎其爲皇極之
在此極之所以當建也嗟乎此心極也存之則
爲天德發之則爲王道此即堯舜執中之傳而
萬世之言道統皆宗焉九疇之綱雖皆治天下
之大經大法而其樞要統會不外乎人主之一
心不然則藩飾無本前乎四疇不能以立後乎
四疇不能以行烏足以言極邪是故欲建極者
其始於心乎
===
詩
四牡脩廣其大有顒薄伐玁狁以奏膚公
有嚴有翼共武之服共武之服以定王
國
吴桂芳
同考試官教諭梁　批　奮揚戒懼之意讀之尚可想
punctuated:
民之被福，若無與於君也。吾知不識不知，懋昭乎帝則之順，惟恐自越於典常；是訓是行，相安於大道之公，無敢自外於彝憲。福之所衣被者，極之所無斁也。是非保極也乎？所謂民之與君，又如此夫！以君民相與之盛，信乎其爲皇極之在此，極之所以當建也。嗟乎！此心，極也。存之則爲天德，發之則爲王道。此即堯舜執中之傳，而萬世之言道統皆宗焉。九疇之綱，雖皆治天下之大經大法，而其樞要統會，不外乎人主之一心。不然，則藩飾無本，前乎四疇不能以立，後乎四疇不能以行，烏足以言極邪？是故欲建極者，其始於心乎！

詩
四牡脩廣，其大有顒。薄伐玁狁，以奏膚公。有嚴有翼，共武之服。共武之服，以定王國。

吴桂芳

同考試官教諭梁，批：奮揚戒懼之意，讀之尚可想
translation_en:
…The people receive blessings as though they had nothing to do with their ruler. Yet I know that, without conscious knowledge or awareness, they earnestly manifest their obedience to the Supreme Lord’s standard, fearing only that they might transgress the constant norms. Following this instruction and putting it into practice, they dwell together peacefully within the impartiality of the Great Way, none daring to place themselves outside the enduring statutes. Wherever blessings extend their shelter, adherence to the Supreme Standard never flags. Is this not preserving the Standard? Such, then, is what is meant by the people’s relationship with their ruler! In this flourishing mutual relationship between ruler and people, truly the August Ultimate resides: this is why the Standard must be established.

Ah! This mind is the Standard. Preserved within, it constitutes heavenly virtue; expressed in action, it constitutes the Kingly Way. This is precisely the tradition of holding fast to the Mean transmitted by Yao and Shun, which all discussions of the succession of the Way through the ages take as their source. Although the guiding principles of the Nine Categories are all great norms and laws for governing the realm, their pivotal point and unifying center lie nowhere beyond the ruler’s own mind. Otherwise, there would be only outward embellishment without a foundation [?]: the four preceding categories could not be established, and the four following categories could not be put into practice. How could this suffice to speak of the Standard? Thus, whoever wishes to establish the Standard should surely begin with the mind!

Book of Odes

“The four stallions are tall and broad;
Their great stature is imposing.
They march against the Xianyun,
To accomplish a mighty achievement.
Stern and vigilant,
They attend to their martial duties.
They attend to their martial duties,
To bring stability to the royal domain.”

Wu Guifang

Comment by Associate Examiner Liang, Instructor: “The spirit of rousing resolve and vigilant apprehension can still be imagined as one reads…”

title: 嘉靖二十二年江西鄉試錄

見

試人美大將之北伐必著其成攘外安內之績
焉夫攘外所以安內也觀其軍容之盛師律之
臧其斯爲節制之兵乎六月盖美尹吉甫北伐
有功而作也若曰聖人無外王師有征我吉甫
===
受分閫之寄蒞敵愾之兵其取勝也必矣何也
兵以威揚於外而其用之以取勝莫利於馬以
今日言之四牡則脩廣矣上駟之選也其大則
有顒矣長驅之材也以之薄伐玁狁宣忠効力
大振長勝之威執訊獲醜茂樹廓清之績而寇
攘以過也疆圉以靖也膚功之所成固有獻之
王庭者矣所謂先人有奪人之心者此也兵以
謀定於內而其制之以全勝又莫先於嚴且敬
也以今日言之操威克之權而紀律嚴明謹愓
punctuated:
見。
同考試官教諭李批：〔有斟　酌〕
同考試官教諭金批：〔詞意　兼勝〕
考試官教授葉批：〔氣壯〕

試人美大將之北伐，必著其成攘外安內之績焉。夫攘外所以安內也。觀其軍容之盛、師律之臧，其斯爲節制之兵乎？《六月》盖美尹吉甫北伐有功而作也。若曰：聖人無外，王師有征。我吉甫受分閫之寄，蒞敵愾之兵，其取勝也必矣。何也？兵以威揚於外，而其用之以取勝，莫利於馬。以今日言之，四牡則脩廣矣，上駟之選也；其大則有顒矣，長驅之材也。以之薄伐玁狁，宣忠効力，大振長勝之威；執訊獲醜，茂樹廓清之績。而寇攘以過也，疆圉以靖也。膚功之所成，固有獻之王庭者矣。所謂先人有奪人之心者，此也。兵以謀定於內，而其制之以全勝，又莫先於嚴且敬也。以今日言之，操威克之權，而紀律嚴明，謹愓

…be envisioned.
Associate Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: “Shows careful consideration.”
Associate Examiner Jin, Instructor, comments: “Both expression and meaning excel.”
Examiner Ye, Professor, comments: “Vigorous in spirit.”
Examiner Zhai, Professor, comments: “Elegant and robust.”
When the poet [?] praises the great general’s northern expedition, he must make manifest his achievement in repelling external enemies and securing peace within. For repelling external enemies is the means of securing peace within. Observe the magnificence of his army’s array and the excellence of its discipline: surely these are troops under orderly command! “The Sixth Month” was presumably composed to praise Yin Jifu’s successful northern expedition. It is as though the poem says: “For the sage, none lie outside his domain; the king’s army undertakes punitive expeditions. Our Jifu has been entrusted with an independent military command and leads troops fired with indignation against the enemy. His victory is assured. Why is this?
“An army displays its might abroad, and in employing it to achieve victory, nothing is more useful than horses. Speaking of the present occasion, the four stallions are tall and broad—the choicest of superior steeds. Their great size is imposing—they have the mettle for a far-ranging advance. With them he attacks the Xianyun, displaying loyalty and exerting his strength, greatly enhancing the awe inspired by enduring victory. He takes prisoners for interrogation and captures the enemy host, splendidly accomplishing the clearing of the realm. The raiders are driven away [?], and the frontiers are pacified. Such great achievements surely provide something to present at the royal court. This is what is meant by taking the initiative and thereby breaking the enemy’s resolve.
“An army establishes its plans within; in controlling it to secure complete victory, nothing takes precedence over strictness and reverent vigilance. Speaking of the present occasion, he wields the authority that prevails through awe, and military discipline is strict and clear; carefully heeding…”

title: 嘉靖二十二年江西鄉試錄
text:
號之戒而夙夜祗懼以之共武之事吾見折衝
之謀不出於樽俎屏翰之業坐運於帷幄而中
外以定也宗社以安也威靈之所著固有恃以
無恐者矣所謂先爲不可勝以待敵之可勝者
此也如是則華夏之氣紓荒服之制明而宵旰
之憂可釋矣以文武之吉甫雖以六月之師無
悔也雖然王者不治之道其惟夷狄乎六月之
師已非司馬之法周亦不可謂不亟矣然其所
謂薄伐者僅太原而止耳其王者之兵乎易曰
師貞丈人吉尹吉甫之謂矣君子是以知周宣
之善任將也
===
約軝錯衡八鸞鶬鶬以假以享我受命溥
將自天降康豐年穰穰來假來饗降福
無疆
熊汝達
同考試官教諭梁　批〔末徽以天命人心意良是〕
同考試官教諭李　批〔歸功先祜意是如此〕
同考試官教諭金　批〔詞不費而意自足〕
punctuated:
號之戒，而夙夜祗懼，以之共武之事。吾見折衝之謀不出於樽俎，屏翰之業坐運於帷幄，而中外以定也，宗社以安也。威靈之所著，固有恃以無恐者矣。所謂先爲不可勝，以待敵之可勝者，此也。如是，則華夏之氣紓，荒服之制明，而宵旰之憂可釋矣。以文武之吉甫，雖以六月之師，無悔也。雖然，王者不治之道，其惟夷狄乎？六月之師，已非司馬之法，周亦不可謂不亟矣。然其所謂薄伐者，僅太原而止耳，其王者之兵乎？《易》曰：「師貞，丈人吉。」尹吉甫之謂矣。君子是以知周宣之善任將也。

約軝錯衡，八鸞鶬鶬。以假以享，我受命溥將。自天降康，豐年穰穰。來假來饗，降福無疆。

熊汝達

同考試官教諭梁，批〔末徽以天命人心意良是〕。
同考試官教諭李，批〔歸功先祜意是如此〕。
同考試官教諭金，批〔詞不費而意自足〕。
translation_en:
…the admonition concerning cries of alarm, remaining reverently fearful morning and night, and thus attending to military affairs. I see plans for repelling the enemy devised without leaving the sacrificial vessels and banquet tables, and the work of shielding the state accomplished while seated within the command tent. Thus affairs within and beyond the realm are settled, and the ancestral temples and altars of state are secure. Wherever this awe-inspiring power manifests itself, there is indeed something to rely upon without fear. This is what is meant by first making oneself invincible and then awaiting the enemy’s vulnerability. In this way, the strain upon the Chinese heartland is relieved, the regulation of the remote domains is made clear, and the ruler may lay aside the anxieties that keep him at work before dawn and until late in the day. With Jifu’s civil and military talents, even a campaign in the sixth month gives no cause for regret. Nevertheless, is it not precisely toward the Yi and Di peoples that a true king follows the principle of refraining from direct governance? A campaign in the sixth month already departed from the rules of the Minister of War; Zhou, too, cannot be said to have been free of haste. Yet what the poem calls its punitive expedition went only as far as Taiyuan and stopped. Was this not the army of a true king? The Book of Changes says: “In conducting an army, correctness is required; for a mature leader, good fortune.” This describes Yin Jifu. From this, the gentleman knows how well King Xuan of Zhou appointed his generals.

“The wheel hubs are bound, the carriage crossbars ornamented; the eight bells ring out harmoniously. We come forward and present offerings; the mandate we have received is vast and great. From Heaven descends peace; abundant harvests fill the years. Come, draw near and partake; send down blessings without limit.”

Xiong Ruda.

Associate Examiner Liang, Instructor, comments: 〔The concluding appeal [?] to Heaven’s mandate and the people’s hearts is excellent in conception.〕
Associate Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: 〔The idea of attributing the achievement to ancestral blessings is as it should be.〕
Associate Examiner Jin, Instructor, comments: 〔The wording is economical, yet the meaning is fully expressed.〕

title: 嘉靖二十二年江西鄉試錄
text:
考試官教授葉　批　簡當
考試官教授翟　批　典實
商人奉祭必歸之天〻之助而獲福之隆也夫
惟孝子為能饗親也商人本人心天命以祀其
先若不專於備物者可以觀孝矣此亦祀成湯
之樂也若曰王者之所以保大業而假有廟者
亦惟於天命人心焉見之矣我商今日之祭豈
唯載清酤進和羹而已耶是故四方諸侯各以
其職來祭也但見其同執而至約軝錯衡其制
===
備也八鸞鶬鶬其聲和也冠裳集而玉帛攸同
其所以駿奔而對越之者不有以得萬國之懽
心乎且我之受命於天也寵綏保定既已廣且
大矣而天又申命用休迄用康年昭仁愛也黍
稷穰穰溥休徵也明馨備而百禮以洽其得以
享祀而孚侑之者不有以受上帝之明賜乎由
是假之而來假享之而來饗思成之綏也而元
吉集焉凡其思或啓之行或翼之罄無不宜而
人心之聯屬蓋有衍之為悠久之休者矣著存
punctuated:
考試官教授葉批：簡當。
考試官教授翟批：典實。

商人奉祭，必歸之天，〻之助而獲福之隆也。夫惟孝子為能饗親也。商人本人心天命以祀其先，若不專於備物者，可以觀孝矣。此亦祀成湯之樂也。若曰：王者之所以保大業而假有廟者，亦惟於天命人心焉見之矣。我商今日之祭，豈唯載清酤、進和羹而已耶？是故四方諸侯各以其職來祭也，但見其同執而至，約軝錯衡，其制備也；八鸞鶬鶬，其聲和也。冠裳集而玉帛攸同，其所以駿奔而對越之者，不有以得萬國之懽心乎？且我之受命於天也，寵綏保定，既已廣且大矣。而天又申命用休，迄用康年，昭仁愛也；黍稷穰穰，溥休徵也。明馨備而百禮以洽，其得以享祀而孚侑之者，不有以受上帝之明賜乎？由是假之而來假，享之而來饗，思成之綏也，而元吉集焉。凡其思或啓之，行或翼之，罄無不宜，而人心之聯屬，蓋有衍之為悠久之休者矣。著存
translation_en:
Examiner Ye, Professor, comments: “Concise and apt.”
Examiner Zhai, Professor, comments: “Grounded in the classics and substantial.”

When the people of Shang offered sacrifices, they invariably attributed the outcome to Heaven: it was through Heaven’s assistance that they obtained such abundant blessings. Only a filial son can truly offer sacrifice to his parents. The people of Shang grounded their sacrifices to their ancestors in human hearts and Heaven’s Mandate. They seemingly did not concern themselves exclusively with preparing material offerings; herein their filial devotion can be seen. This, too, is music for sacrificing to Cheng Tang.

It is as though the song says: The means by which a king preserves his great enterprise and comes into the ancestral temple are to be found solely in Heaven’s Mandate and human hearts. Can the sacrifice that we of Shang offer today consist merely of setting out clear wine and presenting seasoned broth? Thus the regional lords from the four quarters come to sacrifice, each fulfilling his duties. We see them arriving together, bearing their offerings [?]. Their chariot hubs are bound and their crossbars ornamented: their equipment is complete. Their eight bells ring harmoniously: their sound is concordant. Those wearing ceremonial caps and robes assemble, and jade and silk are brought together. That they hasten so eagerly to attend and offer reverence—is this not because the king has won the joyful allegiance of the myriad states?

Moreover, in receiving Heaven’s Mandate, we have already enjoyed favor, reassurance, protection, and stability of great breadth and magnitude. Yet Heaven further renews its command with blessings, bringing us a year of well-being and thereby manifesting its benevolence and love. The millet harvests are abundant, spreading auspicious signs everywhere. The pure, fragrant offerings are prepared, and the hundred rites are performed in harmony. That we can offer these sacrifices and sincerely urge the spirits to partake—is this not because we have received the manifest gifts of the Lord on High?

Thus, when we approach them, they come to us; when we offer to them, they come to partake. Through concentrated remembrance they are brought to rest, and supreme good fortune gathers. In every thought there is something to enlighten them, and in every action something to assist them; everything is fitting without exception. The bonds uniting human hearts thus unfold into blessings enduring far into the future. The ancestors’ manifest presence…

title: 嘉靖二十二年江西鄉試錄
text:
之感也而純嘏錫焉凡夫諸福之物可致之祥
莫不畢至而天心之眷顧蓋有延之爲無疆之
慶者矣是知幽明相感而其幾微天人合一故
其應妙要之皆先福之所及也爲後王者其尚
繹思之哉抑商人尚聲而烈祖之頌乃拳拳焉
歸之天命人心者何哉蓋七世之廟可以觀德
即天命人心之所以去留則先德所當法而先
澤不足恃胥見之矣使後之子孫能作求世德
則商至今存可也彼謂祭無益謂敬不足行者
===
不知其於天命人心何如哉於乎詩人歌頌之
意微矣
春秋
秋齊侯宋公江人黃人會于陽穀〔僖公三年〕
況淑祺

同考試官教諭陳　批〔古人用兵之法此亦可見〕
考試官教授葉　批〔發揮善謀處甚得精神故錄〕
punctuated:
之感也，而純嘏錫焉。凡夫諸福之物、可致之祥，莫不畢至，而天心之眷顧，蓋有延之爲無疆之慶者矣。是知幽明相感，而其幾微；天人合一，故其應妙。要之，皆先福之所及也。爲後王者，其尚繹思之哉！抑商人尚聲，而《烈祖》之頌乃拳拳焉歸之天命人心者，何哉？蓋七世之廟可以觀德，即天命人心之所以去留，則先德所當法，而先澤不足恃，胥見之矣。使後之子孫能作求世德，則商至今存可也。彼謂祭無益、謂敬不足行者，不知其於天命人心何如哉？於乎！詩人歌頌之意微矣！

春秋

秋，齊侯、宋公、江人、黃人會于陽穀。〔僖公三年〕

況淑祺
