translation_en:
…the feeling of their presence, and abundant blessings are bestowed. Every blessing and every auspicious sign that can be brought about arrives in full; Heaven’s favor thus extends into boundless felicity. From this we know that the unseen and visible realms affect one another through subtle workings; Heaven and humanity are united, and thus their responses are wondrous. In essence, all this lies within the reach of ancestral blessings. Should not later kings ponder it deeply? Yet the people of Shang esteemed sound: why, then, does the hymn Illustrious Ancestor so earnestly attribute these things to Heaven’s mandate and the people’s hearts? The temples of seven generations allow one to observe virtue. In the very reasons why Heaven’s mandate and the people’s hearts depart or remain, one sees both that ancestral virtue must be emulated and that ancestral beneficence cannot be relied upon. Had later descendants been able to pursue the virtue transmitted through the generations, Shang could have survived to the present day. As for those who say that sacrifice brings no benefit and that reverence is not worth practicing, how do they suppose they stand with Heaven’s mandate and the people’s hearts? Ah! Subtle indeed is the intent of the poet’s praise!

Spring and Autumn Annals

“In autumn, the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, and men of Jiang and Huang met at Yanggu.” 〔Third year of Duke Xi.〕

Kuang Shuqi

Associate Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: 〔Duke Huan’s subjugation of Chu hinged on this undertaking. This composition grasps that point.〕

Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: 〔Here too one can see the ancients’ methods of employing military force.〕

Examiner Ye, Professor, comments: 〔Its exposition of skillful planning captures the essential spirit particularly well; for this reason it has been selected for inclusion.〕

title: 嘉靖二十二年江西鄉試錄
text:
考試官教授翟　批　律而藏
伯者以謀制外而春秋予焉夫好謀所以成事
也矧欲制外哉觀春秋之末言予陽穀見矣昔
自敗莘以後楚成代興窺周而僭王矣侵鄭而
猾夏矣使爲𢀪者不能舉義何以正天下之防
此師之不可已也不知用謀何以成天下之事
此會之不可已也迺遐講陽穀之好而近自宋公
遠及江黃無弗與者君子以爲是舉也非欲厚
疑以長亂也非徒崇侈以飾觀也攘夷之畧定
===
於是安夏之功始於是其命八國也欲其聚而
戰也兵之正也所以擣其腹心而使之進無所
逞也故雖懸師入境而我無虞焉其命江黃也
欲其分而守也兵之奇也所以翦其羽翼而使
之退無所據也故雖堅壁不動而氣已奪焉萬
全之舉也夫然後齊知必勝楚知必負陘方次
矣完遂盟矣雖曰服之以義而亦其好謀之成
有以先事制之也雖曰來之以禮而亦其多筭
之勝有以先聲奪之也故春秋紀是會也於大
punctuated:
考試官教授翟批：律而藏。

伯者以謀制外，而春秋予焉。夫好謀所以成事也，矧欲制外哉？觀春秋之末言，予陽穀見矣。昔自敗莘以後，楚成代興，窺周而僭王矣，侵鄭而猾夏矣。使爲𢀪者不能舉義，何以正天下之防？此師之不可已也。不知用謀，何以成天下之事？此會之不可已也。迺遐講陽穀之好，而近自宋公，遠及江黃，無弗與者。君子以爲是舉也，非欲厚疑以長亂也，非徒崇侈以飾觀也。攘夷之畧定於是，安夏之功始於是。其命八國也，欲其聚而戰也，兵之正也，所以擣其腹心，而使之進無所逞也。故雖懸師入境，而我無虞焉。其命江黃也，欲其分而守也，兵之奇也，所以翦其羽翼，而使之退無所據也。故雖堅壁不動，而氣已奪焉。萬全之舉也。夫然後齊知必勝，楚知必負。陘方次矣，完遂盟矣。雖曰服之以義，而亦其好謀之成，有以先事制之也；雖曰來之以禮，而亦其多筭之勝，有以先聲奪之也。故春秋紀是會也，於大
translation_en:
Examiner Zhai, Professor, comments: “Disciplined and restrained.”

The hegemon used strategic planning to control external powers, and the Spring and Autumn Annals commends him for it. A fondness for planning is what brings undertakings to fruition; how much more necessary is it when one seeks to control external powers! Looking at the concluding words of the Spring and Autumn Annals [?], we can see its approval of the meeting at Yanggu. After the defeat at Shen, King Cheng of Chu rose in succession, casting covetous eyes upon Zhou and usurping the royal title, invading Zheng and troubling the Chinese states. If the hegemon [?] could not uphold righteousness, how could he set right the boundaries separating the realm from outsiders? This was why a military expedition could not be dispensed with. Without knowing how to employ strategy, how could he accomplish the affairs of the realm? This was why the meeting could not be dispensed with. Thus he extended the bonds of amity at Yanggu far and wide: from the Duke of Song nearby to Jiang and Huang farther away, none failed to participate. The gentleman judges that this undertaking was neither intended to deepen suspicion and foster disorder nor merely to magnify extravagance and make a splendid display. Here the strategy for repelling the outsiders was settled; here the work of securing the Chinese states began.

His orders to the eight states called for them to concentrate their forces and fight. This was the regular use of troops: to strike at the enemy’s heart and prevent it from making headway in an advance. Thus, even when our army penetrated deep into enemy territory, we had no cause for anxiety. His orders to Jiang and Huang called for them to divide their forces and hold their positions. This was the unconventional use of troops: to clip the enemy’s wings and deprive it of any support in retreat. Thus, even while the enemy remained motionless behind strong fortifications, its fighting spirit had already been broken. It was an undertaking that ensured complete success.

Only then did Qi know that victory was certain, and Chu that defeat was certain. The army had scarcely encamped at Xing when Wan concluded the covenant. Although it may be said that Chu was brought to submission through righteousness, this was also the achievement of a fondness for planning, which enabled Qi to bring Chu under control before events unfolded. Although it may be said that Chu was induced to come through ritual propriety, this was also the victory secured by ample calculation, which enabled Qi to overawe Chu through its advance reputation. Thus, when the Spring and Autumn Annals records this meeting, with regard to the great …

title: 嘉靖二十二年江西鄉試錄
text:
國書齊宋焉言大則小者舉之矣於遠人書江
黃焉言遠則近者舉之矣所以善桓謀也由此
觀之衆不可失也強亦不可恃也慮勝而動好
謀而成君子有不戰戰必勝矣雖然是亦衰世
之意也舞干而格因壘而降豈必謀哉然則春
秋非不貴舜也桓不舜也非不貴文也桓不文
也不然何始會陽穀則善而再會陽穀則荒也
哉是故陽穀一會而桓之伯業與之終始由其
無德以將之也故曰仲尼之門無道桓文之事
===
者
遂伐楚　楚屈完來盟于師〔僖公四年〕
會于蕭魚〔襄公十有一年〕　夏楚子蔡侯
陳侯鄭伯許男徐子滕子頓子胡子沈
子小邾子宋世子佐淮夷會于申〔昭公〕
四年
計士元
同考試官教諭劉　批〔發楚鄭所以見服處最明白〕
同考試官教諭陳　批〔春秋善桓悼之意正如此〕
punctuated:
國書齊、宋焉，言大則小者舉之矣；於遠人書江、黃焉，言遠則近者舉之矣。所以善桓謀也。由此觀之，衆不可失也，強亦不可恃也。慮勝而動，好謀而成，君子有不戰，戰必勝矣。雖然，是亦衰世之意也。舞干而格，因壘而降，豈必謀哉？然則《春秋》非不貴舜也，桓不舜也；非不貴文也，桓不文也。不然，何始會陽穀則善，而再會陽穀則荒也哉？是故陽穀一會，而桓之伯業與之終始，由其無德以將之也。故曰：「仲尼之門無道桓文之事者。」
遂伐楚。楚屈完來盟于師。〔僖公四年〕
會于蕭魚。〔襄公十有一年〕
夏，楚子、蔡侯、陳侯、鄭伯、許男、徐子、滕子、頓子、胡子、沈子、小邾子、宋世子佐、淮夷會于申。〔昭公〕四年。
計士元
同考試官教諭劉，批〔發楚鄭所以見服處最明白〕
同考試官教諭陳，批〔春秋善桓悼之意正如此〕
translation_en:
…among the great states, it records Qi and Song: by naming the great, it includes the small. Among the distant peoples, it records Jiang and Huang: by naming the distant, it includes those nearby. This is how it commends Duke Huan’s planning. Viewed in this light, one must not lose the support of the multitude, nor may one rely on strength alone. Act after considering how to secure victory; delight in planning and bring the undertaking to completion. The gentleman may refrain from battle, but if he fights, he will surely win. Nevertheless, this too reflects the outlook of an age of decline. Shun danced with shield in hand and brought others into submission; King Wen used existing siege works and obtained surrender. What need had they of scheming? Thus, it is not that the Spring and Autumn Annals fails to esteem Shun, but that Huan was no Shun; not that it fails to esteem King Wen, but that Huan was no King Wen. Otherwise, why does it commend the first meeting at Yanggu but regard the second as dissolute? Thus the meeting at Yanggu marked both the beginning and the end of Huan’s achievement as hegemon, because he lacked the virtue to guide it. Hence the saying: “Among the disciples of Zhongni, none spoke of the affairs of Dukes Huan and Wen.”
“They then attacked Chu. Qu Wan of Chu came to conclude a covenant with the army.” 〔Fourth year of Duke Xi.〕
“They met at Xiaoyu.” 〔Eleventh year of Duke Xiang.〕
“In summer, the Viscount of Chu, the Marquis of Cai, the Marquis of Chen, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, the Viscount of Xu, the Viscount of Teng, the Viscount of Dun, the Viscount of Hu, the Viscount of Shen, the Viscount of Little Zhu, Zuo, heir apparent of Song, and the Huai Yi met at Shen.” 〔Duke Zhao.〕 Fourth year.
Ji Shiyuan.
Associate Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: 〔“The explanation of how Chu and Zheng were brought into submission is exceptionally clear.”〕
Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: 〔“This is precisely the Spring and Autumn Annals’ intention in commending Dukes Huan and Dao.”〕

title: 嘉靖二十二年江西鄉試錄
text:
考試官教授葉　批　謹嚴
考試官教授翟　批　得旨
春秋于創伯而取其服外之義于繼伯而取其
服貳之誠此見桓得于制楚悼得于撫鄭要皆
春秋所予也且自黍離降而王迹熄首伯以庄
天下者齊桓也維時荆楚暴横為吾中國慮久
矣桓憂之而討以義焉包茅問其不貢而威讓
有令王祭徵其不供而文告有詞卒之召陵退
舍盟禮定而楚勢屈惟共惟順有師徒不勤而
===
邊鄙寧謐者矣使惟戎兵是詰則方城漢水之
險未見其易屈也而奚致屈完肯來耶以全取
勝桓其庶幾矣經故特紀來盟于師蓋美其近
王事也至於黄鳥賦而伯業頹繼是以安天下
者晋悼也維時鄭人携貳為吾侯度擾多矣悼
知之而感以誠焉禮囚禁侵本諸由衷之懇遣
使播告示以樂與之公卒之蕭魚至止會好成
而鄭志恊無反無側有牲歃不事而懷疑聿定
者矣使徒約劑是煩則犧牲玉帛之待未見其
punctuated:
考試官教授葉批：謹嚴。
考試官教授翟批：得旨。
春秋于創伯而取其服外之義，于繼伯而取其服貳之誠。此見桓得于制楚，悼得于撫鄭，要皆春秋所予也。且自黍離降而王迹熄，首伯以庄天下者，齊桓也。維時荆楚暴横，為吾中國慮久矣。桓憂之而討以義焉。包茅問其不貢，而威讓有令；王祭徵其不供，而文告有詞。卒之召陵退舍，盟禮定而楚勢屈，惟共惟順，有師徒不勤而邊鄙寧謐者矣。使惟戎兵是詰，則方城漢水之險，未見其易屈也，而奚致屈完肯來耶？以全取勝，桓其庶幾矣。經故特紀來盟于師，蓋美其近王事也。至於黄鳥賦而伯業頹，繼是以安天下者，晋悼也。維時鄭人携貳，為吾侯度擾多矣。悼知之而感以誠焉。禮囚禁侵，本諸由衷之懇；遣使播告，示以樂與之公。卒之蕭魚至止，會好成而鄭志恊，無反無側，有牲歃不事而懷疑聿定者矣。使徒約劑是煩，則犧牲玉帛之待，未見其
translation_en:
Examiner Ye, an Education Professor, comments: “Careful and rigorous.”
Examiner Zhai, an Education Professor, comments: “Grasps the purport.”
In treating the founding of the hegemony, the Spring and Autumn Annals approves the righteousness by which outsiders were brought to submission; in treating its continuation, it approves the sincerity by which those of divided allegiance were won over. This shows that Duke Huan succeeded in restraining Chu, and Duke Dao in conciliating Zheng: in essence, both received the approval of the Spring and Autumn Annals.
After “Millet Drooping” (Shu li) was relegated to the lower rank and the traces of kingly rule disappeared, the first hegemon to bring order to [?] All Under Heaven was Duke Huan of Qi. At that time, the violence and arrogance of Jing-Chu had long been a source of anxiety to our central states. Troubled by this, Duke Huan undertook a punitive expedition in the name of righteousness. He questioned Chu’s failure to present bundled thatch as tribute, issuing an authoritative rebuke; he called it to account for failing to supply the royal sacrifices, setting forth his grounds in a formal proclamation. Finally, at Shaoling, he withdrew his encampment; the covenant ritual was settled, and Chu’s power yielded. Chu became respectful and obedient, and the borderlands were tranquil without exhausting the army. Had he merely pressed matters by force of arms, the defenses of Fangcheng and the Han River would hardly have been easily overcome. How, then, could he have induced Qu Wan to come willingly? Duke Huan came close indeed to achieving victory while preserving all intact. Thus the Classic specifically records that Qu Wan “came to make a covenant with the army,” praising Duke Huan for approaching the deeds of a true king.
By the time “Yellow Birds” (Huang niao) was recited and the hegemonic enterprise had declined, it was Duke Dao of Jin who succeeded in bringing peace to All Under Heaven. At that time, the people of Zheng wavered in their allegiance, repeatedly disturbing the order governing our regional lords. Duke Dao understood this and moved them through sincerity. His courteous treatment of prisoners and prohibition of incursions sprang from heartfelt earnestness; by dispatching envoys to proclaim his intentions, he demonstrated his impartial willingness to associate with them. Finally, upon reaching Xiaoyu, friendly relations were established at the meeting and Zheng’s intentions were brought into accord. There was neither defection nor deviation: doubts were resolved without resorting to sacrificial victims and blood-swearing. Had he merely troubled them with repeated agreements, then, for all the provision of sacrificial animals, jade, and silk, it is not apparent that he could have …

title: 嘉靖二十二年江西鄉試錄
text:
易格也而奚至會申方叛耶至誠動物悼其近
之矣經故特紀蕭魚之會蓋喜其紹伯事也是
則桓以攘夷而夏安悼以安夏而夷服王不足
而伯固經世者所賴云二君何以得此哉內政
之作和戎之利勞心勞力之說國有人焉其功
不容泯者雖然陽穀會而寵樂荒通吳懷陳而
智不逮果君之懈於盈成乎抑臣之格心未聞
乎是故君子貴王而賤伯
禮記
===
禮行於祖廟而孝慈服焉
董良佐
考試官教授葉　批〔文字縝密有思致非苟作者〕
考試官教授程　批〔說得親切有味〕
〔必爲佳士〕
聖王舉祀先之典斯民德歸厚矣夫祖廟以本
仁通之人心者也聖王祀乎其先則德厚矣民
焉有不覲化者哉且先王患禮教之不達於下
也乃行乎郊社而各有其效矣自其行于祖廟
punctuated:
易格也，而奚至會申方叛耶？至誠動物，悼其近之矣。經故特紀蕭魚之會，蓋喜其紹伯事也。是則桓以攘夷而夏安，悼以安夏而夷服，王不足而伯固經世者所賴云。二君何以得此哉？內政之作，和戎之利，勞心勞力之說，國有人焉，其功不容泯者。雖然，陽穀會而寵樂荒，通吳懷陳而智不逮，果君之懈於盈成乎？抑臣之格心未聞乎？是故君子貴王而賤伯。

禮記

禮行於祖廟而孝慈服焉。

董良佐

考試官教授葉　批〔文字縝密有思致，非苟作者。〕

考試官教授程　批〔說得親切有味。〕〔必爲佳士。〕

聖王舉祀先之典，斯民德歸厚矣。夫祖廟以本仁，通之人心者也。聖王祀乎其先，則德厚矣，民焉有不覲化者哉？且先王患禮教之不達於下也，乃行乎郊社，而各有其效矣。自其行于祖廟
translation_en:
…easy to win over; how, then, could renewed meetings have coincided with further rebellion [?]? In moving others through perfect sincerity, Duke Dao came close to the ideal. The Classic therefore specially records the meeting at Xiaoyu, expressing approval that he carried on the work of the hegemons. Thus Duke Huan repelled the non-Chinese peoples and secured the Chinese states; Duke Dao secured the Chinese states and brought the non-Chinese peoples into submission. Though falling short of true kingship, hegemony was certainly something on which those who ordered the world relied. How did these two rulers achieve this? The institution of domestic government, the benefits of peace with the Rong, and the counsel concerning those who labor with their minds and those who labor with their strength—all owed something to capable men in their states, whose contributions must not be effaced. Nevertheless, at the meeting at Yanggu, indulgence in favorites and pleasures led to excess; in establishing relations with Wu and seeking to win over Chen, wisdom proved inadequate. Was it truly that the rulers grew negligent amid their established successes? Or was it that their ministers failed to rectify their rulers’ hearts? This is why the gentleman esteems kingship and holds hegemony in low regard.

Book of Rites

“When ritual is performed in the ancestral temple, filial devotion and parental kindness are practiced.”

Dong Liangzuo

Examiner Ye, Professor, comments: 〔The writing is closely reasoned and thoughtful; it is not the work of someone writing carelessly.〕

Examiner Cheng, Professor, comments: 〔The exposition is apt and full of flavor.〕〔He is surely an outstanding scholar.〕

When the sage king performs the rites of sacrifice to his ancestors, the virtue of the people returns to sincerity and generosity. The ancestral temple is the means of rooting humaneness and extending it into people’s hearts. When the sage king sacrifices to his ancestors, his virtue is deep and generous. How could the people fail to witness this and be transformed? Moreover, the former kings worried that instruction through ritual might not reach those below. They therefore performed rites at the suburban altar and the altar of soil, each producing its own effect. As for their performance of rites in the ancestral temple…

title: 嘉靖二十二年江西鄉試錄
text:
者而教亦豈不在焉蓋先王志厚義章必立爲
祖考之廟而饗之如祭之以時奉之以物力不
敢以不竭道之以禮安之以樂情不敢以不愼
宣祝嘏以諭志意而神人胥悅者豈惟粢盛之
潔備臣工以駿奔走而幽明交通者庶或明德
之馨禮行於祖廟如此聖王豈要其得四海之
懽哉蓋端本肇風化之原存神妙應物之感故
凡有父者效而法之仁考于焉以興孰不以安
以養而老其老耶凡有子者則而象之慈愛于
===
焉以起孰不以燕以翼而幼其幼耶人無異尚
而名分各定家無殊習而禮俗已刑禮教何患
有不達哉吁衆之服自此則祭誠爲政教之本
非義之脩而禮之藏乎大抵聖王之治天下順
而已矣豈畀之以所無哉亦不過因心之同有
者先以開其機耳先之而外乎吾仁非感也感
之而不開其機徒感也是以堯舜帥天下以仁
而民從之後世謂祭爲無益者良可慨歟此易
曰聖王以神道設教而天下服語曰知其說者
punctuated: 者，而教亦豈不在焉？蓋先王志厚義章，必立爲祖考之廟而饗之。如祭之以時，奉之以物，力不敢以不竭；道之以禮，安之以樂，情不敢以不愼。宣祝嘏以諭志意，而神人胥悅者，豈惟粢盛之潔？備臣工以駿奔走，而幽明交通者，庶或明德之馨。禮行於祖廟如此，聖王豈要其得四海之懽哉？蓋端本肇風化之原，存神妙應物之感。故凡有父者，效而法之，仁考于焉以興，孰不以安以養而老其老耶？凡有子者，則而象之，慈愛于焉以起，孰不以燕以翼而幼其幼耶？人無異尚，而名分各定；家無殊習，而禮俗已刑。禮教何患有不達哉？吁！衆之服自此，則祭誠爲政教之本，非義之脩而禮之藏乎？大抵聖王之治天下，順而已矣，豈畀之以所無哉？亦不過因心之同有者，先以開其機耳。先之而外乎吾仁，非感也；感之而不開其機，徒感也。是以堯舜帥天下以仁，而民從之。後世謂祭爲無益者，良可慨歟！此《易》曰：「聖王以神道設教，而天下服。」《語》曰：「知其說者，
translation_en:
…and could instruction fail to be present in what they enacted in the ancestral temple? The former kings were profound in their intentions and manifest in their righteousness; they therefore necessarily established temples for their forebears and offered sacrifices to them. In sacrificing at the proper seasons and presenting material offerings, they dared not withhold any effort. In guiding them through ritual and bringing them repose through music, they dared not be careless in their feelings. Prayers and blessings were proclaimed to convey their intentions, bringing joy to spirits and men alike: could this have depended solely on the purity of the sacrificial grain? The assembled officers hastened about their duties, and communication passed between the unseen and visible realms: perhaps it was the fragrance of luminous virtue that brought this about. With rites thus performed in the ancestral temple, could the sage kings have been seeking to win the delight of all within the Four Seas? Rather, they rectified the root and opened the source of moral transformation, preserving the numinous efficacy that subtly responds to things and moves people.
Thus all who had fathers followed their example, and benevolence and filial devotion [?] arose among them. Who would not give comfort and sustenance to their own elders, treating them as elders should be treated? All who had children took them as their model, and loving kindness arose among them. Who would not give ease and protection to their own young, treating them as the young should be treated? People upheld the same values, and each person's status and obligations were settled; households shared the same practices, and ritual customs took shape. Why fear that ritual instruction might fail to reach everyone?
Ah! The multitude's submission arose from this. Sacrifice is therefore truly the foundation of government and instruction. Is it not the cultivation of righteousness and the repository of ritual? In governing the world, the sage kings did no more than follow what was already there. How could they bestow upon people something they did not possess? They merely drew upon what all hearts shared, taking the lead in awakening its motivating impulse. To lead others while remaining outside one's own benevolence is not to move them; to move them without awakening that impulse is merely to stir their feelings. Thus Yao and Shun led the world through benevolence, and the people followed them. That later generations should call sacrifice useless is truly lamentable! This is what the Book of Changes says: “The sage kings established instruction through the way of the spirits, and all under Heaven submitted.” The Analects says: “One who understood its meaning…”

title: 嘉靖二十二年江西鄉試錄
text:
之於天下也其如視諸斯乎
樂由中出故靜禮自外作故文大樂必易
大禮必簡
鍾崇武
考試官教授葉　批〔發盡禮樂之妙〕
考試官教授程　批〔斂華就實録之〕
記者原禮樂有本之妙必賛其所以妙也盖禮
樂與天地相爲流通者也原於身心固靜而文
矣然非以易簡賛之抑何以知其然哉樂記君
===
子論禮樂之道其始也不外乎身心其極也可
同乎天地彼聲容兼備人知爲樂矣孰知是樂
之作也本吾心欣喜歡愛之和由中而出者乎
盖君子樂得其道故性術發於聲音而一真凝
定英華形於舞蹈而天理流行雖動實安也何
其靜耶經曲兼全人知爲禮矣孰知是禮之作
也本吾身進退周旋之序自外而作者乎盖君
子酌之以義故威儀著於交錯而斐然成章品
節極其詳明而燦然可觀雖嚴實華也何其文
punctuated:
之於天下也，其如視諸斯乎？

樂由中出，故靜；禮自外作，故文。大樂必易，大禮必簡。

鍾崇武

考試官教授葉，批〔發盡禮樂之妙〕。
考試官教授程，批〔斂華就實，録之〕。

記者原禮樂有本之妙，必賛其所以妙也。盖禮樂與天地相爲流通者也，原於身心，固靜而文矣。然非以易簡賛之，抑何以知其然哉？《樂記》：君子論禮樂之道，其始也不外乎身心，其極也可同乎天地。彼聲容兼備，人知爲樂矣，孰知是樂之作也，本吾心欣喜歡愛之和，由中而出者乎？盖君子樂得其道，故性術發於聲音，而一真凝定；英華形於舞蹈，而天理流行。雖動實安也，何其靜耶！經曲兼全，人知爲禮矣，孰知是禮之作也，本吾身進退周旋之序，自外而作者乎？盖君子酌之以義，故威儀著於交錯，而斐然成章；品節極其詳明，而燦然可觀。雖嚴實華也，何其文
translation_en:
…in relation to all under Heaven, would it not be like looking at this here before him?

“Music issues from within and therefore is still; ritual takes form from without and therefore is patterned. Great music must be easy; great ritual must be simple.”

Zhong Chongwu

Examiner Ye, an Instructor, comments: 〔Fully brings out the subtle workings of ritual and music.〕
Examiner Cheng, an Instructor, comments: 〔Restrains ornament and attends to substance; select it.〕

The compiler of the Record traces the subtle workings of ritual and music to their foundations and must commend what makes those workings so subtle. For ritual and music circulate in mutual communion with Heaven and Earth. Rooted in body and mind, they are indeed still and patterned. Yet unless we commend them in terms of ease and simplicity, how can we understand why this is so? In the Record of Music, the gentleman discusses the Way of ritual and music: at its beginning, it does not extend beyond body and mind; at its culmination, it can accord with Heaven and Earth.

When sound and bodily expression are both fully present, people recognize music. But who understands that the making of this music is founded upon the harmony of joy, delight, affection, and love in our hearts, issuing from within? Because the gentleman finds joy in attaining the Way, the workings of his nature emerge in sound, while his undivided genuineness remains settled and firm; their flowering takes form in dance, while Heaven’s principle flows through it. Though moving, he is truly at peace: how still it is!

When general principles and particular observances are both complete, people recognize ritual. But who understands that the making of this ritual is founded upon the ordered advancing, withdrawing, turning, and moving of our bodies, taking form from without? Because the gentleman weighs these things according to rightness, dignified deportment manifests itself in his dealings with others and forms a beautiful pattern; its gradations and restraints attain the utmost precision and clarity, presenting a brilliant spectacle. Though solemn, it is truly splendid: how patterned…

title: 嘉靖二十二年江西鄉試錄
text:
耶惟其靜焉則與天地同和可以宣一代之盛
不爲樂之大乎大非以其器也一至和之發揚
而無事於矯飾殆猶乾元之資始健以運之易
知而不勞也樂之道豈不易哉惟其文焉則與
天地同序可以嘉天下之會不爲禮之大乎大
非以其度也一至順之顯設而無事於紛擾殆
猶坤元之資生順以承之簡能而不煩也禮之
理豈不簡哉吁禮樂而至於易簡則天下之理
得矣聖人所以無爲而治者其此之謂歟抑考
===
禮樂未作聖人之妙藏於天地禮樂既作天地
之妙寓於聖人聖人天地合而一者也及感於
人心又豈有二理哉故曰樂至則無怨禮至則
不爭雖然必明於天地而後可舉有志於復古
禮變今樂者宜鑒於斯
第貳塲
論
王者如天
胡直
punctuated:
耶？惟其靜焉，則與天地同和，可以宣一代之盛，不爲樂之大乎？大非以其器也，一至和之發揚，而無事於矯飾，殆猶乾元之資始，健以運之，易知而不勞也。樂之道豈不易哉？惟其文焉，則與天地同序，可以嘉天下之會，不爲禮之大乎？大非以其度也，一至順之顯設，而無事於紛擾，殆猶坤元之資生，順以承之，簡能而不煩也。禮之理豈不簡哉？吁！禮樂而至於易簡，則天下之理得矣。聖人所以無爲而治者，其此之謂歟？抑考禮樂未作，聖人之妙藏於天地；禮樂既作，天地之妙寓於聖人。聖人、天地合而一者也，及感於人心，又豈有二理哉？故曰：「樂至則無怨，禮至則不爭。」雖然，必明於天地而後可舉。有志於復古禮、變今樂者，宜鑒於斯。
第貳塲
論
王者如天
胡直
translation_en:
…is it not? Precisely through its stillness, music shares the harmony of Heaven and Earth and can proclaim the flourishing of an age. Is this not the greatness of music? Its greatness does not lie in its instruments: it is wholly the expression of consummate harmony, with no need for contrived embellishment. It resembles the primal power of Qian, from which all things take their beginning: moving them through vigor, it governs through ease, without toil. Is not the Way of music easy? Precisely through its patterned form, ritual shares the order of Heaven and Earth and can lend beauty to the gatherings of all under Heaven. Is this not the greatness of ritual? Its greatness does not lie in its regulations: it is wholly the manifest establishment of consummate compliance, with no need for distracting complexity. It resembles the primal power of Kun, from which all things receive life: supporting them through compliance, it accomplishes through simplicity, without complication. Is not the principle of ritual simple? Ah! When ritual and music attain ease and simplicity, the principles of all under Heaven are grasped. Is this not what is meant by the sages’ governing through nonaction?
Consider further: before ritual and music were created, the subtle workings of the sages lay hidden within Heaven and Earth; once ritual and music were created, the subtle workings of Heaven and Earth resided in the sages. The sages and Heaven and Earth unite as one. When they move human hearts, how could there be two different principles? Thus it is said: “Where music reaches perfection, there is no resentment; where ritual reaches perfection, there is no contention.” Even so, only after understanding Heaven and Earth can one put these into practice. Those intent on restoring ancient ritual and transforming the music of the present should take this as their guide.
Second Session
Discourse
“The True King Is Like Heaven”
Hu Zhi

title: 嘉靖二十二年江西鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭梁　批〔是作意趣深遠詞語老成一氣呵成不煩繩削佳作也〕
同考試官教諭李　批〔是王者氣象〕
同考試官教諭金　批〔高古之作〕
考試官教授葉　批〔議論甚精〕
考試官教授翟　批〔純正〕
聖人之道天道也天覆萬物而不有是故天下
之物取足於天之化而忘乎其爲天也聖人生
萬民法天而不私而其道與天並是故天下之
===
視聖人者猶天之運於上也而安有恩戚於其
間耶故曰聖人之道天道也今夫天陽之舒也
有生殖之德焉仁之所以出也陰之慘也有震
曜之威焉義之所以出也主宰而不居運行而
不息渾淪廣博而不知其始不測其終天亦何
嘗有心於物而爲之者耶而天下之物生成於
大化之中咸以其分而取足焉天之功於是乎
不可測矣聖人之作也總攝羣動而宰制萬有
懼天下之紛紛焉以起相率而求於我莫之止
punctuated:
同考試官教諭梁　批〔是作意趣深遠，詞語老成，一氣呵成，不煩繩削，佳作也。〕
同考試官教諭李　批〔是王者氣象。〕
同考試官教諭金　批〔高古之作。〕
考試官教授葉　批〔議論甚精。〕
考試官教授翟　批〔純正。〕
聖人之道，天道也。天覆萬物而不有，是故天下之物取足於天之化，而忘乎其爲天也。聖人生萬民，法天而不私，而其道與天並。是故天下之視聖人者，猶天之運於上也，而安有恩戚於其間耶？故曰：聖人之道，天道也。
今夫天，陽之舒也，有生殖之德焉，仁之所以出也；陰之慘也，有震曜之威焉，義之所以出也。主宰而不居，運行而不息，渾淪廣博而不知其始，不測其終。天亦何嘗有心於物而爲之者耶？而天下之物生成於大化之中，咸以其分而取足焉。天之功於是乎不可測矣。
聖人之作也，總攝羣動而宰制萬有，懼天下之紛紛焉以起，相率而求於我，莫之止
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Liang, an Instructor, comments: 〔This composition has profound and far-reaching meaning, and its language is mature. Written in one sustained flow, it needs no further correction or trimming. An excellent composition.〕
Associate Examiner Li, an Instructor, comments: 〔This conveys the bearing of a true king.〕
Associate Examiner Jin, an Instructor, comments: 〔A work of lofty, antique character.〕
Examiner Ye, a Professor, comments: 〔The argument is very refined.〕
Examiner Zhai, a Professor, comments: 〔Pure and orthodox.〕
The Way of the sage is the Way of Heaven. Heaven shelters the myriad things without possessing them. Thus all things under Heaven find their needs satisfied through Heaven’s transforming activity and forget that it is Heaven that does this. The sage nurtures the myriad people, modeling himself on Heaven without partiality, and his Way stands alongside Heaven’s. Thus the world regards the sage as it does Heaven moving above: how could personal favor or kinship have any place therein? Hence it is said: the Way of the sage is the Way of Heaven.
Consider Heaven: when yang unfolds, it possesses the virtue of bringing forth and nurturing life; this is the source of benevolence. When yin is harsh, it possesses a terrifying, dazzling majesty; this is the source of righteousness. Heaven presides without claiming the position of master and moves without ceasing. An undivided whole, vast and all-embracing, its beginning cannot be known and its end cannot be fathomed. When has Heaven ever acted upon things with deliberate intent? Yet all things under Heaven are born and brought to maturity within its great transformation, each finding sufficient provision according to its allotted portion. Heaven’s achievement is therefore unfathomable.
When the sage arises, he encompasses all activity and governs all that exists. He fears that the world will rise in turmoil, people following one another in making demands upon him, with no one to halt them…

title: 嘉靖二十二年江西鄉試錄
text:
過迺或役其心之臆决操天下而束縛之馳驟
之欲天下之不吾梗吾知其必不能矣聖人者
憲天以爲聰明舉天下而盡出於天聖人不與
焉而卒收其功者聖人也是故其爲喜也天之
所以生殖也陽之舒也其爲怒也天之所以震
曜也陰之慘也嗟乎是亦天而已矣何也五典
之惇也聖人行之然而不出於我焉則以爲天
叙也五禮之庸也聖人行之然而不出於我焉
則以爲天秩也德之命也罪之討也聖人行之
===
然而不出於我焉則以爲天命也天討也至於
百物之利聖人導之以布上下者也然而不出
於我焉則亦不過因天之時順地之利而已矣
天以其仁生天下之人而付之聖人而聖人以
天之道神天下之化以任其責於天裁成輔相
率本於天之所爲固非有所歡忻震懼於天下
亦不以天下之所取必者而一旦破裂其法以
求中其所欲是故其政惻怛而不狥優游而不
驟幷包廣覆而不遺卒而天下之治無以易之
punctuated: 過，迺或役其心之臆决，操天下而束縛之、馳驟之，欲天下之不吾梗，吾知其必不能矣。聖人者，憲天以爲聰明，舉天下而盡出於天，聖人不與焉，而卒收其功者，聖人也。是故其爲喜也，天之所以生殖也，陽之舒也；其爲怒也，天之所以震曜也，陰之慘也。嗟乎！是亦天而已矣。何也？五典之惇也，聖人行之，然而不出於我焉，則以爲天叙也；五禮之庸也，聖人行之，然而不出於我焉，則以爲天秩也；德之命也，罪之討也，聖人行之，然而不出於我焉，則以爲天命也、天討也。至於百物之利，聖人導之以布上下者也，然而不出於我焉，則亦不過因天之時、順地之利而已矣。天以其仁生天下之人而付之聖人，而聖人以天之道神天下之化，以任其責於天。裁成輔相，率本於天之所爲，固非有所歡忻震懼於天下，亦不以天下之所取必者而一旦破裂其法，以求中其所欲。是故其政惻怛而不狥，優游而不驟，幷包廣覆而不遺，卒而天下之治無以易之
translation_en:
…excesses [?]. If, instead, one gives free rein to the arbitrary judgments of one’s own mind, takes hold of all under Heaven, and binds and drives them, hoping that no one will oppose oneself, I know this must prove impossible. The sage models his discernment on Heaven: everything throughout the world proceeds from Heaven, and the sage does not interpose himself. Yet it is the sage who ultimately reaps the achievement. Thus his joy is Heaven’s means of engendering and nourishing life, the unfolding of yang; his anger is Heaven’s means of inspiring awe, the severity of yin. Ah! This too is simply Heaven. Why is this so? The sage puts into practice the strengthening of the five cardinal relationships; yet this does not originate in himself, and so he regards it as Heaven’s ordering. The sage puts into practice the observance of the five rites; yet this does not originate in himself, and so he regards it as Heaven’s ranking. The sage appoints the virtuous and punishes the guilty; yet these acts do not originate in himself, and so he regards them as Heaven’s appointments and Heaven’s punishments. As for the benefits afforded by the myriad things, the sage directs their distribution among those above and below; yet this does not originate in himself either. It amounts merely to following Heaven’s seasons and according with the advantages of the earth.

Heaven, through its benevolence, gives life to the people of the world and entrusts them to the sage. Through Heaven’s Way, the sage brings about wondrous transformation throughout the world, thereby discharging his responsibility to Heaven. In shaping things to completion and assisting their development, he invariably takes Heaven’s workings as his basis. Certainly, he does not act out of delight in, or fear of, the world; nor does he, because of what people insist upon, suddenly tear apart his established rules to satisfy their desires. Thus his government is compassionate without yielding to improper demands, unhurried without precipitous action, and all-embracing and far-reaching without leaving anyone out. In the end, the order achieved throughout the world admits of no improvement upon it …

title: 嘉靖二十二年江西鄉試錄
text:
者天也故天下之人老有所終幼有所養鰥寡
孤獨得其所安君臣不得不義父子不得不親
兄弟不得不順男女不得不別比閭族黨不得
不睦善積而必彰惡積而必癉天下之人自易
其惡自至其中而舉不姦於其道不姦於其治
天之所覆地之所載莫不揚休利用各得其願
而不相借安於其化而不相躐蓋雨露之爲潤
而不可窮也日月之爲耀而不可隱也雷霆之
爲威而不可測也至其忘也亦且自以爲吾固
===
有之吾固安之而不辭聖人何有於我也是謂
大順大化治之極也吾故曰聖人之道天道也
嗟乎是道也帝得之而帝王得之而王故其時
雍風動之治平成允殖咸和之治盛德大業蕩
蕩乎民無能名蓋與天同其大矣下是而伯者
操其智術嘵嘵然日號於天下自以爲功嗟乎
亦見其小矣此王伯之辨也雖然心一也誠之
而王則王矣假之而伯則伯矣故子思子曰維
天之命於穆不已蓋曰天之所以爲天也於乎
punctuated:
者，天也。故天下之人，老有所終，幼有所養，鰥寡孤獨得其所安。君臣不得不義，父子不得不親，兄弟不得不順，男女不得不別，比閭族黨不得不睦。善積而必彰，惡積而必癉。天下之人自易其惡，自至其中，而舉不姦於其道，不姦於其治。天之所覆，地之所載，莫不揚休利用，各得其願而不相借，安於其化而不相躐。蓋雨露之爲潤而不可窮也，日月之爲耀而不可隱也，雷霆之爲威而不可測也。至其忘也，亦且自以爲：「吾固有之，吾固安之，而不辭。聖人何有於我也？」是謂大順大化，治之極也。吾故曰：「聖人之道，天道也。」
嗟乎！是道也，帝得之而帝，王得之而王。故其時雍風動之治，平成允殖咸和之治，盛德大業，蕩蕩乎民無能名，蓋與天同其大矣。下是而伯者操其智術，嘵嘵然日號於天下，自以爲功。嗟乎！亦見其小矣。此王伯之辨也。雖然，心一也，誠之而王則王矣，假之而伯則伯矣。故子思子曰：「維天之命，於穆不已。」蓋曰天之所以爲天也。「於乎
translation_en:
…is Heaven. Thus, among all the people under Heaven, the aged are provided for to the end of their lives, the young are nurtured, and widowers, widows, orphans, and the solitary find security. Rulers and ministers cannot but observe righteousness; fathers and sons cannot but love one another; elder and younger brothers cannot but live in concord; men and women cannot but maintain their distinctions; and neighbors, village communities, and kinship groups cannot but live in harmony. Accumulated goodness is certain to be recognized, and accumulated evil is certain to be punished. The people of the world reform their own evil and themselves attain the mean, so that none transgress the Way or disrupt its governance. All whom Heaven covers and Earth supports celebrate its blessings and benefit from its provisions. Each obtains what they desire without borrowing from others; each rests content in its transforming influence without overstepping others. Its moistening influence, like rain and dew, cannot be exhausted; its radiance, like the sun and moon, cannot be concealed; its majesty, like thunder, cannot be fathomed. When people have forgotten it, they even think to themselves: “I have always possessed this; I have always been at ease in it, without demur [?]. What has the sage done for me?” This is called supreme harmony and supreme transformation, the highest perfection of governance. Hence I say: “The Way of the sage is the Way of Heaven.”
Alas! Through obtaining this Way, the ancient emperors became true emperors, and the kings became true kings. Thus their rule brought universal harmony and moved the people as the wind moves things; it brought order to the land and waters, abundant growth, and concord among all. Their magnificent virtue and great achievements were so vast that the people could find no words to describe them: their greatness indeed matched Heaven’s. Below this level, the hegemon wields his cleverness and stratagems, noisily proclaiming himself to the world day after day and taking credit for his accomplishments. Alas! This only reveals his smallness. Such is the distinction between the king and the hegemon. Nevertheless, the mind is one: if one makes it sincere and pursues kingship, one becomes a true king; if one borrows the appearance of virtue and pursues hegemony, one becomes a hegemon. Thus Master Zisi said: “Heaven’s mandate—ah, how profound and unceasing!” This speaks of what makes Heaven Heaven. “Oh! …

title: 嘉靖二十二年江西鄉試錄
text:
不顯文王之德之純蓋曰文王之所以爲文也
是故誠也者天之命也聖人之樞要也天以誠
故無心而成化聖人以誠故有心而無爲誠也
者其天德王道之成乎而愼獨其功也
表
擬宋以韓琦范仲淹爲樞密副使謝表慶
曆三年
同考試官教諭葉　批　賀涇
〔䊀作組織成言　若出二公之手〕
同考試官教諭廖　批
〔四六最宜純厚塲中如此者　而忠愛之心負荷之重雖當時爲之不過如此敬服敬服〕
===
絶少
同考試官學正黃　批　〔詞嚴意懇〕
考試官教授葉　批　〔警拔〕
考試官教授翟　批　〔典則〕
慶曆三年三月某日伏蒙
聖恩以臣琦臣仲淹爲樞密副使者臣琦等誠
惶誠恐稽首頓首上言伏以
punctuated:
不顯文王之德之純！蓋曰文王之所以爲文也。是故誠也者，天之命也，聖人之樞要也。天以誠，故無心而成化；聖人以誠，故有心而無爲。誠也者，其天德王道之成乎！而愼獨其功也。

表
擬宋以韓琦、范仲淹爲樞密副使謝表，慶曆三年。
同考試官教諭葉，批。賀涇。
〔䊀作組織成言，若出二公之手。〕
同考試官教諭廖，批。
〔四六最宜純厚，塲中如此者，而忠愛之心、負荷之重，雖當時爲之，不過如此。敬服！敬服！〕

translation_en:
…“How manifest was the purity of King Wen’s virtue!” This speaks of what made King Wen worthy of the name Wen. Thus sincerity is Heaven’s mandate and the essential pivot of the sage. Through sincerity, Heaven accomplishes transformation without conscious intention; through sincerity, the sage possesses conscious intention yet acts without contrivance. Is sincerity not the consummation of heavenly virtue and the kingly Way? Vigilance when alone is the practice by which it is attained.

Memorial
A hypothetical memorial of thanks for the Song appointment of Han Qi and Fan Zhongyan as Vice Commissioners of the Bureau of Military Affairs, in the third year of Qingli [1043].
By He Jing.

As for its spirit of loyalty and devotion, and its sense of the weight of responsibility, even a composition written on the actual occasion could have done no better. Admirable! Admirable!〕 [“Extremely rare” appears separately after the annotation in the transcription.]
Comment by Associate Examiner Huang, a Director of Studies: 〔Dignified language and earnest intent.〕
Comment by Examiner Ye, a Professor: 〔Striking and outstanding.〕
Comment by Examiner Zhai, a Professor: 〔Classical and exemplary.〕

title: 嘉靖二十二年江西鄉試錄
text:
天極西樞翊
王靈於宥密神兵右府參
廟勝於幾微權總虎符寵伻玉鉉才必兼於
文武任實繫於安危亶聯巖石之具瞻竝
荷
絲綸之榮渥撫循靡措歡懼交增伏念臣琦
奮身疎遠學不逮於中人〔臣仲淹寄跡孤〕
貧志本甘於虀粥安懷用世叨際
昌期釋褐首玷於南宮占雲偶符於太史心
惟慕古每懷鞠瘁之忠志在先憂獨持慷
慨之節馳驅粗勤於郡幕先後謬列於諫
===
垣寢
內降而俯從垂
貞明於日月伏聲言而觸憲涵
大德於雷霆豈拙謀身惟知許
國屢蹶而起百折不回屬靈夏之未賔竊節
旄之誤寵詎曰重厚之可屬自憐樸直之
無私誓戮力於西陲期宣功於兩路城開
punctuated:
天極西樞，翊王靈於宥密；神兵右府，參廟勝於幾微。權總虎符，寵伻玉鉉，才必兼於文武，任實繫於安危。亶聯巖石之具瞻，竝荷絲綸之榮渥。撫循靡措，歡懼交增。
伏念臣琦，奮身疎遠，學不逮於中人；〔臣仲淹寄跡孤〕貧，志本甘於虀粥。安懷用世，叨際昌期。釋褐首玷於南宮，占雲偶符於太史。心惟慕古，每懷鞠瘁之忠；志在先憂，獨持慷慨之節。馳驅粗勤於郡幕，先後謬列於諫垣。寢內降而俯從，垂貞明於日月；伏聲言而觸憲，涵大德於雷霆。豈拙謀身，惟知許國。屢蹶而起，百折不回。屬靈夏之未賔，竊節旄之誤寵。詎曰重厚之可屬，自憐樸直之無私。誓戮力於西陲，期宣功於兩路。城開
translation_en:
…The western pivot of Heaven’s pole upholds Your Majesty’s numinous authority in the secrecy of deliberation; the Right Bureau commanding the imperial forces participates in the court’s plans for victory at their subtlest beginnings. Its authority encompasses the tiger tallies of military command; imperial favor appoints men to the jade handles of the ministerial tripod. Their abilities must embrace both civil and military affairs, for their charge truly determines security or peril. We have indeed joined the ranks of those whom all regard as pillars of the state, and together received the abundant honor of Your Majesty’s decree. Reflecting upon this, we know not how to comport ourselves; joy and apprehension increase together.
We humbly consider that I, your servant Qi, rose from a humble and remote station, my learning falling short even of an ordinary man’s; 〔your servant Zhongyan lived in orphaned〕 poverty, content at heart with pickled greens and gruel. How could we have entertained hopes of employment in the world? Yet undeservedly we encountered this flourishing age. On first exchanging commoners’ clothes for official robes, we presumptuously gained places through the Ministry of Rites examinations; by chance, we fulfilled the Grand Astrologer’s cloud divinations. Our hearts sought only to emulate the ancients, ever cherishing the loyalty that labors to exhaustion; our resolve was to worry before others, steadfastly maintaining a generous and resolute integrity. In our busy service on prefectural staffs, we showed some diligence; in succession, we undeservedly entered the ranks of the remonstrance officials. When we sought to halt orders issued from within the palace, Your Majesty graciously consented, displaying steadfast brightness like the sun and moon; when our utterances brought us into conflict with the law [?], Your Majesty’s thunderous authority harbored great benevolence. Was it merely that we were inept at advancing our own interests? We knew only to devote ourselves to the state. Repeatedly stumbling, we rose again; through a hundred setbacks, we did not turn back.
When Ling and Xia had not yet submitted, we undeservedly received the favor of military command, with its credentials and yak-tail standards. How could we claim to possess the gravity and generosity worthy of such trust? We could only take consolation in our plain honesty and freedom from selfish motives. We vowed to exert our united strength on the western frontier, hoping to render distinguished service in the two circuits. The fortifications opened…

title: 嘉靖二十二年江西鄉試錄
text:
天塹敢攄南仲之謀圖上
帝廷愧無馬援之勇幸
神武而不殺請受纓縻豈威信以能來適逢
兵偃懼犬馬之未稱寧斧鉞之敢逖不謂
破膽之謠上塵
聰聽忽膺
陪幄之召下及踈庸章五上而弗
俞魂屢驚而未定茲蓋伏遇
○
○
○
○
===
凝神恭默
憲天聰明
握三皇五帝之真符續
一祖
二宗之閎烈
聖神文武堯德安安
明類長君文心翼翼
禮樂建中和之極
仁義握威福之權暘耀陰藏海浸河潤迺遒循
punctuated: 天塹，敢攄南仲之謀；圖上帝廷，愧無馬援之勇。幸神武而不殺，請受纓縻；豈威信以能來，適逢兵偃。懼犬馬之未稱，寧斧鉞之敢逖？不謂破膽之謠，上塵聰聽；忽膺陪幄之召，下及踈庸。章五上而弗俞，魂屢驚而未定。茲蓋伏遇○○○○，凝神恭默，憲天聰明，握三皇五帝之真符，續一祖二宗之閎烈。聖神文武，堯德安安；明類長君，文心翼翼。禮樂建中和之極，仁義握威福之權。暘耀陰藏，海浸河潤，迺遒循
translation_en:
…the natural moat: I ventured to deploy a plan like Nan Zhong’s; presenting a map at the imperial court, I was ashamed to lack Ma Yuan’s courage. Fortunately, Your Majesty’s divine martial power prevailed without killing, and they asked to submit to bonds. How could my authority and trustworthiness have brought them to submission? I merely happened upon a time when arms were laid aside. I feared that my humble service was inadequate; how would I dare evade the executioner’s axe? I never imagined that rumors that shattered my courage would rise to trouble Your Majesty’s hearing. Suddenly a summons to attend Your Majesty’s inner councils reached even one as inept and ordinary as myself. Five times I submitted a memorial, but permission to decline was not granted; repeatedly startled, my spirit has yet to settle.
This, I humbly acknowledge, is because I have encountered Your Majesty [four circle marks in the text], who concentrates his spirit in reverent silence and models his perceptiveness upon Heaven; who holds the true warrant of the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors and continues the magnificent achievements of the one imperial ancestor and two imperial forebears. Sagely and divine, accomplished in civil and military affairs, Your Majesty possesses Yao’s virtue with effortless ease. Discerning the kinds of things and acting as sovereign [?], Your Majesty has the reverent heart of King Wen. Through rites and music, you establish the highest standard of equilibrium and harmony; through benevolence and righteousness, you wield the authority to punish and reward. Like sunlight shining and shade sheltering, like the sea’s pervading waters and the river’s moisture, you then follow [?]…

title: 嘉靖二十二年江西鄉試錄
text:
躬夏禹之勤儉
挹虞舜之溫恭服每御於澣衣膳循頒於却
蛤任賢去佞丕宏道長之風昭德塞違屢
下直言之
詔協五珠之上瑞實六穗之康年虎豹熊羆
光絡天象尊罍彝鼎化貫地紘雖恭已而
無爲猶求賢而如渴寵頒
渙命誤採虛名臣等敢不砥節弼諧協毗維
於密勿瀝心籌勝裨粲賛於韜鈐上羿
===
神謨俯酬
輿望斃而後已身自許於孔明知
無不爲心敢殊於寇準苟涓埃之可竭雖
糜殞而弗辭伏願
無怠無荒
惟精惟一
王猷允塞廣綏在宥之仁
文德誕敷靜攝無爲之化
金匱藏周廷之九法泰山
奠漢室之四維臣等無任瞻
punctuated:
躬夏禹之勤儉，挹虞舜之溫恭。服每御於澣衣，膳循頒於却蛤。任賢去佞，丕宏道長之風；昭德塞違，屢下直言之詔。協五珠之上瑞，實六穗之康年。虎豹熊羆，光絡天象；尊罍彝鼎，化貫地紘。雖恭已而無爲，猶求賢而如渴。寵頒渙命，誤採虛名。臣等敢不砥節弼諧，協毗維於密勿；瀝心籌勝，裨粲賛於韜鈐。上羿神謨，俯酬輿望。斃而後已，身自許於孔明；知無不爲，心敢殊於寇準？苟涓埃之可竭，雖糜殞而弗辭。
伏願無怠無荒，惟精惟一。王猷允塞，廣綏在宥之仁；文德誕敷，靜攝無爲之化。金匱藏周廷之九法，泰山奠漢室之四維。臣等無任瞻
translation_en:
…You personally embody the diligence and frugality of Yu of Xia and draw upon the gentleness and reverence of Shun of Yu. You regularly wear washed garments, and the provision of your meals follows the example of refusing clams [?]. You employ the worthy and dismiss flatterers, greatly fostering the ascendancy of the Way; you manifest virtue and restrain wrongdoing, repeatedly issuing edicts inviting frank speech. The supreme auspice of five pearls appears in concord, and stalks bearing six ears bring abundant harvests. Tigers, leopards, and bears shine among the celestial configurations; ritual wine vessels and cauldrons spread your transforming influence to the bounds of the earth. Though you govern through reverent self-possession and nonaction, you still thirst for worthy men.
You have graciously promulgated your imperial command, mistakenly accepting our empty reputations. How could we, your servants, fail to temper our integrity and assist harmonious government, lending support through diligent service; or pour out our hearts in devising victory, contributing our assistance [?] to military strategy? Above, we would assist [?] your divine plans; below, fulfill the hopes of the people. In serving until death, we pledge ourselves to emulate Kongming; in carrying out everything we know to be right, how dare our hearts differ from that of Kou Zhun? If we can exhaust even our smallest capacity to serve, we will not shrink from being crushed and destroyed.
We humbly pray that you remain neither idle nor neglectful, but ever discerning and single-minded. May your royal plans be fully realized, extending the benevolence that brings peace through generous government; may your civil virtue spread far and wide, quietly sustaining the transforming influence of nonaction. May the metal coffer preserve the nine laws of the Zhou court, and may Mount Tai secure the four sustaining bonds of the Han house. We, your servants, cannot contain ourselves as we gaze…

title: 嘉靖二十二年江西鄉試錄
text:
天仰
聖激切屏營之至謹奉
表稱
謝以
聞
第叄場
策五道
第一問
張仲
同考試官教諭祝　批〔讀子此作善摸寫〕
===
聖心之純其亦涵濡而有得者與
同考試官學正陳　批〔善鋪張處不可及〕
考試官教授葉　批〔推本敬一最得本原〕
考試官教授翟　批〔忠愛之言〕
帝王所天天永命之道二曰敬天也法祖也
夫所謂敬天者必吾之精神常與天心相
為流通非徒脩飾於對越之時而已也夫
所謂法祖者亦惟聿脩厥德以光大前人
punctuated:
天仰聖，激切屏營之至，謹奉表稱謝以聞。
第叄場，策五道。第一問。張仲。
同考試官教諭祝批〔讀子此作善摸寫〕聖心之純，其亦涵濡而有得者與？
同考試官學正陳批〔善鋪張處不可及〕
考試官教授葉批〔推本敬一最得本原〕
考試官教授翟批〔忠愛之言〕
帝王所天天永命之道二：曰敬天也，法祖也。夫所謂敬天者，必吾之精神常與天心相為流通，非徒脩飾於對越之時而已也。夫所謂法祖者，亦惟聿脩厥德，以光大前人
translation_en:
…looking up to Heaven and reverently regarding Your Majesty, with the utmost heartfelt fervor and trembling awe, we respectfully submit this memorial to express our gratitude for Your Majesty’s hearing.
Third session: five policy essays. First question. Zhang Zhong.
Associate Examiner Zhu, Instructor, comments: “Reading this composition of yours, I find that you skillfully depict the purity of the imperial mind. Have you, too, gained understanding through immersion in its influence?”
Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: “Your skill in expansive exposition is unsurpassable.”
Examiner Ye, Professor, comments: “By tracing matters back to reverent single-mindedness, you have most successfully grasped their fundamental source.”
Examiner Zhai, Professor, comments: “Words of loyalty and affection.”
There are two ways by which emperors and kings serve Heaven and perpetuate their mandate [?]: revering Heaven and emulating their ancestors. What is meant by revering Heaven requires that one’s spirit constantly commune with Heaven’s mind; it is not merely a matter of cultivating an outward bearing when standing reverently before Heaven. What is meant by emulating the ancestors likewise consists in continuing to cultivate their virtue, thereby bringing greater glory to one’s predecessors’…

title: 嘉靖二十二年江西鄉試錄
text:
之業非徒規規於制度文爲之間而已也
此之謂窮神則善繼其志知化則善述其
事所以上亨天心光昭先德垂盛美而保
大業也嗚呼此帝王傳心之要法而我
皇上敬
天法
祖之學可以仰窺其萬一矣嘗聞之書曰欽若
昊天敬授人時言敬天也則敬天之說見
於詩而非始於詩也詩曰不愆不忘率由
===
舊章言法祖也則法祖之說見於書而非
止於書也蓋自精一執中之訓闡於堯舜
而心法之傳有自來矣嗣是而興禹之祗
台湯之顧諟文王之昭事武王之上帝臨
女皆所以敬天也啓之敬承太甲之圖終
高宗之思道成王之繼序皆所以法祖也
蓋古之聖人終日乾乾無一時而不對越
于天而所以覲揚先王之耿光大烈者兢
兢然惟恐失墜粹乎無以議者此也後世
punctuated: 之業，非徒規規於制度文爲之間而已也。此之謂窮神則善繼其志，知化則善述其事，所以上亨天心，光昭先德，垂盛美而保大業也。嗚呼！此帝王傳心之要法，而我皇上敬天法祖之學，可以仰窺其萬一矣。嘗聞之，《書》曰：「欽若昊天，敬授人時。」言敬天也，則敬天之說見於《詩》，而非始於《詩》也。《詩》曰：「不愆不忘，率由舊章。」言法祖也，則法祖之說見於《書》，而非止於《書》也。蓋自精一執中之訓闡於堯舜，而心法之傳有自來矣。嗣是而興，禹之祗台，湯之顧諟，文王之昭事，武王之上帝臨女，皆所以敬天也；啓之敬承，太甲之圖終，高宗之思道，成王之繼序，皆所以法祖也。蓋古之聖人終日乾乾，無一時而不對越于天，而所以覲揚先王之耿光大烈者，兢兢然惟恐失墜。粹乎無以議者，此也。後世
translation_en:
…the achievements of their predecessors, rather than merely confining themselves to institutions, regulations, and formal observances. This is what is meant by fathoming the spirit and thus carrying forward their intentions well, and understanding transformation and thus continuing their undertakings well. By these means, rulers reach the heart of Heaven above, gloriously illuminate their predecessors’ virtue, transmit their splendid excellence, and preserve their great enterprise. Ah! These are the essential methods by which emperors and kings transmit the teaching of the heart. Through them we may reverently glimpse a fraction of our Emperor’s learning in revering Heaven and emulating his ancestors.

I have heard it said that the Book of Documents declares: “Reverently conform to august Heaven, and respectfully impart to the people the seasons for their labors.” This speaks of revering Heaven. Thus, although the teaching of revering Heaven appears in the Book of Odes, it did not originate with that book. The Book of Odes says: “Neither erring nor forgetting, follow the old statutes.” This speaks of emulating the ancestors. Thus, although the teaching of emulating the ancestors appears in the Book of Documents, it is not confined to that book.

Ever since Yao and Shun elucidated the injunction to remain discerning and single-minded and hold fast to the mean, the transmission of this teaching of the heart has had an established source. Among those who arose thereafter, Yu’s reverent attention to himself [?], Tang’s constant regard for Heaven’s bright mandate, King Wen’s illustrious service, and King Wu’s admonition that “the Lord on High watches over you” were all ways of revering Heaven. Qi’s reverent succession, Tai Jia’s concern to carry through to the end, Gaozong’s contemplation of the Way, and King Cheng’s continuation of the succession were all ways of emulating the ancestors.

The sages of antiquity were tirelessly diligent throughout the day; there was never a moment when they did not stand reverently before Heaven. In honoring and extolling the brilliant radiance and great achievements of the former kings, they were ever watchful, fearing only that they might let this inheritance fall away. Herein lay their purity, beyond reproach. In later ages…

title: 嘉靖二十二年江西鄉試錄
text:
正心之學弗講徒欲借之以爲昭假對揚
之具是故避殿減膳罪已求言亦曰克謹
天戒也然而彌文之飾適以爲瀆慨慕貞
觀編類聖範亦曰世德作求也然而陳迹
之拘奚補於治甚至有爲天變不足畏祖
宗不足法之說者則大戾也於乎此理欲
之分而理亂安危之判也愚嘗伏讀
聖政之記
祖訓之編矣我
===
太祖高皇帝以
天縱之聖當貞元之會奮跡淮甸用夏變夷
執符御曆以復我帝王之天下蓋自開闢以
來
巍功煥文上比跡於堯舜湯武之盛昭明高
朗與天無極故其大經大法巨細畢備
宏謨懿範萬代如見其言敬天曰天道微妙
難知人事感通易見天人一理必以類應
又曰人以一心對越上帝毫髮不誠怠心
punctuated:
正心之學弗講，徒欲借之以爲昭假對揚之具。是故避殿減膳，罪已求言，亦曰克謹天戒也；然而彌文之飾，適以爲瀆。慨慕貞觀，編類聖範，亦曰世德作求也；然而陳迹之拘，奚補於治？甚至有爲天變不足畏、祖宗不足法之說者，則大戾也。於乎！此理欲之分，而理亂安危之判也。
愚嘗伏讀《聖政之記》、《祖訓之編》矣。我太祖高皇帝以天縱之聖，當貞元之會，奮跡淮甸，用夏變夷，執符御曆，以復我帝王之天下。蓋自開闢以來，巍功煥文，上比跡於堯舜湯武之盛，昭明高朗，與天無極。故其大經大法，巨細畢備；宏謨懿範，萬代如見。其言敬天曰：「天道微妙難知，人事感通易見。天人一理，必以類應。」又曰：「人以一心對越上帝，毫髮不誠，怠心
translation_en:
…the learning of rectifying the heart went unstudied, and people merely sought to borrow it as a means of approaching Heaven and acknowledging ancestral blessings. Thus they withdrew from the main hall, reduced their meals, reproached themselves, and solicited advice, claiming thereby to heed Heaven’s warnings conscientiously. Yet these elaborate displays of ceremonial observance served only to show disrespect. They yearned admiringly for the Zhenguan reign and compiled classified collections of sagely precedents, claiming thereby to carry forward the virtue of successive generations. Yet what benefit to government could come from confinement to the traces of the past? Some even advanced the claim that Heaven’s anomalies need not be feared and the imperial ancestors need not be followed as models: this was a grave departure from the proper way. Alas! Here lies the distinction between principle and selfish desire, and the dividing line between order and disorder, security and peril.
I have humbly read the Record of Sagely Governance and the Compilation of Ancestral Instructions. Our Emperor Taizu Gao, endowed by Heaven with sagely wisdom, arose at the juncture of cyclical renewal. He rose to prominence in the Huai region and transformed the barbarians through Chinese civilization. Taking up the mandate and assuming imperial rule, he restored to us the realm of the ancient emperors and kings. Since the beginning of the world, his towering achievements and brilliant civil accomplishments have rivaled the flourishing ages of Yao, Shun, Tang, and Wu. Radiant, lofty, and luminous, they are as boundless as Heaven. Thus his great guiding principles and laws were complete in every detail, great and small; his grand plans and excellent models remain as vividly present as if seen before one’s eyes, for ten thousand generations.
Speaking of reverence for Heaven, he said: “The Way of Heaven is subtle and difficult to know; the responsive connection manifested in human affairs is readily seen. Heaven and humanity share one principle and must respond to one another according to their kind.” He also said: “A person stands before the Lord on High with a single heart. If there is the slightest insincerity, a negligent heart…”

title: 嘉靖二十二年江西鄉試錄
text:
必秉其機至於露禱蒙席卽降甘澍致齋
觀心上契冲漠赫赫乎天地之鑒臨也其
作
祖訓曰日月之能久照萬世不改其明堯舜之
道不息萬世不改其行又曰荒墜厥緒幾
於亡夏顚覆典刑幾於亡商其言具悉周
至㢈思於日夜委曲開諭時召於燕閒洋
洋乎萬世之
光訓也
===
列聖相承夙夜祗惕守爲家法彌引翼而昌大
之而我
聖祖之
聖功峻烈益以闡耀恭惟我
皇上文武聖神繼
天立極所以克享
天心光昭
祖訓無不竭其精衷詰其指極摩復
四郊之祀而天地以位焉日月以明焉故其
punctuated:
必秉其機。」至於露禱蒙席，卽降甘澍；致齋觀心，上契冲漠，赫赫乎天地之鑒臨也！其作《祖訓》曰：「日月之能久照，萬世不改其明；堯舜之道不息，萬世不改其行。」又曰：「荒墜厥緒，幾於亡夏；顚覆典刑，幾於亡商。」其言具悉周至，㢈思於日夜，委曲開諭，時召於燕閒，洋洋乎萬世之光訓也！
列聖相承，夙夜祗惕，守爲家法，彌引翼而昌大之，而我聖祖之聖功峻烈益以闡耀。恭惟我皇上文武聖神，繼天立極，所以克享天心、光昭祖訓，無不竭其精衷，詰其指極。摩復四郊之祀，而天地以位焉，日月以明焉，故其
translation_en:
…will surely seize its opportunity.” When he prayed under the open sky, covered with a mat, welcome rain immediately descended. Through ritual purification and contemplation of his heart, he attained accord above with the silent, formless realm. How manifestly Heaven and Earth watched over him! In composing the Ancestral Instructions (Zuxun), he said: “The sun and moon can shine enduringly because, through ten thousand generations, they do not alter their brightness. The Way of Yao and Shun never ceases because, through ten thousand generations, its practice remains unchanged.” He also said: “Neglecting and letting fall the inherited enterprise brings one close to the ruin of the Xia; overturning established norms brings one close to the ruin of the Shang.” His words were comprehensive and thorough. He pondered them day and night [?], explaining and instructing in full detail, and from time to time summoned his subjects during his leisure. How abundant were these glorious instructions for ten thousand generations!
Successive sage emperors inherited them, remaining reverent and vigilant morning and night, preserving them as the house laws of the dynasty, and continually furthering and enlarging them. Thus the sacred achievements and towering accomplishments of our sagely founder shone ever more brilliantly. We reverently consider that our present emperor, accomplished in civil and martial affairs, sagely and divinely perceptive, succeeds Heaven and establishes the supreme standard. In seeking to win Heaven’s favor and illuminate the Ancestral Instructions, he exhausts his utmost sincerity and examines their ultimate purport. He has restored [?] the sacrifices at the four suburban altars, whereby Heaven and Earth occupy their proper positions and the sun and moon shine in their proper brightness. Thus his…

title: 嘉靖二十二年江西鄉試錄
text:
精誠之所格流通於玄漠禱雨而雨禱雪
而雪其或水旱風霾之變則又祇懼於仁
愛之眷痛加脩省下及臣工以回
天意此與我
聖祖之心豈異也恢宏
九廟之制而
祖功
宗德以隆焉
嚴父
===
慈母以親焉故其仁孝之所達大歆於祫享見
堯於墻見堯於羹乃又肇於
皇史宬之建
追先閣之勒尊崇
訓錄憲章
祖德此與我
聖祖之心又豈異也雖然此特其文者耳愚嘗
莊誦我
皇上敬一之箴心箴之註矣夫敬也者存其心
punctuated: 精誠之所格，流通於玄漠，禱雨而雨，禱雪而雪。其或水旱風霾之變，則又祇懼於仁愛之眷，痛加脩省，下及臣工，以回天意。此與我聖祖之心豈異也？恢宏九廟之制，而祖功宗德以隆焉，嚴父慈母以親焉。故其仁孝之所達，大歆於祫享，見堯於墻，見堯於羹。乃又肇於皇史宬之建、追先閣之勒，尊崇訓錄，憲章祖德。此與我聖祖之心又豈異也？雖然，此特其文者耳。愚嘗莊誦我皇上《敬一》之箴、《心箴》之註矣。夫敬也者，存其心
translation_en:
…His perfect sincerity reaches into and pervades the mysterious, unseen realm: when he prays for rain, rain falls; when he prays for snow, snow falls. Should there be such calamities as floods, droughts, violent winds, or dust storms, he responds with reverent fear to Heaven’s benevolent solicitude, earnestly undertaking self-cultivation and self-examination and extending these requirements to his officials, so as to turn Heaven’s intent. How could this differ from the heart of our sagely founding ancestor?

He has enlarged and enhanced the system of the Nine Ancestral Temples, thereby exalting the achievements and virtues of his ancestors and drawing close to his august father and loving mother. Thus, through the reach of his benevolence and filial devotion, the ancestral spirits greatly delight in the joint ancestral sacrifice. He sees Yao upon the wall and sees Yao in his broth. He has moreover initiated the construction of the Imperial Historical Archives, Huangshicheng, and the engraving of inscriptions at the Pavilion for Honoring Ancestors, Zhuixiange, revering the recorded ancestral instructions and taking ancestral virtue as his model. How, again, could this differ from the heart of our sagely founding ancestor?

Even so, these are merely its outward manifestations. I, in my ignorance, have reverently recited Our Majesty’s Admonition on Reverence and Unity and his commentary on the Admonition of the Mind. Reverence means preserving one’s mind…

title: 嘉靖二十二年江西鄉試錄
text:
而不忽也一也者純乎理而無雜也而脩
之
郊廟之顯閒居之隱言行之大終始之純何其
嚴也夫視聽言動純於心者不欲其攻取
於物也而求之邪正之分忠讒之辯號令
之謹妄動之戒何其切也敬一交養內外
合一此
聖心獨得之妙信未易以窺測而名言者愚嘗
伏讀我
===
聖祖觀心亭之記有曰體道凝神誠一弗二擬
問心有曰運之至精守之永久則其心源
之相接愚又有以仰窺
聖祖
神孫之合德雖堯舜之執中禹湯文武之敬德
其精蘊無以加於此矣記曰惟孝子爲能
饗親惟仁人爲能饗帝此之謂也而執事
又欲以爲今日祈天永命之一助顧豈有
芻蕘之言可裨於堯舜禹湯文武者哉執
punctuated: 而不忽也。一也者，純乎理而無雜也。而脩之，郊廟之顯、閒居之隱、言行之大、終始之純，何其嚴也！夫視聽言動，純於心者，不欲其攻取於物也。而求之，邪正之分、忠讒之辯、號令之謹、妄動之戒，何其切也！敬一交養，內外合一，此聖心獨得之妙，信未易以窺測而名言者。愚嘗伏讀我聖祖《觀心亭之記》，有曰：「體道凝神，誠一弗二。」《擬問心》有曰：「運之至精，守之永久。」則其心源之相接，愚又有以仰窺聖祖神孫之合德。雖堯舜之執中，禹湯文武之敬德，其精蘊無以加於此矣。《記》曰：「惟孝子爲能饗親，惟仁人爲能饗帝。」此之謂也。而執事又欲以爲今日祈天永命之一助，顧豈有芻蕘之言可裨於堯舜禹湯文武者哉？執
translation_en:
…and does not neglect it. Oneness means being wholly grounded in principle, without admixture. In cultivating this—in the public solemnity of the suburban sacrifices and ancestral temples, in the privacy of leisure, in the great matters of speech and conduct, and in purity from beginning to end—how exacting he is! Seeing, hearing, speaking, and acting must be pure within the mind: he does not wish them to pursue and seize upon external things. In seeking this—in distinguishing the deviant from the correct, discerning loyalty from slander, exercising care in issuing commands, and guarding against rash action—how earnest he is! Reverence and oneness nourish each other; the inner and outer become one. This is the subtle understanding uniquely attained by the sagely imperial mind, which is indeed difficult to fathom or express in words.

I have reverently read our sagely founder’s Record of the Pavilion for Contemplating the Mind, which says: “Embody the Way and concentrate the spirit; be sincere and single-minded, without division.” His Imagined Questions to the Mind says: “Exercise it with the utmost refinement; preserve it forever.” From this continuity in the wellspring of their minds, I can also glimpse with reverence the unity in virtue between the sagely founder and his divine descendant. Even Yao and Shun’s holding fast to the Mean, and Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu’s reverence for virtue, could add nothing to the profound essence of this. The Book of Rites says: “Only a filial son can offer sacrifice to his parents; only a humane person can offer sacrifice to the Supreme Deity.” This is what it means.

Yet you, sir, also wish to obtain some assistance toward praying to Heaven today for an enduring Mandate. But could the words of a humble grass-cutter or wood-gatherer possibly benefit a Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, or Wu? You…

title: 嘉靖二十二年江西鄉試錄
text:
事久道化成之說天行不息之說固已言
之矣眞惓惓忠愛之懷也愚也惟願加之
意而已
第二問
鍾崇武
考試官教授葉　批〔周公良法美意自足無斁顧舉　而用之何如耳子發明殆盡可嘉〕
考試官教授翟　批〔經權並用治道在所不免讀此　亦見子之用世矣〕
===
善治者任人而不專於人故分肅任法而
不泥於法故機神蓋聖人之道有經焉有
權焉經者法之常所以定天下之志也志
定而分斯肅矣權者法之變所以作天下
之氣也氣作而機斯神矣志不定氣不作
則人將有懈怠廢弛之患自恃取必之心
故善治者必任法於人而時或操縱於巳
使權嘗運於法之外而法自囿於權之中
此天下之志以定天下之氣以作而治道
punctuated:
事久道化成之說、天行不息之說，固已言之矣，眞惓惓忠愛之懷也。愚也惟願加之意而已。

第二問
鍾崇武
考試官教授葉　批〔周公良法美意，自足無斁，顧舉　而用之何如耳。子發明殆盡，可嘉。〕
考試官教授翟　批〔經權並用，治道在所不免。讀此，亦見子之用世矣。〕

善治者任人而不專於人，故分肅；任法而不泥於法，故機神。蓋聖人之道有經焉，有權焉。經者，法之常，所以定天下之志也。志定而分斯肅矣。權者，法之變，所以作天下之氣也。氣作而機斯神矣。志不定，氣不作，則人將有懈怠廢弛之患、自恃取必之心。故善治者必任法於人，而時或操縱於巳，使權嘗運於法之外，而法自囿於權之中。此天下之志以定，天下之氣以作，而治道
translation_en:
…you have already spoken of transformation achieved through enduring adherence to the Way, and of Heaven’s ceaseless movement. These words truly express your earnest loyalty and concern. I, in my ignorance, wish only that you give them further attention.

Second Policy Question
Zhong Chongwu
Examiner, Professor Ye, comments: 〔The Duke of Zhou’s excellent laws and fine intentions are in themselves worthy of unflagging adherence; the issue is simply how they are put into practice. Your elucidation is nearly exhaustive—commendable indeed.〕
Examiner, Professor Zhai, comments: 〔Employing both constant principles and discretionary judgment is unavoidable in the art of government. Reading this, one also sees your capacity to serve the world.〕

Those skilled in governing entrust responsibilities to people without relying exclusively upon them; thus the distinctions of responsibility remain ordered. They rely upon laws without being bound rigidly by them; thus their responses to circumstances are wondrously effective. For the Way of the sages embraces both constant principles and discretionary judgment. Constant principles are the enduring norms of law, by which the purposes of all under Heaven are settled. Once those purposes are settled, distinctions of responsibility become orderly. Discretionary judgment is the adaptation of law, by which the energies of all under Heaven are roused. Once those energies are roused, responses to circumstances become wondrously effective. If purposes are unsettled and energies unstirred, people will fall prey to indolence and neglect, and develop a self-reliant insistence on having their own way. Thus those skilled in governing must entrust the administration of law to others, while at times retaining in their own hands the power to tighten or loosen control. They allow discretion to operate beyond the law, while the law itself is encompassed within discretion. Through this, the purposes of all under Heaven are settled, their energies are roused, and the Way of government…

title: 嘉靖二十二年江西鄉試錄
text:
可舉治化可成也愚請因執事明問而陳
之唐虞之治粹乎其不可及已夏后氏尚
忠先賞後罰商人尚質先罰後賞尊尊親
親之道其始也非專一於寛寛嚴未必不善
夫何世衰道微無能以通其變而時異勢
殊雖聖人豈能保其終此其蠢野驕蕩之
敝不可勝數矣周公懲二代之敝因時制
宜作爲周禮一書觀其以治國之道莫切
於張官置吏也官吏不職則治道爲之不
===
振立國之本莫切於愛民也民罔協中則
國本爲之不立所以有八柄以馭百官有
八統以馭萬民是臣之所理者禮樂刑政
皆天工也使事不總於一則三百六十之
屬渙散無統於是六卿各率其屬以聽於
冢宰警飭而不敢怠無非所以奉太宰之
治是百官之志蓋有所定矣夫太宰兼行
之使毎歲不受其會以詔王則生殺予奪
不出於天子焉知一定之法可恃耶故邪
punctuated: 可舉，治化可成也。愚請因執事明問而陳之。唐虞之治，粹乎其不可及已！夏后氏尚忠，先賞後罰；商人尚質，先罰後賞。尊尊親親之道，其始也非專一於寛，寛嚴未必不善。夫何世衰道微，無能以通其變，而時異勢殊，雖聖人豈能保其終？此其蠢野驕蕩之敝，不可勝數矣。周公懲二代之敝，因時制宜，作爲《周禮》一書。觀其以治國之道，莫切於張官置吏也；官吏不職，則治道爲之不振。立國之本，莫切於愛民也；民罔協中，則國本爲之不立。所以有八柄以馭百官，有八統以馭萬民。是臣之所理者，禮樂刑政，皆天工也。使事不總於一，則三百六十之屬渙散無統。於是六卿各率其屬以聽於冢宰，警飭而不敢怠，無非所以奉太宰之治。是百官之志，蓋有所定矣。夫太宰兼行之，使毎歲不受其會以詔王，則生殺予奪不出於天子，焉知一定之法可恃耶？故邪
translation_en:
…can be put into practice, and transformative governance can be achieved. In my humble judgment, allow me to expound upon this in response to your discerning question. The governance of Tang and Yu was so pure that it could not be equaled! The Xia rulers esteemed loyalty, placing rewards before punishments; the Shang people esteemed substance, placing punishments before rewards. Their ways of honoring the honored and cherishing kin were not, at their inception, devoted exclusively to leniency. Both leniency and severity could serve good ends. Yet why was it that, as the age declined and the Way waned, no one could adapt these practices to changing circumstances? With times and conditions altered, how could even a sage guarantee their ultimate outcome? The resulting evils of uncouthness, arrogance, and license were beyond counting.

Taking warning from the evils of the two preceding dynasties, the Duke of Zhou fashioned measures appropriate to his time and composed the book Rites of Zhou (Zhouli). Looking at its approach to governing a state, nothing is more urgent than establishing offices and appointing officials: when officials fail in their duties, the way of government languishes. As for the foundation of a state, nothing is more urgent than caring for the people: when the people fail to accord with the mean, the state's foundation cannot stand. Hence there are eight handles for controlling the officials and eight unifying principles for governing the myriad people. What ministers administer—rites, music, punishments, and government—are all Heaven's work. If affairs were not brought under a single authority, the three hundred and sixty offices would be scattered, lacking unified direction. Thus the six ministers each lead their subordinates in obeying the Minister of State (Zhongzai). Vigilant and disciplined, they dare not be negligent; all their efforts serve the governance of the Grand Steward (Taizai). In this way, the purposes of the officials have something to settle upon.

Now, the Grand Steward exercises these functions together. If he did not receive their annual accounts and report them to the king, then the powers of life and death, granting and taking away, would not proceed from the Son of Heaven. How could one know that a fixed system of laws could be relied upon? Thus, the wrongful [?] …

title: 嘉靖二十二年江西鄉試錄
text:
之大者必歸於王欲其總攬乾剛獨斷於
上太宰則不過守成憲之常耳若内府供
王之好賜予及冢宰之好賜予此好賜予
之常也若司會以周知四國之治及冢宰
廢置之常也若小宰之六叙以正
其位以置其食此祿位稍食之常也若表
記言親而不尊祭義言貴親尚齒此親親
之常也太宰守其常不得違道以自私是
太宰之志亦有所定矣在下欲干其法也
===
制於天子而不敢在上欲易其法也守於
太宰而不能稽始慮終相維相濟任人而
不專於人其分肅者有如此然使一切聽
於法而無闔闢出入於其間則吾之法有
時而窮人情取必之餘亦有時而玩是非
可常之道也故自八柄言之有德者宜貴
也或無爵而未貴有功者宜富也或無祿
而未富或置之尊貴而使自愛或奪其榮
富而使貧窶凡此皆人主所用以聳動天
punctuated: 之大者必歸於王，欲其總攬乾剛，獨斷於上。太宰則不過守成憲之常耳。若内府供王之好賜予及冢宰之好賜予，此好賜予之常也；若司會以周知四國之治及冢宰，廢置之常也；若小宰之六叙，以正其位，以置其食，此祿位稍食之常也；若《表記》言親而不尊，《祭義》言貴親尚齒，此親親之常也。太宰守其常，不得違道以自私，是太宰之志亦有所定矣。在下欲干其法也，制於天子而不敢；在上欲易其法也，守於太宰而不能。稽始慮終，相維相濟，任人而不專於人，其分肅者有如此。然使一切聽於法，而無闔闢出入於其間，則吾之法有時而窮，人情取必之餘，亦有時而玩，是非可常之道也。故自八柄言之，有德者宜貴也，或無爵而未貴；有功者宜富也，或無祿而未富；或置之尊貴而使自愛，或奪其榮富而使貧窶。凡此皆人主所用以聳動天
translation_en:
…the greatest of these must be referred to the king, so that he may hold sovereign authority in its entirety and decide alone from above. The Grand Steward, however, merely observes the standing provisions of established statutes. For example, the Inner Treasury supplies the gifts and rewards bestowed at the pleasure of the king and of the Grand Steward: these are the standing provisions for such gifts and rewards. The Grand Accountant comprehensively ascertains the administration of the realms in all four directions, together with the Grand Steward [?]: these are the standing provisions for dismissal and appointment. The Lesser Steward’s six rules of precedence rectify officials’ positions and determine their allowances: these are the standing provisions for rank, emoluments, and grain allowances. The chapter “Record of Exemplary Conduct” speaks of showing affection without conferring honor, while “The Meaning of Sacrifices” speaks of honoring relatives and respecting seniority: these are the standing provisions for treating kin with familial affection. The Grand Steward observes these standing provisions and may not depart from the Way to serve his own interests. Thus the Grand Steward’s purposes, too, have a settled direction.

Should those below wish to infringe these rules, they are restrained by the Son of Heaven and dare not do so; should the ruler above wish to alter them, they are upheld by the Grand Steward, and he cannot do so. Examining beginnings and considering outcomes, they constrain and assist one another. Responsibility is entrusted to men without allowing it to rest exclusively with them: such is the strictness of their respective spheres. Yet if everything were governed by fixed rules, with no room for opening or closing, inclusion or exclusion, those rules would sometimes reach their limits. Once people came to count on certain outcomes, they would also sometimes treat the rules lightly. This is no enduring way of governing.

Thus, speaking of the eight instruments of authority, those with virtue ought to be honored, yet some have no noble rank and remain without honor; those with merit ought to be enriched, yet some have no emoluments and remain without wealth. Sometimes a man is placed in an honored and exalted position so that he will cherish his standing; sometimes he is stripped of his glory and wealth and reduced to poverty. All these are means employed by the ruler to stir all under Heaven…

title: 嘉靖二十二年江西鄉試錄
text:
下之具而不使人有自必者也自八統言
之親故賓客固當敦敬而尊禮賢能勳貴
固當任使而保護然恃恩者易驕恃才者
易傲而服勤盡瘁之士亦不能無累日取
貴之心令也親親未巳而賢賢繼之尊貴
未巳而下下繼之不拘於一而迭出於八
此又人主之所用以爲轉移變化之術而
不使有自恃之心我可以取必於人而人
不可以取必於我任法而不泥於法其機
===
神者有如此故太宰之分惟守其常以待
百官萬民有一定之法人主用其權抑揚
進退皆在我而百官萬民不得執法以要
君使天下之人見太宰必然之法不敢以
不自盡見人主或然或不然之權内不敢
以自恃外不敢以自必激昂奮勵懈怠者
强於爲善廢弛者興舉無窮此成周之世
所以無一官不盡其職無一民不入於善
天下之氣以作而志亦於是乎定矣後世
punctuated:
下之具，而不使人有自必者也。自八統言之，親故賓客固當敦敬而尊禮，賢能勳貴固當任使而保護。然恃恩者易驕，恃才者易傲，而服勤盡瘁之士亦不能無累日取貴之心。令也，親親未巳而賢賢繼之，尊貴未巳而下下繼之，不拘於一而迭出於八。此又人主之所用以爲轉移變化之術，而不使有自恃之心。我可以取必於人，而人不可以取必於我；任法而不泥於法，其機神者有如此。

故太宰之分，惟守其常，以待百官萬民，有一定之法；人主用其權，抑揚進退皆在我，而百官萬民不得執法以要君。使天下之人見太宰必然之法，不敢以不自盡；見人主或然或不然之權，内不敢以自恃，外不敢以自必。激昂奮勵，懈怠者强於爲善，廢弛者興舉無窮。此成周之世所以無一官不盡其職，無一民不入於善，天下之氣以作，而志亦於是乎定矣。後世
translation_en:
…means for stirring all under Heaven, without allowing anyone to count on a guaranteed outcome. As for the eight principles of unification, relatives, old associates, and guests should certainly be treated with sincere respect and honored with due ceremony; the worthy, the capable, the meritorious, and the noble should certainly be employed and protected. Yet those who rely on favor readily become presumptuous, and those who rely on talent readily become arrogant. Even men who labor diligently and exhaust themselves in service cannot be entirely free of the hope that accumulated days of service will bring them high status. Now [?], before showing affection to relatives has ceased, honoring the worthy follows; before honoring the noble has ceased, condescending to the lowly follows. The ruler does not confine himself to one principle but draws on all eight in turn. This, too, is a means by which the ruler effects shifts and transformations, preventing people from becoming complacently self-reliant. I may demand certain performance from others, but others may not demand certain treatment from me. He relies on established rules without being bound by them: such is the wondrous subtlety of his operation.

Thus the Grand Steward’s duty is simply to uphold constant standards, dealing with the hundred officials and the myriad people through fixed rules. The ruler exercises discretionary authority: raising or lowering, advancing or dismissing—all lie with him, and officials and people may not invoke the rules to constrain their sovereign. When people throughout the realm see the Grand Steward’s invariably applied rules, they dare not fail to exert themselves fully. When they see the ruler’s discretion to act one way or otherwise, inwardly they dare not presume upon their advantages, and outwardly they dare not count on any guaranteed outcome. Aroused and striving, the indolent exert themselves to do good, and neglected affairs are revived and carried forward without end. This is why, in the age of the perfected Zhou order, no official failed to fulfill his duties and no person failed to turn toward goodness. The vitality of all under Heaven was thereby roused, and their resolve was also thereby settled. In later ages…

title: 嘉靖二十二年江西鄉試錄
text:
頌周公之聖舉成王於有道之隆者良以
此耳至其衰也則法是而人非矣穆王區
區志於復古然關雎麟趾之意不存焉治
敎政刑皆神化之糟粕而已何怪其治不
古若哉恭惟我
國家創制立法師意周官參酌盡善如六卿
之分職而羣吏之黜陟則吏部主之諸司
有職掌臺諫得舉刺而考課殿最則銓衡
揆之至於予奪廢置則固聽於
宸斷而不敢自擅上下相維人法並用此
===
祖宗以來所以身致太平也肆我
皇上天縱神聖鋭意中興總攬
乾綱精覈吏治仁義惠威之用斷自
聖心神明變化之機有如天運何者非
聖人之大權乎將事之臣又皆仰承
休德日兢兢焉勉舉其職庶明勵翼而無出
位之思又何莫非
聖人之大經乎宜天下化中莫不鼓舞震慴親
punctuated:
頌周公之聖，舉成王於有道之隆者，良以此耳。至其衰也，則法是而人非矣。穆王區區志於復古，然關雎麟趾之意不存焉，治敎政刑皆神化之糟粕而已，何怪其治不古若哉？恭惟我國家創制立法，師意周官，參酌盡善。如六卿之分職，而羣吏之黜陟則吏部主之；諸司有職掌，臺諫得舉刺，而考課殿最則銓衡揆之。至於予奪廢置，則固聽於宸斷而不敢自擅。上下相維，人法並用，此祖宗以來所以身致太平也。
肆我皇上天縱神聖，鋭意中興，總攬乾綱，精覈吏治。仁義惠威之用，斷自聖心；神明變化之機，有如天運，何者非聖人之大權乎？將事之臣又皆仰承休德，日兢兢焉勉舉其職，庶明勵翼，而無出位之思，又何莫非聖人之大經乎？宜天下化中，莫不鼓舞震慴，親
translation_en:
…that later generations praise the Duke of Zhou’s sagacity and exalt King Cheng as a ruler under whom the Way greatly flourished is indeed for this reason alone. When that order declined, however, the laws remained right, but the men were no longer worthy. King Mu earnestly aspired to restore antiquity, yet the spirit of “Guanju” (The Ospreys) and “Linzhi” (The Qilin’s Hoof) was absent. Administration, instruction, government, and punishment were merely the dregs of a transformative influence once wondrously effective. What wonder that his government failed to equal that of antiquity? Reverently considering our dynasty, in creating institutions and establishing laws it has followed the intent of the Offices of Zhou, weighing and adapting their provisions to achieve the utmost excellence. Thus, duties are divided among the six ministers, while the demotion and promotion of officials are directed by the Ministry of Personnel. The various offices have their assigned responsibilities, and the censors and remonstrance officials may commend or impeach; the authorities charged with personnel selection assess the lowest and highest ratings in evaluations of official performance. As for granting and withdrawing, dismissing and appointing, they assuredly defer to the imperial decision and dare not act on their own authority. Superiors and subordinates sustain one another, and men and laws are employed together. This is how our imperial ancestors brought about Great Peace through their own efforts.
Now our emperor, endowed by Heaven with divine sagacity, is resolutely intent upon restoring prosperity. He holds all sovereign authority in his hands and scrutinizes the administration of officials with precision. The exercise of benevolence, righteousness, gracious favor, and awe-inspiring authority is determined by his sagely mind; the workings of his wondrous adaptations resemble the movements of Heaven. Which of these is not the sage’s great discretionary power? The ministers who carry out affairs all reverently receive his excellent virtue. Daily vigilant, they strive to discharge their duties; the assembled worthies diligently assist him, without any thought of exceeding their stations. How is any of this not the sage’s great constant order? Fittingly, throughout the realm under his transforming influence [?], all are stirred to joyful exertion and tremble in awe, feeling affection …

title: 嘉靖二十二年江西鄉試錄
text:
而知所尊尊而知所親無偏無黨可以追
唐虞超三代垂之萬世而無敝矣但恐承
平日久奉行于下者眞實之意或有少衰
昔荀悅有核眞之說司馬光有務實之規
此固已試之徵也雖然宋儒謂仁義人主
之術有天德便可以語王道其要只在謹
獨則知愼獨又爲人君天德之本斯有君
有臣而政不患其不舉也故曰君道得而
萬化行相道得而萬國理此杞人之過計
===
未知可進於
廟堂否也
第三問
況叔祺
同考試官教諭劉 批 〔遷固之辯考據博洽是〕
可以論史學矣
同考試官教諭陳 批 〔有識見有議論佳士也〕
考試官教授葉 批 〔精詳〕
考試官教授翟 批 〔博洽〕
punctuated:
而知所尊，尊而知所親，無偏無黨，可以追唐虞、超三代，垂之萬世而無敝矣。但恐承平日久，奉行于下者眞實之意或有少衰。昔荀悅有核眞之說，司馬光有務實之規，此固已試之徵也。雖然，宋儒謂仁義人主之術，有天德便可以語王道，其要只在謹獨。則知愼獨又爲人君天德之本，斯有君有臣，而政不患其不舉也。故曰：「君道得而萬化行，相道得而萬國理。」此杞人之過計，未知可進於廟堂否也。
第三問
況叔祺
同考試官教諭劉批〔遷固之辯，考據博洽，是〕可以論史學矣。
同考試官教諭陳批〔有識見，有議論，佳士也。〕
考試官教授葉批〔精詳。〕
考試官教授翟批〔博洽。〕
translation_en:
…and know whom to revere; revering, they know whom to hold dear. Without partiality or faction, this rule can rival the ages of Tang and Yu, surpass the Three Dynasties, and be handed down through ten thousand generations without deterioration. The only fear is that, after a long period of peace, the sincerity of those charged with carrying it out below may diminish somewhat. Formerly, Xun Yue advocated examining what is genuine, and Sima Guang enjoined attention to practical substance. These are indeed precedents already tested in practice. Nevertheless, the Song Confucians said that benevolence and righteousness are the ruler’s methods: with Heaven’s virtue, one may speak of the Kingly Way, whose essential point lies simply in vigilance when alone. Thus we know that vigilance when alone is also the foundation of the ruler’s Heavenly virtue. With ruler and ministers fulfilling their roles in this way, there need be no fear that government will fail to be carried out. Hence the saying: “When the Way of the ruler is fulfilled, all transformations proceed; when the Way of the chief minister is fulfilled, the myriad states are well governed.” These are the excessive anxieties of a man of Qi who fears the sky may fall; I do not know whether they may be presented at court.
Third Policy Question
Kuang Shuqi
Associate Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: “His discussion of Sima Qian and Ban Gu draws on extensive and thorough textual evidence. Such a man may indeed discuss historical scholarship.”
Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: “He has discernment and offers cogent arguments. A fine scholar.”
Examiner Ye, Professor, comments: “Precise and detailed.”
Examiner Zhai, Professor, comments: “Broadly learned and thorough.”

title: 嘉靖二十二年江西鄉試錄
text:
史何爲而作也史之作以明道也是故其
爲史也天下之理亂國家之盛衰君臣之
是非得失禮樂刑政之因革興廢燦然可
睹然皆天下之公議臣不得以私其君子
不得以私其父然後信其言而可傳於久
使千百世而下耿耿不磨取以爲法戒故
曰史之作以明道也執事以司馬遷班固
下問遷固之史非知道者然誦其言如出
乎其時要亦不可不謂非遷固之功也嘗
===
遡唐虞三代以前書詩春秋皆史也尚書
則紀傳之祖也大雅小雅則頌述之祖也
春秋編年通紀則紀事之祖也文中子曰
聖人述史三焉其述書也帝王之制備其
述詩也興衰之由顯其述春秋也邪正之
跡明此三者同出於史而不可雜也故史
與經其義一而已矣自漢以來司馬遷之
作史記班固之作漢書皆號稱良史之才
當其時博極羣書必曰劉向楊雄然稱遷
punctuated:
史何爲而作也？史之作，以明道也。是故其爲史也，天下之理亂，國家之盛衰，君臣之是非得失，禮樂刑政之因革興廢，燦然可睹。然皆天下之公議，臣不得以私其君，子不得以私其父，然後信其言而可傳於久，使千百世而下耿耿不磨，取以爲法戒。故曰：史之作，以明道也。
執事以司馬遷、班固下問。遷、固之史，非知道者，然誦其言，如出乎其時，要亦不可不謂非遷、固之功也。嘗遡唐虞三代以前，書、詩、春秋皆史也。尚書則紀傳之祖也，大雅、小雅則頌述之祖也，春秋編年通紀則紀事之祖也。文中子曰：「聖人述史三焉：其述書也，帝王之制備；其述詩也，興衰之由顯；其述春秋也，邪正之跡明。此三者同出於史，而不可雜也。」故史與經，其義一而已矣。
自漢以來，司馬遷之作史記，班固之作漢書，皆號稱良史之才。當其時，博極羣書，必曰劉向、楊雄，然稱遷
translation_en:
Why are histories written? Histories are written to illuminate the Way. Thus, in a history, order and disorder throughout the realm, the flourishing and decline of states, the rights and wrongs and successes and failures of rulers and ministers, and the continuities, changes, establishment, and abolition of rites, music, punishments, and government are all clearly visible. Yet these are all matters for the impartial judgment of the realm. A minister must not show partiality toward his ruler, nor a son toward his father. Only then can the historian’s words command trust and be transmitted far into the future, remaining vivid and undiminished for hundreds and thousands of generations, to serve as models and warnings. Hence I say: histories are written to illuminate the Way.
You, honored examiners, have condescended to ask about Sima Qian and Ban Gu. The histories of Qian and Gu are not the work of men who understood the Way. Yet reading their words aloud is like hearing voices from those very times. This, after all, must surely be credited to Qian and Gu [?; the transcription contains an apparently contradictory extra negative]. Tracing back to the time of Tang Yao and Yu Shun and the Three Dynasties and earlier, the Documents, the Odes, and the Spring and Autumn Annals were all histories. The Book of Documents was the ancestor of the annals-and-biographies form; the Greater Odes and Lesser Odes were the ancestors of eulogistic accounts; and the Spring and Autumn Annals, recording events continuously in chronological order, was the ancestor of historical narratives. Master Wenzhong said: “The Sage transmitted history in three forms. In his transmission of the Documents, the institutions of emperors and kings were fully set forth; in his transmission of the Odes, the causes of flourishing and decline were revealed; in his transmission of the Spring and Autumn Annals, the traces of wickedness and uprightness were made clear. These three all originated in history, yet must not be confused with one another.” Thus history and the Classics have but a single underlying meaning.
Since the Han, Sima Qian, who composed the Records of the Grand Historian, and Ban Gu, who composed the Book of Han, have both been acclaimed as men with the talent of fine historians. Among those of their time whose learning encompassed the full range of books, one must name Liu Xiang and Yang Xiong. Yet in praising Qian …

title: 嘉靖二十二年江西鄉試錄
text:
之序事辯而不華質而不俚其文直其事
核不虛美不隱悪瞱之序也亦稱固之序
事不激詭不抑抗贍而不穢詳而有體信
非良史之才不能也然固之譏遷曰是非
頗謬於聖人論大道則先黄老而後六經
序遊俠則退處士而進姦雄述貨殖則崇
貨利而羞貧賤今讀遷史謂黄老之旨約
事簡謂六經之寡要少功謂原憲之蓬戶
褐衣謂奸雄之言必信行必果謂本富為
===
上末富次之無巖穴奇士之行好語仁義
而長貧賤則固之譏遷者信矣至於瞱之
譏固則曰排死節否正直而不取殺身成
仁之美輕仁義而賤守節今讀固書於王
章之死而以自蹈刑戮非之於京房棄市
而以不容失身罪之於何武而有一革障
江河之譏於諸葛豐而有狂督之誚於紀
信而不傳其忠於孔休而不明其節則瞱
之譏固者又信矣然固譏遷失而固亦未
punctuated: 之序事，辯而不華，質而不俚，其文直，其事核，不虛美，不隱悪。瞱之序也，亦稱固之序事，不激詭，不抑抗，贍而不穢，詳而有體，信非良史之才不能也。然固之譏遷曰：「是非頗謬於聖人，論大道則先黄老而後六經，序遊俠則退處士而進姦雄，述貨殖則崇貨利而羞貧賤。」今讀遷史，謂黄老之旨約事簡，謂六經之寡要少功，謂原憲之蓬戶褐衣，謂奸雄之言必信、行必果，謂本富為上、末富次之，無巖穴奇士之行，好語仁義而長貧賤，則固之譏遷者信矣。至於瞱之譏固，則曰：「排死節，否正直，而不取殺身成仁之美，輕仁義而賤守節。」今讀固書，於王章之死，而以自蹈刑戮非之；於京房棄市，而以不容失身罪之；於何武，而有一革障江河之譏；於諸葛豐，而有狂督之誚；於紀信，而不傳其忠；於孔休，而不明其節，則瞱之譏固者又信矣。然固譏遷失，而固亦未
translation_en:
…his narration of events is eloquent without being ornate, plain without being vulgar; his writing is straightforward and his facts verified, neither bestowing unfounded praise nor concealing wrongdoing. The preface by Ye 瞱 [?] likewise praises Ban Gu’s narration of events as neither sensational nor strange, neither unduly depreciatory nor exaggerated, ample without being cluttered, and detailed yet properly organized. Truly, none but a talented historian could accomplish this. Yet Gu criticizes Sima Qian, saying: “His judgments of right and wrong diverge considerably from those of the sages. In discussing the Great Way, he places Huang-Lao teachings before the Six Classics; in recounting the lives of wandering knights, he demotes scholars living in retirement and promotes unscrupulous men of power; in describing the acquisition of wealth, he exalts material profit and treats poverty and low status as shameful.” Now, reading Qian’s history, we find him saying that Huang-Lao teachings are concise in their essentials and simple in their application; that the Six Classics offer few essentials and little practical benefit; that Yuan Xian had a brushwood door and wore coarse clothing; that unscrupulous men of power invariably kept their word and carried their actions through; and that wealth derived from primary occupations ranks highest, while wealth derived from secondary occupations comes next, whereas those who lack the conduct of exceptional recluses dwelling among cliffs and caves delight in speaking of benevolence and righteousness yet remain perpetually poor and lowly. Thus Gu’s criticism of Qian is indeed justified.

As for Ye’s criticism of Gu, he says: “He disparages those who die for their principles, condemns the upright, and fails to appreciate the excellence of sacrificing one’s life to fulfill benevolence. He makes light of benevolence and righteousness and demeans fidelity to principle.” Now, reading Gu’s book, we find that, concerning Wang Zhang’s death, he censures him for bringing execution upon himself; concerning Jing Fang’s execution in the marketplace, he blames him for failing to gain acceptance and bringing about his own destruction. He mocks He Wu for attempting to block the rivers with a single piece of leather [?], and reproaches Zhuge Feng for frenzied supervision [?]. He does not transmit Ji Xin’s loyalty or make clear Kong Xiu’s integrity. Thus Ye’s criticism of Gu is also justified. Yet although Gu criticizes Qian’s errors, Gu himself has not yet…

title: 嘉靖二十二年江西鄉試錄
text:
爲得睥議固失而睥益甚焉嗟乎此史之
難也以至於宋蘇子由議遷之淺近踈畧
刪遷史之舊而又增三皇而別孔氏謂之
古史劉知幾取前代諸史之得失而評議
之力攻其短謂之史通今觀子由古史其
叙帝王爲善爲不善之類朱子稱其言近
道非近世儒者所能及然顧其本末有大
不相應者其曰帝王之道以無爲宗萬物
莫能攖之此特以老子浮屠之意論聖人
===
