非能知聖人者也若論禹益避位之事類
皆以世俗不誠之心度聖賢則其失甚矣
知幾之作史通謂項羽不當曰紀謂陳勝
不當曰世家至論五行則專攻班氏之短
至有錯謬失宜乖理不辯之語徐堅深重
其書謂居史職者宜置座右唐玄宗亦讀
而善之信不誣也然疑古惑經之作雖堯
舜伯禹不免見疑夫子春秋不免見貶至
其所自作則因唐舊史之文猥陋不綱至
punctuated:
爲得，睥議固失，而睥益甚焉。嗟乎！此史之難也。以至於宋蘇子由議遷之淺近踈畧，刪遷史之舊，而又增三皇而別孔氏，謂之《古史》。劉知幾取前代諸史之得失而評議之，力攻其短，謂之《史通》。今觀子由《古史》，其叙帝王爲善爲不善之類，朱子稱其言近道，非近世儒者所能及。然顧其本末，有大不相應者。其曰：「帝王之道，以無爲宗，萬物莫能攖之。」此特以老子、浮屠之意論聖人，非能知聖人者也。若論禹、益避位之事，類皆以世俗不誠之心度聖賢，則其失甚矣。
知幾之作《史通》，謂項羽不當曰紀，謂陳勝不當曰世家。至論五行，則專攻班氏之短，至有錯謬失宜、乖理不辯之語。徐堅深重其書，謂居史職者宜置座右。唐玄宗亦讀而善之，信不誣也。然疑古惑經之作，雖堯、舜、伯禹不免見疑，夫子《春秋》不免見貶。至其所自作，則因唐舊史之文，猥陋不綱，至
translation_en:
…was not correct either. Pi [?] criticized Ban Gu’s errors, yet Pi’s own were still worse. Alas! Such is the difficulty of writing history. Later, in the Song dynasty, Su Ziyou criticized Sima Qian for being superficial and cursory. He abridged Qian’s original history, added the Three Sovereigns, and treated Confucius separately, calling his work Ancient History (Gushi). Liu Zhiji assessed the merits and faults of the histories of earlier dynasties and vigorously attacked their shortcomings, calling his work Comprehensive Study of Historiography (Shitong). Looking now at Ziyou’s Ancient History, we find that Master Zhu praised its accounts of rulers’ good and bad conduct as approaching the Way in their pronouncements, beyond the reach of recent Confucian scholars. Yet its fundamental principles and their application are greatly at odds. It says: “The Way of emperors and kings takes nonaction as its guiding principle; none of the myriad things can disturb it.” This merely discusses the sages through the ideas of Laozi and Buddhism; it does not show an understanding of the sages. When discussing such matters as Yu and Yi withdrawing from the throne, he generally measures sages and worthies by the insincere dispositions of ordinary people. His errors here are grave indeed.
In writing Comprehensive Study of Historiography, Zhiji argued that the account of Xiang Yu should not be designated “Basic Annals,” nor that of Chen Sheng “Hereditary House.” When discussing the Five Phases, he concentrated exclusively on attacking Ban Gu’s shortcomings, even using such expressions as “erroneous and inappropriate” and “contrary to principle and lacking discrimination.” Xu Jian held the book in great esteem, saying that those serving as historiographers should keep it beside their seats. Emperor Xuanzong of Tang also read and approved of it: this is indeed no false report. Yet in his writings questioning antiquity and casting doubt on the Classics, even Yao, Shun, and the great Yu were not spared suspicion, nor was the Master’s Spring and Autumn Annals spared disparagement. As for his own historical writing, he followed the text of the old Tang histories; it was crude and ill-organized, even to the point of…

title: 嘉靖二十二年江西鄉試錄
text:
瑣瑣於氏族方物之志宋子京謂工於譏
人而拙於用己者也故論漢以前良史之
才莫過於遷固後之議史者惟古史史通
二書爲近理其亦遷固之藥石然皆非遷
固之儔也倪思又著爲班馬異同之辯以
班史仍史記之舊又多刪改務趨簡嚴至
有刪而遺其事實改而失其本意者蓋又
止於文而已耳固非所以論遷固也故嘗
謂遷之奇偉固之縝密若不可置優劣於
===
其閒譬之創業守成自有難易遷史之創
業者也固史之守成者也其遷固之辯乎
至於遷之不能以知免極刑固之陷於大
戮明哲保身之道均之未聞也吾又安取
焉甚矣史之難也昔袁氏有曰史之爲難
有五煩而不整一難也俗而不典二難也
書不實錄三難也賞罰不中四難也文不
勝質五難也愚則曰不然非史之難也知
道之難也夫道明則意見定而持論正其
punctuated: 瑣瑣於氏族方物之志。宋子京謂工於譏人而拙於用己者也。故論漢以前良史之才，莫過於遷固；後之議史者，惟《古史》《史通》二書爲近理，其亦遷固之藥石，然皆非遷固之儔也。倪思又著爲班馬異同之辯，以班史仍《史記》之舊，又多刪改，務趨簡嚴，至有刪而遺其事實、改而失其本意者，蓋又止於文而已耳，固非所以論遷固也。故嘗謂遷之奇偉，固之縝密，若不可置優劣於其閒。譬之創業守成，自有難易：遷，史之創業者也；固，史之守成者也。其遷固之辯乎？至於遷之不能以知免極刑，固之陷於大戮，明哲保身之道，均之未聞也，吾又安取焉？甚矣，史之難也！昔袁氏有曰：「史之爲難有五：煩而不整，一難也；俗而不典，二難也；書不實錄，三難也；賞罰不中，四難也；文不勝質，五難也。」愚則曰：「不然，非史之難也，知道之難也。」夫道明則意見定而持論正，其
translation_en: …dwelling on petty details in treatises on clans and local products. Song Zijing described him as adept at criticizing others but clumsy in putting his own abilities to use. Thus, among the talents of accomplished historians of the Han and earlier periods, none surpassed Sima Qian and Ban Gu. Of later works discussing history, only the Ancient History (Gu shi) and Generalities on History (Shi tong) approach sound principles. They serve as corrective medicine for Qian and Gu, yet their authors are no peers of either man. Ni Si also wrote a discussion of the similarities and differences between Ban Gu and Sima Qian, observing that Ban’s history followed the existing Records of the Grand Historian but made numerous deletions and revisions in pursuit of concision and rigor, sometimes deleting factual details or revising away the original meaning. Yet this, too, concerns literary expression alone; it is certainly no basis for judging Qian and Gu. Thus I have often said that Qian’s extraordinary grandeur and Gu’s meticulous care seem to preclude ranking one above the other. If we compare them to founding an enterprise and preserving its achievements, however, there is naturally a difference in difficulty: Qian founded the enterprise of history; Gu preserved its achievements. Might this distinguish Qian from Gu? As for Qian’s failure to use his wisdom to escape the severest punishment, and Gu’s falling victim to a violent death, neither seems to have understood the way of preserving oneself through clear-sighted wisdom. What, then, should I take from them? How difficult the writing of history is! A certain Yuan once said: “There are five difficulties in writing history: being prolix and disorganized is the first; being vulgar rather than classically refined is the second; failing to record events truthfully is the third; assigning rewards and punishments inappropriately is the fourth; and having literary expression unequal to the substance is the fifth.” I, in my ignorance, say: “Not so. The difficulty lies not in writing history, but in understanding the Way.” For when the Way is clear, one’s views are settled and one’s judgments correct; one’s…

title: 嘉靖二十二年江西鄉試錄
text:
言足以信今而傳後雖以俟之萬世可也
其何五難之云邪是故春秋者經中之史
綱目者史中之經此萬世是非之權衡古
今史學之龜鑑而又何取於遷固乎
第四問
吳桂芳
同考試官教諭梁　批〔謚法書法聖王馭世之大權此作獨能發明其藴雖使古人復生亦當不能辯析之矣讀之凜然〕
===
同考試官教諭李　批〔古雅雄渾眞爲有見之言知子他日必能完名矣敬服〕
同考試官教諭金　批〔古人兢兢業業作德日休以下不敢縱肆所恃者此耳不可不爲之防也是作得之〕
考試官教授葉　批〔明贍〕
考試官教授翟　批〔典則〕
天下有公道有公法道也者本人心之是
非不可得而易焉者也法也者立萬世之
權衡不可得而私焉者也道以維持其法
punctuated:
言足以信今而傳後，雖以俟之萬世可也。其何五難之云邪？是故《春秋》者，經中之史；《綱目》者，史中之經。此萬世是非之權衡，古今史學之龜鑑，而又何取於遷、固乎？

第四問
吳桂芳
同考試官教諭梁　批〔謚法、書法，聖王馭世之大權。此作獨能發明其藴，雖使古人復生，亦當不能辯析之矣。讀之凜然。〕
同考試官教諭李　批〔古雅雄渾，眞爲有見之言。知子他日必能完名矣，敬服。〕
同考試官教諭金　批〔古人兢兢業業，作德日休，以下不敢縱肆，所恃者此耳。不可不爲之防也，是作得之。〕
考試官教授葉　批〔明贍。〕
考試官教授翟　批〔典則。〕

天下有公道，有公法。道也者，本人心之是非，不可得而易焉者也；法也者，立萬世之權衡，不可得而私焉者也。道以維持其法
translation_en:
…his words suffice to command belief in the present and to be transmitted to posterity; they may even await judgment for ten thousand generations. Why, then, speak of these five difficulties? Thus the Spring and Autumn Annals is history within the classics, while the Outline and Details (Gangmu) is a classic within history. These are the scales of right and wrong for ten thousand generations, the models and mirrors of historical scholarship, ancient and modern. What further need, then, to draw upon Sima Qian and Ban Gu?

Fourth Policy Question
Wu Guifang

Comment by Associate Examiner Liang, Instructor: 〔The rules for conferring posthumous names and the conventions of historical writing are great instruments of authority through which sage kings govern the world. This essay alone succeeds in elucidating their underlying significance. Even were the ancients brought back to life, they could not, I think, analyze it further. Reading it inspires awe.〕

Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Instructor: 〔Classically elegant, powerful, and full-bodied: these are truly words of insight. I know that you will one day be able to preserve your reputation intact. I respectfully admire you.〕

Comment by Associate Examiner Jin, Instructor: 〔The ancients were vigilant and diligent, cultivating virtue and daily growing more admirable; those below did not dare indulge themselves without restraint [?]. This alone was what they relied upon. Such safeguards are indispensable, and this essay grasps the point.〕

Comment by Examiner Ye, Professor: 〔Lucid and ample.〕

Comment by Examiner Zhai, Professor: 〔Classical and exemplary.〕

Under Heaven there are impartial principles and impartial standards. Principles are rooted in the human heart’s sense of right and wrong and cannot be altered. Standards establish the scales of judgment for ten thousand generations and cannot be bent to private interests. Principles sustain those standards…

title: 嘉靖二十二年江西鄉試錄
text:
而法可久法以通變乎道而道可行古之
聖人所以綱維世道而砥礪士心者孰有
外於此者乎逮至三代而下君臣失綱務
爲一切苟簡之治而先王之典法湮鈌而
不講然其公道公法之在天下不可泯沒
至今猶爲可恃也又孰有要於謚法書法
者乎謚法孰始之記曰先王謚以尊名節
以一惠是謚法古未詳也而詳於周公謂
大戴禮所載是也書法孰始之記曰言則
===
左史書之動則右史書之是書法古亦未
嚴也而嚴於孔子謂假魯史以作春秋是
也然則周公以法行道而子孫百世不能
改孔子以道行法而亂臣賊子知所懼其
心一而已矣故曰勸得其道而天下樂爲
善懲得其道而天下懼爲惡又曰有德者
必褒而善自此可勸有罪者必貶而惡自
此可懲誠有見於道法之不相悖而不可
一日無者也周公孔子立百王不易之法
punctuated: 而法可久，法以通變乎道而道可行。古之聖人所以綱維世道而砥礪士心者，孰有外於此者乎？逮至三代而下，君臣失綱，務爲一切苟簡之治，而先王之典法湮鈌而不講。然其公道公法之在天下不可泯沒，至今猶爲可恃也，又孰有要於謚法書法者乎？謚法孰始之？記曰：「先王謚以尊名，節以一惠。」是謚法古未詳也，而詳於周公，謂《大戴禮》所載是也。書法孰始之？記曰：「言則左史書之，動則右史書之。」是書法古亦未嚴也，而嚴於孔子，謂假魯史以作《春秋》是也。然則周公以法行道，而子孫百世不能改；孔子以道行法，而亂臣賊子知所懼。其心一而已矣。故曰：「勸得其道，而天下樂爲善；懲得其道，而天下懼爲惡。」又曰：「有德者必褒，而善自此可勸；有罪者必貶，而惡自此可懲。」誠有見於道法之不相悖而不可一日無者也。周公孔子立百王不易之法
translation_en:
…and thereby the standards can endure; the standards give the Way practical expression through adaptation, so that the Way can be put into practice. Could any means by which the ancient sages upheld the moral order of the world and tempered the resolve of scholars have fallen outside this? After the Three Dynasties, rulers and ministers lost their guiding principles, pursuing expedient and perfunctory government in everything, while the statutes and standards of the former kings fell into obscurity and neglect. Yet the impartial Way and impartial standards existing in the world could not be effaced, and remain dependable even today. Among these, what could be more important than the rules for conferring posthumous names and the conventions of historical writing?

Who originated the rules for posthumous names? The Record of Rites says: “The former kings used posthumous names to honor names, summing up a life in a single distinguishing quality.” Thus these rules were not fully elaborated in antiquity; they became so under the Duke of Zhou—as recorded in the Elder Dai’s Record of Rites (Da Dai Li). Who originated the conventions of historical writing? The Record of Rites says: “Words were recorded by the Scribe of the Left; actions were recorded by the Scribe of the Right.” Thus these conventions, too, were not yet rigorous in antiquity; they became so under Confucius, who drew upon the historical records of Lu to compose the Spring and Autumn Annals.

The Duke of Zhou therefore used standards to put the Way into practice, and his descendants could not alter them for a hundred generations. Confucius used the Way to apply standards, and rebellious ministers and treacherous sons knew what to fear. Their intentions were one and the same. Hence it is said: “When encouragement follows the proper way, all under Heaven delight in doing good; when punishment follows the proper way, all under Heaven fear doing evil.” It is also said: “Those with virtue must receive praise, and thereby goodness can be encouraged; those with guilt must receive censure, and thereby evil can be chastened.” These words truly recognize that the Way and standards do not conflict, and that neither can be dispensed with for even a day. The Duke of Zhou and Confucius established standards that a hundred kings could not alter…

title: 嘉靖二十二年江西鄉試錄
text:
而使斯道乆而常存者又豈外於此哉三
代而下繼周公而作者有劉熙之書有來
奧之書有沈約之書有賀琛之書然而莫
詳於蘇洵繼孔子而作者有馬遷之書有
班固之書有子由之書有歐陽之書然而
莫嚴於綱目雖曰以人而傳亦以人而異
而卒以章章明顯不可掩覆此其徵效也
以書法言之楊雄漢臣也當其時以文學
顯未有如雄者乃甘心仕莽反爲美新符
===
命之作以誇耀之視之龔勝薛方其愧葢
多矣故綱目以死書之而又曰莽大夫葢
賊雄所以賊莽也雄自成帝時葢已爲郎
矣而顧又莽之仕哉荀彧亦漢臣也以操
之姦而爲之腹心間關許下出畫奇策固
非不知操者則成操之簒者彧也乃欲以
正論尼之九錫之日以自附於殺身之義
良亦可憫矣故綱目以自殺爲文而又繫
之官者葢曰操官之也彧之悔也葢晚矣
punctuated:
而使斯道乆而常存者，又豈外於此哉？三代而下，繼周公而作者，有劉熙之書，有來奧之書，有沈約之書，有賀琛之書，然而莫詳於蘇洵；繼孔子而作者，有馬遷之書，有班固之書，有子由之書，有歐陽之書，然而莫嚴於綱目。雖曰以人而傳，亦以人而異，而卒以章章明顯，不可掩覆，此其徵效也。
以書法言之，楊雄，漢臣也。當其時，以文學顯，未有如雄者，乃甘心仕莽，反爲美新符命之作以誇耀之。視之龔勝、薛方，其愧葢多矣。故綱目以死書之，而又曰莽大夫，葢賊雄所以賊莽也。雄自成帝時葢已爲郎矣，而顧又莽之仕哉？荀彧亦漢臣也，以操之姦，而爲之腹心，間關許下，出畫奇策，固非不知操者，則成操之簒者彧也。乃欲以正論尼之九錫之日，以自附於殺身之義，良亦可憫矣。故綱目以自殺爲文，而又繫之官者，葢曰操官之也。彧之悔也，葢晚矣。
translation_en:
…and in enabling this Way to endure and remain forever, how could they have gone beyond this? After the Three Dynasties, among those who continued the work of the Duke of Zhou were Liu Xi, Lai Ao [?], Shen Yue, and He Chen, each with his writings; yet none was more comprehensive than Su Xun. Among those who continued the work of Confucius were Ma Qian [Sima Qian], Ban Gu, Ziyou [Su Zhe], and Ouyang [Ouyang Xiu], each with his writings; yet none was more rigorous than the Outline and Details (Gangmu). Although these principles are transmitted through individuals and also vary according to the individual, in the end they become unmistakably manifest and cannot be concealed. This is evidence of their efficacy.
To speak of historical wording: Yang Xiong was a subject of the Han. In his day, no one surpassed him in literary renown, yet he willingly served Wang Mang and even composed works praising the Xin dynasty and its auspicious signs of Heaven’s mandate, thereby glorifying it. Compared with Gong Sheng and Xue Fang, he surely had much to be ashamed of. Thus the Outline and Details records his demise simply as “died,” and further calls him “Wang Mang’s Grand Master.” Condemning Yang Xiong was a means of condemning Wang Mang. Yang Xiong had already been a Gentleman of the Palace since Emperor Cheng’s reign; how could he then have entered Wang Mang’s service?
Xun Yu too was a subject of the Han. Despite Cao Cao’s treachery, he became his trusted confidant, laboring amid difficulties at Xu and devising extraordinary strategies. He certainly was not someone who failed to understand Cao Cao; thus it was Xun Yu who brought Cao Cao’s usurpation to fruition. Yet, when the conferral of the Nine Bestowments was at hand, he sought to obstruct it with principled arguments, hoping thereby to associate himself with the righteousness of sacrificing one’s life. He was indeed pitiable. Thus the Outline and Details uses the wording “killed himself” and also appends his official title, meaning that it was Cao Cao who had appointed him. Xun Yu’s repentance came too late.

title: 嘉靖二十二年江西鄉試錄
text:
若雄者失身於其終而或者又失身於其
始君子不可不慎也陶潛博學不羣其令
彭澤也賦歸去來之辭而不爲折腰之辱
其高潔可知也然自以爲大尉侃之孫耻
屈身於劉宋至於書甲子以終其身嗟乎
晉亡矣而潛心乎晉故綱目以晉徵士書
之予其節也狄仁傑面折廷諍雖仕於周
而其母子姑姪孰親之譬足以感悟其心
其剛正可知也蒙耻奮忠卒取日於虞淵
===
嗟乎唐已周矣而仁傑又反而唐也故綱
目先書周以示臣法而卒繫之唐予其忠
也若潛之始終爲晉仁傑之始終爲唐是
以君子交予之也此非春秋之義乎蘇轍
所謂域中有三大而史之權與天與君竝
者此也以謚法言之張良志本爲韓乃委
身於高祖運籌畫策輔成漢業是以有四
百年之安謂其有儒者氣象是矣謚以文
成其誰曰不可然而黄石之恠君子或譏
punctuated:
若雄者，失身於其終，而或者又失身於其始，君子不可不慎也。陶潛博學不羣，其令彭澤也，賦《歸去來》之辭，而不爲折腰之辱，其高潔可知也。然自以爲大尉侃之孫，耻屈身於劉宋，至於書甲子以終其身。嗟乎！晉亡矣，而潛心乎晉，故《綱目》以晉徵士書之，予其節也。狄仁傑面折廷諍，雖仕於周，而其母子姑姪孰親之譬，足以感悟其心，其剛正可知也。蒙耻奮忠，卒取日於虞淵。嗟乎！唐已周矣，而仁傑又反而唐也，故《綱目》先書周以示臣法，而卒繫之唐，予其忠也。若潛之始終爲晉，仁傑之始終爲唐，是以君子交予之也。此非《春秋》之義乎？蘇轍所謂域中有三大，而史之權與天與君竝者，此也。
以謚法言之，張良志本爲韓，乃委身於高祖，運籌畫策，輔成漢業，是以有四百年之安。謂其有儒者氣象，是矣；謚以文成，其誰曰不可？然而黄石之恠，君子或譏
translation_en:
As for Yang Xiong, he compromised his integrity at the end, while another did so at the beginning. A gentleman cannot be too careful. Tao Qian was widely learned and stood apart from others. While serving as Magistrate of Pengze, he composed his “Return Home!” and refused the humiliation of bowing at the waist. His lofty purity is evident from this. Yet, regarding himself as the grandson of the Grand Commandant Tao Kan, he was ashamed to bend in service to the Liu Song dynasty, and thus dated his writings by the sexagenary cycle for the rest of his life. Alas! Jin had fallen, but Qian remained devoted to Jin. Hence the Outline and Details records him as a “summoned scholar of Jin,” commending his integrity. Di Renjie confronted the ruler directly and remonstrated at court. Although he served Zhou, his comparison asking which bond was closer—that between mother and son or that between aunt and nephew—was sufficient to move and awaken her heart. His firmness and uprightness are evident from this. Bearing disgrace and exerting himself in loyalty, he finally retrieved the sun from Yu Yuan, the abyss of sunset. Alas! Tang had already become Zhou, yet Renjie turned it back into Tang. Thus the Outline and Details first records Zhou to make clear the standard for a minister, but ultimately associates him with Tang, commending his loyalty. Qian belonged to Jin from beginning to end, and Renjie belonged to Tang from beginning to end: for this reason, gentlemen commend them both. Is this not the moral principle of the Spring and Autumn Annals? This is what Su Zhe meant when he said that there are three great powers within the realm, and that the authority of history stands alongside Heaven and the ruler.
To speak in terms of the rules for posthumous titles, Zhang Liang’s original purpose was to serve Han 韓; yet he committed himself to Gaozu, devising strategies and plans and helping establish the imperial enterprise of Han 漢, thereby bringing about four hundred years of peace. It is right to say that he possessed the bearing of a Confucian scholar. Who could object to granting him the posthumous title Wencheng, “Cultured and Accomplished”? Yet the strange affair of Huangshi is something that gentlemen sometimes criticize …

title: 嘉靖二十二年江西鄉試錄
text:
焉魏徵性本鯁直幸致身於太宗正色立
朝恥君不及堯舜是以有貞觀之盛謂其
直臣是矣謚以文貞以事太宗而言也忘
君事讎君子終恥焉就二子而言之子房
之功業元證之直言亦古人所難也賈充
蚤侯父爵不可謂不榮也主成濟之虐悖
以成司馬之篡處非其據徒有諂媚之容
蓋篡弒之賊也内外從亂曰荒君子猶不
能免於誅也而乃更之何哉許敬宗幼以
===
文名召用是亦可謂遭際矣揣高宗之昏
懦以助武昭儀之立謀殺忠良卒成唐室
之禍蓋姦佞之雄也名與實爽曰繆君子
猶以為未盡也而亦更之又何邪就二子
而論之不更未足以誅惡更之亦反以彌
彰蓋後世不可掩也此非周公之法乎王
福疇所謂得失一朝榮辱千載者此也嗚
呼書法謚法之難又有不可得而輕重者
矣雖然謚法賜於君上太常得以定之而
punctuated: 焉。魏徵性本鯁直，幸致身於太宗，正色立朝，恥君不及堯舜，是以有貞觀之盛。謂其直臣，是矣；謚以文貞，以事太宗而言也。忘君事讎，君子終恥焉。就二子而言之，子房之功業、元證之直言，亦古人所難也。賈充蚤侯父爵，不可謂不榮也。主成濟之虐悖，以成司馬之篡，處非其據，徒有諂媚之容，蓋篡弒之賊也。「内外從亂曰荒」，君子猶不能免於誅也，而乃更之，何哉？許敬宗幼以文名召用，是亦可謂遭際矣。揣高宗之昏懦，以助武昭儀之立，謀殺忠良，卒成唐室之禍，蓋姦佞之雄也。「名與實爽曰繆」，君子猶以為未盡也，而亦更之，又何邪？就二子而論之，不更未足以誅惡，更之亦反以彌彰，蓋後世不可掩也。此非周公之法乎？王福疇所謂「得失一朝，榮辱千載」者，此也。嗚呼！書法、謚法之難，又有不可得而輕重者矣。雖然，謚法賜於君上，太常得以定之，而
translation_en:
…for this. Wei Zheng was by nature unbending and outspoken. Fortunately gaining a position under Taizong, he stood at court with stern integrity, ashamed that his ruler should fall short of Yao and Shun. Thus came the flourishing age of Zhenguan. To call him an upright minister is correct; to give him the posthumous title Wenzhen, “Cultured and Upright,” is to judge him by his service to Taizong. Yet forgetting one’s ruler and serving his enemy is something a gentleman will always regard as shameful. Considering these two men, the achievements of Zifang and the forthright speech of Yuanzheng [?; apparently referring to Wei Zheng] were accomplishments difficult even for the ancients to attain.

Jia Chong early became a marquis through his father’s title; this certainly constituted honor. He directed Cheng Ji’s cruel and rebellious act, thereby bringing about the Sima clan’s usurpation. Occupying a position to which he had no right, he displayed nothing but servile flattery: he was indeed a villain guilty of usurpation and regicide. “One who follows disorder both within and without is called Huang”—“Disorderly.” Even this, in the judgment of gentlemen, could not spare him condemnation. Why, then, was the title changed? Xu Jingzong was summoned to office on the strength of his literary reputation in youth; this too may be called a fortunate opportunity. Calculating upon Gaozong’s benightedness and weakness, he helped bring about the elevation of Wu, Lady of Bright Deportment, and plotted the deaths of loyal and worthy men, ultimately bringing calamity upon the Tang ruling house. He was indeed an archvillain of treachery and flattery. “One whose reputation diverges from reality is called Miu”—“False.” Gentlemen still considered this insufficient to express his wickedness. Why, then, was this title changed as well? Considering these two men, even leaving their titles unchanged would not have sufficed to condemn their wickedness; changing them instead made it all the more conspicuous. The truth cannot be concealed from later generations. Is this not the method of the Duke of Zhou? This is what Wang Fuchou meant by “Success and failure belong to a single age; honor and disgrace endure for a thousand years.”

Alas! Such are the difficulties of historical judgment and the assignment of posthumous titles: here are matters whose weight cannot arbitrarily be increased or diminished. Nevertheless, posthumous titles are bestowed by the sovereign, and the Court of Imperial Sacrifices may determine them, but…

title: 嘉靖二十二年江西鄉試錄
text:
權不可不謹書法雖後世之草茅亦得奮
筆以俟而論不可不公權有弗謹則請乞
風行而稱謂無稽如獨孤及之議呂諲梁
肅之議楊綰可愧也論有弗公則實錄微
而紀事不足信欲如趙盾不能改董狐之
筆崔氏不能奪南史之簡不可得也然則
欲復周公之法明孔子之旨使公道常明
於天下者豈無其要哉亦惟慎博采之至
公明臣工之實行袪好惡之私絶毀譽之
===
原由蘇洵以師周公之意使公論明於朝
著而後謚法可信也致之以經史訪之於
衆議毋忌諱於簡牘毋出入於愛憎由朱
子以探孔子之旨使國是定於當時而後
書法有徵也如是則不必爵賞而人皆樂
爲善不必刑罰而人皆耻爲惡剛正之氣
可振而邪佞之風自息矣不然其能免於
踈濫之失乎此狂瞽之言也
第五問
punctuated:
權不可不謹。書法，雖後世之草茅亦得奮筆以俟，而論不可不公。權有弗謹，則請乞風行，而稱謂無稽，如獨孤及之議呂諲、梁肅之議楊綰，可愧也。論有弗公，則實錄微，而紀事不足信。欲如趙盾不能改董狐之筆、崔氏不能奪南史之簡，不可得也。然則欲復周公之法、明孔子之旨，使公道常明於天下者，豈無其要哉？亦惟慎博采之至公，明臣工之實行，袪好惡之私，絶毀譽之原，由蘇洵以師周公之意，使公論明於朝著，而後謚法可信也。致之以經史，訪之於衆議，毋忌諱於簡牘，毋出入於愛憎，由朱子以探孔子之旨，使國是定於當時，而後書法有徵也。如是，則不必爵賞而人皆樂爲善，不必刑罰而人皆耻爲惡，剛正之氣可振，而邪佞之風自息矣。不然，其能免於踈濫之失乎？此狂瞽之言也。

第五問
translation_en:
…this authority must be exercised with care. As for the principles of historical writing, even men outside official life in later ages may take up the brush and await judgment, but their assessments must be impartial. If authority is exercised without care, petitions and solicitations become widespread, and the designations bestowed lack any sound basis. Dugu Ji’s assessment of Lü Yin and Liang Su’s assessment of Yang Wan are shameful examples. If assessments are not impartial, truthful records decline, and accounts of events cannot be trusted. One could then no longer hope for cases like Zhao Dun’s inability to alter Dong Hu’s writing or the Cui clan’s inability to wrest away the Grand Historian of the South’s tablets.

Is there, then, no essential means of restoring the Duke of Zhou’s rules and elucidating Kongzi’s intent, so that impartial justice may always shine throughout the realm? One must carefully maintain the utmost impartiality in gathering testimony broadly, ascertain officials’ actual conduct, dispel the partiality of personal likes and dislikes, and cut off the sources of slander and flattery. By following Su Xun in taking the Duke of Zhou’s intent as a model, one can make impartial judgment manifest at court; only then can the rules for conferring posthumous names be trusted. Examine the matter through the classics and histories, and seek testimony in the judgments of the many. Let there be no concealment out of fear in written records, and no inclusion or exclusion prompted by affection or hatred. Follow Master Zhu in probing Kongzi’s intent, so that the accepted judgment of the state may be settled in its own time; only then will historical writing have a firm basis.

If this is done, people will all delight in doing good without needing ranks or rewards, and all will be ashamed to do evil without needing punishments. A spirit of firmness and uprightness can be revived, and the habits of wickedness and flattery will cease of themselves. Otherwise, how can one avoid the faults of carelessness and indiscriminate bestowal? These are the words of an ill-informed and presumptuous man.

Fifth Policy Question

title: 嘉靖二十二年江西鄉試錄
text:
胡杰
同考試官敎諭葉　批〔井田廢後世之法皆無可恃〕
者義
〔國家立法最善然法久敝生存乎其人耳此作責成處最爲得之故錄〕
同考試官敎諭廖　批〔明白詳盡時務策宜如此〕
同考試官學正黃　批〔責成守令更歸重於令甚〕
是
考試官敎授葉　批〔詳明而切實〕
考試官敎授翟　批〔救敝之道盡矣〕
===
夫賦稅之法與征輸之道此誠江西之民
憂而今時之急務也執事發策必欲操切
理要根極弊源嘉惠羣黎力追往哲此俊
傑之能辦而非樸樕之所明也雖然請毋
以空言相詡而以由衷自畢可乎先之以
作法之情次之以壞法之故求其影使之
因影以得形提其綱使之因綱以振目此
固承學區區之初而亦執事皇皇之臆也
蓋自井地之制大潰于秦均田之議不行
punctuated:
胡杰

同考試官敎諭葉　批〔井田廢，後世之法皆無可恃〕者義。〔國家立法最善，然法久敝生，存乎其人耳。此作責成處最爲得之，故錄。〕
同考試官敎諭廖　批〔明白詳盡，時務策宜如此。〕
同考試官學正黃　批〔責成守令，更歸重於令，甚〕是。
考試官敎授葉　批〔詳明而切實。〕
考試官敎授翟　批〔救敝之道盡矣。〕

夫賦稅之法與征輸之道，此誠江西之民憂，而今時之急務也。執事發策，必欲操切理要，根極弊源，嘉惠羣黎，力追往哲。此俊傑之能辦，而非樸樕之所明也。雖然，請毋以空言相詡，而以由衷自畢，可乎？先之以作法之情，次之以壞法之故，求其影，使之因影以得形；提其綱，使之因綱以振目。此固承學區區之初，而亦執事皇皇之臆也。蓋自井地之制大潰于秦，均田之議不行
translation_en:
Hu Jie

Associate Examiner Ye, Instructor, comments: “Since the well-field system was abolished, none of the methods of later ages can be relied upon.” The following words, zhe yi, are unclear [?]. “The state's laws are most excellent; yet as laws grow old, abuses arise. Everything depends upon the people who administer them. This essay is particularly sound in its discussion of assigning responsibility for results; hence its inclusion.”
Associate Examiner Liao, Instructor, comments: “Clear and thorough. Policy essays on current affairs should be like this.”
Associate Examiner Huang, School Instructor, comments: “It holds prefects and county magistrates responsible for results, placing still greater weight upon the magistrates. Quite right.”
Examiner Ye, Professor, comments: “Detailed, clear, and practical.”
Examiner Zhai, Professor, comments: “The means of remedying abuses are fully set forth.”

The laws governing taxation and the methods of collection and remittance are indeed a source of distress for the people of Jiangxi and an urgent concern of our time. In setting this policy question, you surely intend to grasp the essentials of the matter, probe the very roots of abuses, bestow benefits upon the common people, and strive to emulate the wise men of the past. This is something outstanding men can accomplish, beyond the understanding of someone of my humble abilities. Nevertheless, may I dispense with empty professions and instead set forth fully what lies in my heart? I shall begin with the intentions behind the establishment of the laws, then proceed to the causes of their deterioration: seeking their shadow, so that through it their form may be discerned; lifting the net's main cord, so that through it all the meshes may be spread out. This is indeed my modest original intention as a student, and also the concern that occupies your thoughts.

Now, ever since the well-field system utterly collapsed under the Qin, proposals for equalizing landholdings failed to be implemented…

title: 嘉靖二十二年江西鄉試錄
text:
於漢唐人口分世業之法最爲近古矣安
史之亂海內雲擾版圖隳於避地賦法壞
於奉軍取之無定則徵之無定時誠如昔
人所論者我
國家以墾田定賦矣在地曰夏稅稅有差在
田曰秋粮粮有則所謂定法也因時起徵
矣稅始五月訖于秋粮始十月訖于冬所
謂定時也夫上之則壞而緣時所以宜民
而示之仁也下之力本以供賦所以急君
===
而示之義也上下相維仁義交至承學所
謂先之以作法之情者此也然民漓則僞
起法久則弊生僞起則日滋弊生則日壞
故變亂日興逋負日廣誠如執事所云者
夫變亂之故六一曰奇分二曰灑派三曰
擴飛四曰倒失五曰詭寓六曰懸虛奇分
者析子戶而無籍名灑派者愚小民而無
定數擴飛者過都越里而莫原其從倒失
者遞推轉收而莫見其止詭寓者先則於
punctuated:
於漢。唐人口分世業之法，最爲近古矣。安史之亂，海內雲擾，版圖隳於避地，賦法壞於奉軍，取之無定則，徵之無定時，誠如昔人所論者。我國家以墾田定賦矣。在地曰夏稅，稅有差；在田曰秋粮，粮有則，所謂定法也。因時起徵矣，稅始五月，訖于秋；粮始十月，訖于冬，所謂定時也。夫上之則壞而緣時，所以宜民而示之仁也；下之力本以供賦，所以急君而示之義也。上下相維，仁義交至，承學所謂先之以作法之情者，此也。
然民漓則僞起，法久則弊生；僞起則日滋，弊生則日壞。故變亂日興，逋負日廣，誠如執事所云者。夫變亂之故六：一曰奇分，二曰灑派，三曰擴飛，四曰倒失，五曰詭寓，六曰懸虛。奇分者，析子戶而無籍名；灑派者，愚小民而無定數；擴飛者，過都越里而莫原其從；倒失者，遞推轉收而莫見其止；詭寓者，先則於
translation_en:
… under the Han. The Tang system of per capita allotments and hereditary holdings came closest to ancient practice. During the An Lushan and Shi Siming rebellion, turmoil swept the realm. Population registers and land records deteriorated as people fled, and the taxation system broke down under the demands of provisioning the armies. Exactions followed no fixed rules, and collections had no fixed times, just as earlier writers have discussed. Our dynasty has fixed taxes according to cultivated acreage. On land, the levy is called the summer tax, assessed at differing rates; on fields, it is called the autumn grain levy, assessed according to prescribed rules. This is what is meant by fixed regulations. Collection begins according to the season: the summer tax begins in the fifth month and ends in autumn; the grain levy begins in the tenth month and ends in winter. This is what is meant by fixed times. Those above let their rules deteriorate [?] yet accommodate the seasons, thereby meeting the people's needs and showing them benevolence. Those below devote their efforts to agriculture to supply the taxes, thereby attending to their ruler's urgent needs and showing righteousness. Above and below sustain one another, and benevolence and righteousness are reciprocally fulfilled. This is what I, a student, meant by first considering the intentions behind establishing the regulations.
Yet when the people lose their integrity, deception arises; when regulations have been in force for a long time, abuses develop. Once deception arises, it grows daily; once abuses develop, deterioration advances daily. Thus disorder increases by the day, and tax arrears grow ever larger, just as you have said. There are six causes of this disorder: first, irregular subdivision; second, scattered apportionment; third, far-flung transfers; fourth, shifting and loss; fifth, fraudulent lodging; and sixth, unsupported entries. Irregular subdivision means splitting off subsidiary households without registering their names. Scattered apportionment means deceiving ordinary people through assessments of no fixed amount. Far-flung transfers means passing liabilities across du and li administrative boundaries so that their origins cannot be traced. Shifting and loss means successively passing liabilities along and transferring collections, with no discernible endpoint. Fraudulent lodging means, first, in [?] …

title: 嘉靖二十二年江西鄉試錄
text:
絶貸栽數於流移托名於寄庄借頓於親
識附麗於權勢者是也懸虛者戶無考則
懸於戶爲戶虛里無考則懸於里爲里虛
都無考則懸於都爲都虛縣無考則懸於
縣爲縣虛者是也是六者里書之受賕而
豪強之爲害者也至於貧者挨目前則減
畆自困愚民貪小利則抱納不推久漸湮
迷遂成逃絶豈獨豪強之罪哉逋負之故
五一曰予數緩二曰端緒繁三曰大戶持
===
四曰駔儈行五曰役累重吏胥待賄而後
派故緩一糧十則以起徵故繁糧長圖覊
餘而大戶執本價故持孱弱者存畏難之
心壟斷者有泊制之術故駔儈行矣産廢
於賠虛而數不繼力分於借辦而用愈繁
故役累重矣此五者上下之因循而糧里
之交困者也至於積年敗役之營充貪官
汚吏之賄縱萬分僥倖一或蠲除豈獨侵
牟之罪哉承學所謂次之以壞法之故者
punctuated:
絶貸，栽數於流移，托名於寄庄，借頓於親識，附麗於權勢者是也。懸虛者，戶無考則懸於戶，爲戶虛；里無考則懸於里，爲里虛；都無考則懸於都，爲都虛；縣無考則懸於縣，爲縣虛者是也。是六者，里書之受賕而豪強之爲害者也。至於貧者挨目前，則減畆自困；愚民貪小利，則抱納不推。久漸湮迷，遂成逃絶，豈獨豪強之罪哉？
逋負之故五：一曰予數緩，二曰端緒繁，三曰大戶持，四曰駔儈行，五曰役累重。吏胥待賄而後派，故緩；一糧十則以起徵，故繁；糧長圖覊餘，而大戶執本價，故持；孱弱者存畏難之心，壟斷者有泊制之術，故駔儈行矣；産廢於賠虛而數不繼，力分於借辦而用愈繁，故役累重矣。此五者，上下之因循而糧里之交困者也。至於積年敗役之營充，貪官汚吏之賄縱，萬分僥倖，一或蠲除，豈獨侵牟之罪哉？承學所謂次之以壞法之故者
translation_en:
…extinct households [?], planting assessed amounts upon displaced persons, registering them under the names of outlying estates, lodging them with relatives and acquaintances, and attaching them to powerful patrons: these are the practices in question. As for fictitious outstanding assessments: when no household can be verified, an assessment is left outstanding against the household, creating a fictitious household liability; when no li can be verified, it is left against the li, creating a fictitious li liability; when no du can be verified, it is left against the du, creating a fictitious du liability; and when no county can be verified, it is left against the county, creating a fictitious county liability. These six practices arise from village clerks accepting bribes and powerful families doing harm. Yet poor people, struggling to get through the present, reduce their registered acreage and bring hardship upon themselves; ignorant people, coveting small gains, undertake tax payments without transferring the liability. Over time the records become obscured and confused, until the liabilities are assigned to absconded or extinct households. Can the blame lie solely with the powerful families?
There are five causes of arrears: first, delays in issuing assessment figures; second, excessive procedural complexity; third, obstruction by great households; fourth, the activities of brokers; and fifth, heavy service burdens. Clerks wait for bribes before apportioning liabilities, hence the delays. A single grain levy is collected under ten assessment rates, hence the complexity. Grain chiefs seek to retain surplus receipts [?], while great households insist on the original price, hence the obstruction. The weak are afraid of difficulties, while monopolists possess techniques of manipulation [?]; thus brokers flourish. Property is ruined by making good fictitious liabilities, so that the required amounts cannot be supplied; resources are divided by borrowing to meet obligations, while expenses grow ever more numerous. Thus service burdens become heavy. These five conditions arise from habitual negligence at both higher and lower levels, leaving grain chiefs and village service personnel alike in distress. Furthermore, men who have for years defaulted on service obligations maneuver to secure appointments [?], while corrupt officials and clerks accept bribes and let them act unchecked. They cling to the faint hope that some remission may eventually be granted. Can the fault be solely that of those who profiteer? What I, a student, meant by proceeding next to the causes of the law’s breakdown…

title: 嘉靖二十二年江西鄉試錄
text:
此也玆欲懸詭清而常賦不亂愚以爲丈
量之法可行也不可輕也歲造之法可舉
也不可據也天下之事無有盡利而無害
者計其分數則爲之故驗土膏均糧則使
貧富不至於甚偏清尺籍摘奸欺使繩墨
不至於大壞如此而已如欲盡利而無害
必復井田而後可而豈其時哉至欲逋侵
絕而常限不踰愚以爲遠年之逋可緩也
不可迫也近時之宄可懲也不可縱也蓋
===
天下之事未有盡法而無情者計其事勢
則爲之故任催年革端緒則事簡而民易
從治倉臯時派徵則法行而上可信如此
而已如欲盡法而無情必如桑孔而後可
而豈其道哉承學所謂求其影使之因影
以得形者凡此類也夫事至求影而不得
其形於乎執事之心亦困矣無已則愚請
以贅說更其端可乎故夫探本之論三一
曰議差役二曰議法令三曰議責成何謂
punctuated:
此也。玆欲懸詭清而常賦不亂，愚以爲丈量之法可行也，不可輕也；歲造之法可舉也，不可據也。天下之事，無有盡利而無害者，計其分數則爲之。故驗土膏，均糧則，使貧富不至於甚偏；清尺籍，摘奸欺，使繩墨不至於大壞。如此而已。如欲盡利而無害，必復井田而後可，而豈其時哉？至欲逋侵絕而常限不踰，愚以爲遠年之逋可緩也，不可迫也；近時之宄可懲也，不可縱也。蓋天下之事，未有盡法而無情者，計其事勢則爲之。故任催年，革端緒，則事簡而民易從；治倉臯，時派徵，則法行而上可信。如此而已。如欲盡法而無情，必如桑孔而後可，而豈其道哉？承學所謂求其影，使之因影以得形者，凡此類也。夫事至求影而不得其形，於乎，執事之心亦困矣！無已，則愚請以贅說更其端，可乎？

故夫探本之論三：一曰議差役，二曰議法令，三曰議責成。何謂
translation_en:
…This is what I mean. Now, if we wish to clear away fictitious registrations and fraudulent tax arrangements without disrupting regular taxation, I humbly believe that land measurement may be implemented, but must not be undertaken lightly; annual compilation of registers may be instituted, but cannot be relied upon. In the affairs of the world, nothing brings benefit alone without harm: one must weigh their relative proportions before acting. Thus, examine the fertility of the soil and equalize grain-tax rates, so that the burdens on rich and poor do not become excessively unequal; rectify the land registers and expose fraud, so that established standards do not fall into serious disorder. That is all. If we wished to secure every benefit without any harm, we would have to restore the well-field system before this could be achieved. But is this the time for it?

As for wishing to eliminate arrears and embezzlement and prevent the regular deadlines from being exceeded, I humbly believe that long-standing arrears may be given more time and must not be pressed for urgently; recent wrongdoing should be punished and must not be tolerated. For in the affairs of the world, one cannot apply the law to the utmost without regard for human circumstances: one must assess the situation before acting. Thus, entrust collection to the responsible annual personnel [?] and eliminate procedural complications, and affairs will be simplified and the people will readily comply; put the granaries in order [?] and apportion and collect taxes at the proper times, and the law will operate and those above can be trusted. That is all. If we wished to enforce the law to the utmost without regard for human circumstances, we would have to act like Sang and Kong before this could be achieved. But is that the proper way?

These are all instances of what I, a student, have called seeking the shadow so that, through the shadow, one may find the form. When affairs reach the point where one seeks the shadow but cannot find its form—alas, your mind, sir, must also be sorely troubled! If we must pursue the matter further, may I offer some additional remarks and approach it from another starting point?

There are three discussions that probe the root: first, a discussion of labor-service assignments; second, a discussion of laws and ordinances; and third, a discussion of holding officials responsible for results. What is meant by…

title: 嘉靖二十二年江西鄉試錄
text:
議差役夫爲弊者勢也非民之情也江西
之役稱最難者糧長也故凡樂爲糧長者
皆民之蠹也其次如聽解大戶驛傳頭戶
之類甚難也故凡樂爲是役者皆民之蠹
也斯役之來皆足以覆人故其爲弊之初
心以避役也非以避稅也及其久而不可
核則其流者也今擇糧長闗合而領批使
里長催徵而均解附帶幇補聽其自便而
官寔親焉不可乎大戶頭戶之類凡其役
===
之難者皆量其體裁而寬其分數不可乎
治民者每求民之所不便而推移之以服
其心以平其情吾知驅之爲弊不爲也何
謂議法令欺隱有没入之法抗違有遷徙
之法稽越有遍謫之法貪黷有大刑之法
令則上下狥姑息而法之不盡行者固多
矣是惟服民之心平民之情而後盡我之
法焉斯不怨故法令次之何謂議責成令
之居官視爲傳舍而不顧者非意也責成
punctuated:
議差役？夫爲弊者，勢也，非民之情也。江西之役稱最難者，糧長也。故凡樂爲糧長者，皆民之蠹也。其次，如聽解大戶、驛傳頭戶之類，甚難也。故凡樂爲是役者，皆民之蠹也。斯役之來，皆足以覆人，故其爲弊之初心，以避役也，非以避稅也。及其久而不可核，則其流者也。今擇糧長，闗合而領批，使里長催徵而均解，附帶幇補，聽其自便，而官寔親焉，不可乎？大戶、頭戶之類，凡其役之難者，皆量其體裁而寬其分數，不可乎？治民者，每求民之所不便而推移之，以服其心，以平其情，吾知驅之爲弊不爲也。
何謂議法令？欺隱有没入之法，抗違有遷徙之法，稽越有遍謫之法，貪黷有大刑之法。令則上下狥姑息，而法之不盡行者固多矣。是惟服民之心，平民之情，而後盡我之法焉，斯不怨。故法令次之。
何謂議責成？令之居官，視爲傳舍而不顧者，非意也，責成
translation_en:
…discussing service obligations? Abuses arise from the force of circumstances, not from the people's inherent disposition. Among service obligations in Jiangxi, that of grain chief is said to be the most onerous. Thus all who gladly serve as grain chiefs are parasites upon the people. Next come such extremely onerous duties as those of substantial households assigned to remittance service [?] and leading households responsible for the postal relay service. Thus all who gladly undertake these duties are likewise parasites upon the people. When these obligations fall upon someone, any of them can ruin him. Hence people's original intention in resorting to abuses is to evade service, not taxes. When these practices have persisted so long that they can no longer be investigated, that is a subsequent development.
Could we not now select grain chiefs, coordinate their assignments [?] and have them receive official certificates, and make the community heads press for collection and share the remittance duties equitably, allowing them to arrange supplementary assistance as convenient, while the officials themselves actually oversee the work? For substantial households, leading households, and the like, wherever their service is onerous, could we not assess the nature of their duties and reduce their allotted shares? Those who govern the people should always seek out what causes them hardship and make adjustments, thereby winning their allegiance and allaying their discontent. I know that then, even if driven to commit abuses, they would not do so.
What is meant by discussing laws and ordinances? For fraudulent concealment there is confiscation; for defiance and disobedience, compulsory relocation; for delays and transgressions, banishment [?]; and for corruption, severe punishment. Yet now [?], those above and below yield to expedient leniency, and instances in which the laws are not fully enforced are indeed numerous. Only after winning the people's allegiance and allaying their discontent should we enforce our laws in full; then they will feel no resentment. Thus laws and ordinances come second.
What is meant by discussing accountability for results? When magistrates regard their offices as temporary lodgings and neglect their duties, this is not their intention; the means of holding them accountable…

title: 嘉靖二十二年江西鄉試錄
text:
之術不專且不至也然其急者在守令而
令之視守尤切爲何則其地近其分親也
地近則易知分親則易治故爲令者苟加
志於民何民弗濟苟存心於事何事弗成
自定賦言之由戶總以核里總里總核都
總都總核縣總而縣之實徵可知矣由縣
虛以求都虛都虛求里虛里虛求戶虛而
縣之虛數可知矣自起徵言之給戶由立
約劑凡折直皆入於官帑而不入於糧里
===
之手則輸直者無負矣脩倉庾信期會凡
本粟皆入於官廥而不入於駔儈之手則
輸粟者無負矣近固有行之而甚效者在
賢令一加之意耳愚請著爲甲凡縣令之
至者毋束以期會薄書之煩而以清糧專
責之計其縣虛三分之以弊吏治每歲縣
登其清出之數以上之府府有要府以上
之司司有成司以上之撫按撫按有會會
則計其清出之通以下上其考大要察其
punctuated:
之術不專且不至也。然其急者在守令，而令之視守尤切。爲何？則其地近，其分親也。地近則易知，分親則易治。故爲令者，苟加志於民，何民弗濟？苟存心於事，何事弗成？自定賦言之，由戶總以核里總，里總核都總，都總核縣總，而縣之實徵可知矣。由縣虛以求都虛，都虛求里虛，里虛求戶虛，而縣之虛數可知矣。自起徵言之，給戶由，立約劑，凡折直皆入於官帑，而不入於糧里之手，則輸直者無負矣。脩倉庾，信期會，凡本粟皆入於官廥，而不入於駔儈之手，則輸粟者無負矣。近固有行之而甚效者，在賢令一加之意耳。
愚請著爲甲，凡縣令之至者，毋束以期會薄書之煩，而以清糧專責之。計其縣虛，三分之，以弊吏治。每歲縣登其清出之數，以上之府，府有要；府以上之司，司有成；司以上之撫按，撫按有會。會則計其清出之通，以下上其考。大要察其
translation_en:
…the methods of holding officials accountable for results are neither sufficiently focused nor thoroughly applied. Yet the most urgent responsibility rests with prefects and county magistrates, and it bears still more directly upon magistrates than upon prefects. Why? Because their jurisdictions are close at hand and their duties bring them into intimate contact with the people. Proximity makes conditions easier to understand; close involvement makes government easier to administer. Thus, if a magistrate devotes his attention to the people, whom can he not aid? If he puts his mind to affairs, what can he not accomplish?
As for fixing tax assessments, use household totals to verify village totals, village totals to verify township totals, and township totals to verify county totals; the county’s actual collectible assessment can then be known. Work back from the county’s unsupported assessment to that of its townships, from the townships to the villages, and from the villages to the households; the amount of the county’s unsupported assessment can then be known. As for initiating collection, issue household tax notices and establish contractual documents. If all commuted payments enter the government treasury rather than passing into the hands of grain and village headmen, those paying in money will suffer no loss. Repair the granaries and keep faithfully to the appointed collection dates. If all grain paid in kind enters government storehouses rather than passing into brokers’ hands, those delivering grain will suffer no loss. Recently, indeed, some have implemented these measures with considerable success. It requires only that a worthy magistrate give the matter his attention.
I humbly propose that this be established as a regulation [?]. When county magistrates arrive at their posts, they should not be constrained by the burdens of deadlines and paperwork, but should be given specific responsibility for rectifying grain-tax accounts. Calculate each county’s unsupported assessment and divide it into three portions, using this to judge the officials’ administration [?]. Each year the county should record the amount it has cleared and submit it to the prefecture, where a summary is to be maintained. The prefecture should submit it to the provincial administration commission, where a consolidated account is to be maintained. The commission should submit it to the grand coordinator and regional inspector, who are to maintain an aggregate account. On compiling this account, they should calculate the total amount cleared and accordingly lower or raise the magistrate’s performance rating. The essential point is to scrutinize his…

title: 嘉靖二十二年江西鄉試錄
text:
歆法者先去之而半登者爲稱格至於一
歲起徵之數雖升斗不盡亦懲焉積之以
三年之通而縣虛絶歲輸無奇者聽其代
否則叙誥之此則地官蓋嘗一行而遽輟
者夫使上之人內則堅執競之心外則嚴
淑慝之令吾知數年之間必有可觀者出
焉而丈量歲造之法或不戒而畢行矣承
學所謂操其綱使之循綱以振目者此類
也故夫緣情以作法法勝則傷仁立法以
===
制情情勝則害義由仁義以立政則政行
矣酌情法以宜民則民化矣此固草茅之
所談也若夫宗本前哲之規模叅考歷代
之利害如陸贄所稱放名田而少爲之限
不驚民不動衆不用井田之制而獲井田
之利如蘇軾所論此則執事之責也固非
承學所逮也幸與進而明敎之
punctuated: 歆法者，先去之，而半登者爲稱格。至於一歲起徵之數，雖升斗不盡，亦懲焉。積之以三年之通，而縣虛絶、歲輸無奇者，聽其代；否則叙誥之。此則地官蓋嘗一行而遽輟者。夫使上之人，內則堅執競之心，外則嚴淑慝之令，吾知數年之間必有可觀者出焉，而丈量歲造之法，或不戒而畢行矣。承學所謂操其綱，使之循綱以振目者，此類也。故夫緣情以作法，法勝則傷仁；立法以制情，情勝則害義。由仁義以立政，則政行矣；酌情法以宜民，則民化矣。此固草茅之所談也。若夫宗本前哲之規模，叅考歷代之利害，如陸贄所稱放名田而少爲之限，不驚民，不動衆，不用井田之制而獲井田之利，如蘇軾所論，此則執事之責也，固非承學所逮也。幸與進而明敎之。
translation_en:
…first remove those who abuse the law [?], and judge those who bring half the amount onto the registers to have met the standard. As for the amount assessed for collection in any one year, punish them if even a sheng or a dou remains uncollected. Reckon the cumulative total over three years: if the county’s fictitious assessments have been eliminated and its annual remittances leave no outstanding balance, permit its magistrate to be replaced; otherwise, subject him to graded admonition [?]. This is something that the fiscal authorities apparently once implemented but abruptly discontinued. If those above inwardly maintain a firm resolve to exert themselves and outwardly enforce strict orders distinguishing the good from the wicked, I know that within a few years results worth seeing will emerge. The procedures for surveying land and compiling annual registers might then all be carried out without further injunctions. This is the sort of thing that I, a student, mean by grasping the headrope of a net and making its meshes open by following that rope.

Thus, when laws are fashioned according to circumstances and human feelings, allowing law to prevail excessively injures benevolence; when laws are established to regulate human feelings, allowing those feelings to prevail excessively harms righteousness. Establish government through benevolence and righteousness, and its measures will take effect. Weigh human circumstances and law so as to suit the people, and the people will be transformed. These are, of course, matters that a man outside office may discuss. As for taking the models of earlier worthies as the foundation and examining the benefits and drawbacks of successive dynasties—for example, permitting private landholding while imposing modest limits upon it, as Lu Zhi advocated, and obtaining the benefits of the well-field system without alarming the people, mobilizing the populace, or employing that system itself, as Su Shi discussed—these are your responsibilities, gentlemen. They assuredly lie beyond the reach of a student such as myself. I hope you will allow me to advance and favor me with your illuminating instruction.

title: 嘉靖二十二年江西鄉試錄
text:
江西鄉試録後序
嘉靖癸卯江西鄉試録成教
授翟表序之備矣御史揖〔天〕
〔榮〕使申告曰
聖天子嗣大歷服惟今二十有二
載此邦蓋凡八賔興矣得人
之盛爲天下稱首豈直山川
===
産才之良實惟
文明弘賁覃布其耿光休烈以又
寧區宇多士用是遭際
昌期罔不含英茹華負鳴世之志
始〔天〕〔榮〕之入院校籌也觀於
初試見其根據經傳不鑿不
浮嘆曰懿哉斯其有得聖賢
punctuated:
江西鄉試録後序

嘉靖癸卯，江西鄉試録成，教授翟表序之備矣。御史揖〔天〕〔榮〕，使申告曰：「聖天子嗣大歷服，惟今二十有二載。此邦蓋凡八賔興矣，得人之盛，爲天下稱首。豈直山川産才之良？實惟文明弘賁，覃布其耿光休烈，以又寧區宇。多士用是遭際昌期，罔不含英茹華，負鳴世之志。始〔天〕〔榮〕之入院校籌也，觀於初試，見其根據經傳，不鑿不浮，嘆曰：『懿哉！斯其有得聖賢
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Jiangxi Provincial Examination

In the guimao year of Jiajing [1543], the Record of the Jiangxi Provincial Examination was completed. Prefectural School Instructor Zhai Biao had already provided a comprehensive preface. The Censor bowed to Tianrong and asked him to elaborate as follows:

“Our sagely Son of Heaven succeeded to the great imperial mandate twenty-two years ago. In that time, this province has held eight examinations to advance worthy men. Its abundant recruitment of talent is acclaimed as foremost in the realm. Could this be due solely to the excellence of the talent nurtured by its mountains and rivers? In truth, imperial cultural brilliance has splendidly adorned the land, spreading its radiant light and glorious achievements far and wide to aid in bringing peace to the realm. Thus the many scholars have encountered a flourishing age; all have absorbed the finest cultural nourishment and cherish the ambition to make their voices heard in the world.

“When I, Tianrong, first entered the examination compound to assess the scripts [?], I examined the work from the first session and found it grounded in the Classics and their commentaries, neither forced nor superficial. I exclaimed: ‘How admirable! Have they indeed gained an understanding of the sages and worthies …

title: 嘉靖二十二年江西鄉試錄
text:
之訓乎再試之見其雄深典
雅動閑矩度嘆曰富哉文乎
其兼尚世之體裁乎三試之
則見其鋪敘今古陳說世務
出入乎百家子史之言根極
理要愈叩之而愈不匱則又
嘆曰渢渢乎美矣至矣通儒
===
之義備矣豈三代之遺乎既
乃仰而思之則又作而嘆曰
夫文安從生哉言者心之聲
也文言之粹也聖人之道藴
之爲德行發之爲事業令多
士之文郁郁乎盛矣抑不知
其中所藴果皆光明俊偉以
punctuated:
之訓乎？」再試之，見其雄深典雅，動閑矩度，嘆曰：「富哉，文乎！其兼尚世之體裁乎？」三試之，則見其鋪敘今古，陳說世務，出入乎百家子史之言，根極理要，愈叩之而愈不匱，則又嘆曰：「渢渢乎！美矣，至矣！通儒之義備矣，豈三代之遺乎？」
既乃仰而思之，則又作而嘆曰：「夫文安從生哉？言者，心之聲也；文，言之粹也。聖人之道，藴之爲德行，發之爲事業。令多士之文郁郁乎盛矣，抑不知其中所藴，果皆光明俊偉，以
translation_en:
…the teachings of the sages and worthies?” At the second session, seeing that their writing was powerful, profound, classical, and elegant, and that it everywhere conformed to established standards, they exclaimed: “How rich this writing is! Does it also embrace the literary forms of earlier ages?” At the third session, they saw how the candidates expounded matters ancient and modern, discussed the affairs of the age, ranged through the writings of the various masters and historians, and traced principles to their essential foundations. The more deeply they probed, the more inexhaustible these writings proved. Then they exclaimed again: “How abundant! How beautiful, how consummate! The full significance of comprehensive classical learning is embodied here. Could this be a legacy of the Three Dynasties?”
Then, looking upward in reflection, they rose and sighed once more: “From where does writing arise? Speech is the voice of the heart; writing is the finest essence of speech. The Way of the sages, stored within, becomes virtuous conduct; expressed outwardly, it becomes achievement in affairs. Now [?] the writing of these many scholars flourishes in rich abundance. Yet we do not know whether what they harbor within is indeed all luminous, noble, and great, so that …

title: 嘉靖二十二年江西鄉試錄
text:
毋浮于爾言者乎夫主司校
閱惟其文焉爾其人固不可
得而知也
國家取士亦非徒以其藝焉爾
盖將欲得夫所謂賢人君子
登進勵翼輔理承化以共成
正大光明之治爾多士榮膺
===
茲選行將策名
天府入對
大廷布列在位則夫慎飭辭令宣
布忠誠敷求輔世之勲以恢
張
帝王之業亦皆爾多士之責也其
尚懋昭明德精白迺心庶幾
punctuated: 毋浮于爾言者乎？夫主司校閱，惟其文焉爾，其人固不可得而知也。國家取士，亦非徒以其藝焉爾，盖將欲得夫所謂賢人君子，登進勵翼，輔理承化，以共成正大光明之治。爾多士榮膺茲選，行將策名天府，入對大廷，布列在位，則夫慎飭辭令，宣布忠誠，敷求輔世之勲，以恢張帝王之業，亦皆爾多士之責也。其尚懋昭明德，精白迺心，庶幾
translation_en: …so that your words are not empty [?]? When the officials presiding over the examination assess the submissions, they see only the writing; they cannot truly know the people themselves. Nor does the state select men merely for their literary skill. Its purpose is to obtain those who may rightly be called worthy men and gentlemen, advance them to office, and have them exert themselves in its support, assist in government, and carry forward its transforming influence, together bringing about upright and enlightened rule. You scholars have had the honor of being chosen in this selection. Soon your names will be inscribed in the registers of the imperial government, you will appear before the great court to answer questions, and you will take your places in office. To be circumspect in your speech, give expression to your loyal sincerity, and strive widely for achievements that benefit the age, thereby extending the imperial enterprise—all these are also your responsibilities. May you strive to make your luminous virtue manifest and purify your hearts, in the hope that…

title: 嘉靖二十二年江西鄉試錄
text:
上不負
天子下不負所學俾永有辭于世
是
國家之楨也非天榮之幸也御
史與諸大夫之幸也其或非
然也御史與諸大夫亦既勞
止矣是天榮之罪也夫是天
榮之罪也夫於乎爾多士其
慎之哉
山東東昌府儒學教授葉天
榮謹序
punctuated:
上不負天子，下不負所學，俾永有辭于世。是國家之楨也，非天榮之幸也，御史與諸大夫之幸也。其或非然也，御史與諸大夫亦既勞止矣，是天榮之罪也夫！是天榮之罪也夫！於乎！爾多士其慎之哉！
山東東昌府儒學教授葉天榮謹序。
translation_en:
…so that, above, you do not fail the Son of Heaven and, below, do not fail what you have learned, enabling you forever to merit praise in the world. This is a mainstay of the state, not good fortune for me, Tianrong, but good fortune for the Censor and the other officials. Should it prove otherwise, the Censor and the other officials will have labored in vain, and the fault will be mine, Tianrong’s! The fault will be mine, Tianrong’s! Ah, you assembled scholars, take heed!
Preface respectfully composed by Ye Tianrong, Instructor in the Confucian School of Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong.

title: 嘉靖二十二年江西鄉試錄
text:
言足以信今而傳後雖以俟之萬世可也
其何五難之云邪是故春秋者經中之史
綱目者史中之經此萬世是非之權衡古
今史學之龜鑑而又何取於遷固乎
第四問
吳桂芳
同考試官教諭梁　批〔諡法書法聖王馭世之大權此作獨能發明其蘊雖使古人復生亦當不能辯析之矣讀之凜然〕
同考試官教諭李　批〔古雅雄渾眞爲有見之言知子他日必能完名矣敬服〕
同考試官教諭金　批〔古人兢兢業業作德日休中人以下不敢縱肆所恃者此耳不可不爲之防也是作得之〕
===
考試官教授葉　批〔明贍〕
考試官教授翟　批〔典則〕
天下有公道有公法道也者本人心之是
非不可得而易焉者也法也者立萬世之
權衡不可得而私焉者也道以維持其法
punctuated:
言足以信今而傳後，雖以俟之萬世可也。其何五難之云邪？是故《春秋》者，經中之史；《綱目》者，史中之經。此萬世是非之權衡，古今史學之龜鑑，而又何取於遷、固乎？

第四問
吳桂芳
同考試官教諭梁　批〔諡法、書法，聖王馭世之大權。此作獨能發明其蘊，雖使古人復生，亦當不能辯析之矣。讀之凜然。〕
同考試官教諭李　批〔古雅雄渾，眞爲有見之言。知子他日必能完名矣。敬服。〕
同考試官教諭金　批〔古人兢兢業業，作德日休；中人以下，不敢縱肆，所恃者此耳。不可不爲之防也。是作得之。〕
考試官教授葉　批〔明贍。〕
考試官教授翟　批〔典則。〕

天下有公道，有公法。道也者，本人心之是非，不可得而易焉者也；法也者，立萬世之權衡，不可得而私焉者也。道以維持其法
translation_en:
…these words suffice to command trust in the present and be transmitted to posterity; they may even await the judgment of ten thousand generations. Why, then, speak of the five difficulties? Thus the Spring and Autumn Annals is history among the classics, while the Outline and Details (Gangmu) is a classic among histories. These are the balance for weighing right and wrong for ten thousand generations, the authoritative mirror for historical scholarship past and present. What further need is there to draw upon Sima Qian and Ban Gu?

Fourth Policy Question
Wu Guifang

Associate Examiner Liang, Instructor, comments: 〔The rules for conferring posthumous names and the principles of historical writing are great instruments of authority by which sage kings govern the world. This essay alone brings their underlying meaning to light. Even if the ancients came back to life, they could hardly analyze the matter further. Reading it inspires awe.〕

Associate Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: 〔Classically elegant, powerful, and full: these are truly words of insight. I know that you will one day preserve your good name intact. I regard you with respect and admiration.〕

Associate Examiner Jin, Instructor, comments: 〔The ancients were vigilant and diligent, cultivating virtue and daily advancing in goodness; those of middling character and below dared not give themselves free rein. What they relied upon was precisely this. Restraints must therefore be established. This essay grasps the point.〕

Examiner Ye, Professor, comments: 〔Clear and ample.〕

Examiner Zhai, Professor, comments: 〔Classical and well ordered.〕

In the world there are impartial moral principles and impartial standards. Moral principles are rooted in the human heart’s sense of right and wrong and cannot be altered. Standards establish a balance for ten thousand generations and cannot be bent to private interests. Moral principles sustain those standards…

title: 嘉靖二十二年江西鄉試錄
text:
而法可久法以通變乎道而道可行古之
聖人所以綱維世道而砥礪士心者孰有
外於此者乎逮至三代而下君臣失綱務
爲一切苟簡之治而先王之典法湮缺而
不講然其公道公法之在天下不可泯没
至今猶爲可恃也又孰有要於謚法書法
者乎謚法孰始之記曰先王謚以尊名節
以一惠是謚法古未詳也而詳於周公謂
大戴禮所載是也書法孰始之記曰言則
===
左史書之動則右史書之是書法古亦未
嚴也而嚴於孔子謂假魯史以作春秋是
也然則周公以法行道而子孫百世不能
改孔子以道行法而亂臣賊子知所懼其
心一而已矣故曰勸得其道而天下樂爲
善懲得其道而天下懼爲惡又曰有德者
必褒而善自此可勸有罪者必貶而惡自
此可懲誠有見於道法之不相悖而不可
一日無者也周公孔子立百王不易之法
punctuated:
而法可久，法以通變乎道，而道可行。古之聖人所以綱維世道而砥礪士心者，孰有外於此者乎？逮至三代而下，君臣失綱，務爲一切苟簡之治，而先王之典法湮缺而不講。然其公道公法之在天下，不可泯没，至今猶爲可恃也。又孰有要於謚法書法者乎？
謚法孰始之？記曰：「先王謚以尊名，節以一惠。」是謚法古未詳也，而詳於周公，謂《大戴禮》所載是也。書法孰始之？記曰：「言則左史書之，動則右史書之。」是書法古亦未嚴也，而嚴於孔子，謂假魯史以作《春秋》是也。
然則周公以法行道，而子孫百世不能改；孔子以道行法，而亂臣賊子知所懼。其心一而已矣。故曰：「勸得其道，而天下樂爲善；懲得其道，而天下懼爲惡。」又曰：「有德者必褒，而善自此可勸；有罪者必貶，而惡自此可懲。」誠有見於道法之不相悖而不可一日無者也。周公孔子立百王不易之法
translation_en:
…and the standards can endure; through the standards, the Way is adapted to changing circumstances and can be put into practice. What means did the ancient sages employ to uphold the moral order of the world and temper the resolve of scholars that fell outside this? After the Three Dynasties, rulers and ministers lost their guiding principles and devoted themselves to makeshift, perfunctory government; the former kings’ institutions and standards fell into obscurity and disrepair and ceased to be studied. Yet the impartial Way and impartial standards existing in the world could not be obliterated, and even today they remain a source of support. What could be more essential than the rules for conferring posthumous names and the conventions of historical writing?
Who originated the rules for conferring posthumous names? The Record of Rites says: “The former kings used posthumous names to honor a person’s name, encapsulating his character in a single distinguishing quality.” These rules were not fully elaborated in antiquity, but were made detailed by Zhou Gong, the Duke of Zhou: this refers to what is recorded in the Elder Dai’s Record of Rites. Who originated the conventions of historical writing? The Record of Rites says: “When there were words, the Scribe of the Left recorded them; when there were actions, the Scribe of the Right recorded them.” These conventions, too, were not yet rigorous in antiquity, but were made rigorous by Kongzi, Confucius: this refers to his drawing on the historical records of Lu to compose the Spring and Autumn Annals.
Thus Zhou Gong employed standards to put the Way into practice, and descendants for a hundred generations could not alter them; Kongzi employed the Way to apply standards, and rebellious ministers and treacherous sons knew what to fear. Their intent was one and the same. Hence it is said: “When encouragement follows the proper way, all under Heaven delight in doing good; when punishment follows the proper way, all under Heaven fear doing evil.” It is also said: “Those who possess virtue must be praised, and thereby goodness can be encouraged; those who bear guilt must be censured, and thereby evil can be deterred.” These words indeed show an understanding that the Way and standards do not conflict and cannot be dispensed with for even a single day. Zhou Gong and Kongzi established standards that a hundred successive kings could not alter…

title: 嘉靖二十二年江西鄉試錄
text:
而使斯道乆而常存者又豈外於此哉三
代而下繼周公而作者有劉熙之書有來
奧之書有沈約之書有賀琛之書然而莫
詳於蘇洵繼孔子而作者有馬遷之書有
班固之書有子由之書有歐陽之書然而
莫嚴於綱目雖曰以人而傳亦以人而異
而卒以章章明顯不可掩覆此其徵效也
以書法言之楊雄漢臣也當其時以文學
顯未有如雄者乃甘心仕莽反爲美新符
===
命之作以誇耀之視之龔勝薛方其愧蓋
多矣故綱目以死書之而又曰莽大夫蓋
賊雄所以賊莽也雄自成帝時蓋已爲郎
矣而顧又莽之仕哉荀彧亦漢臣也以操
之姦而爲之腹心間關許下出畫奇策固
非不知操者則成操之簒者彧也乃欲以
正論尼之九錫之日以自附於殺身之義
良亦可憫矣故綱目以自殺爲文而又繫
之官者蓋曰操官之也彧之悔也蓋晚矣
punctuated:
而使斯道乆而常存者，又豈外於此哉？三代而下，繼周公而作者，有劉熙之書，有來奧之書，有沈約之書，有賀琛之書，然而莫詳於蘇洵。繼孔子而作者，有馬遷之書，有班固之書，有子由之書，有歐陽之書，然而莫嚴於《綱目》。雖曰以人而傳，亦以人而異，而卒以章章明顯，不可掩覆，此其徵效也。
以書法言之，楊雄，漢臣也。當其時，以文學顯，未有如雄者，乃甘心仕莽，反爲《美新》《符命》之作以誇耀之。視之龔勝、薛方，其愧蓋多矣。故《綱目》以死書之，而又曰「莽大夫」，蓋賊雄所以賊莽也。雄自成帝時，蓋已爲郎矣，而顧又莽之仕哉？荀彧亦漢臣也，以操之姦而爲之腹心，間關許下，出畫奇策，固非不知操者，則成操之簒者，彧也。乃欲以正論尼之九錫之日，以自附於殺身之義，良亦可憫矣。故《綱目》以自殺爲文，而又繫之官者，蓋曰操官之也。彧之悔也，蓋晚矣。
translation_en:
…and enabled this Way to endure through time: how could their achievement have lain outside this principle? After the Three Dynasties, those who wrote in succession to the Duke of Zhou included Liu Xi, Lai Ao [?], Shen Yue, and He Chen; yet none was more comprehensive than Su Xun. Those who wrote in succession to Confucius included Sima Qian, Ban Gu, Ziyou, and Ouyang; yet none was more rigorous than the Outline and Details (Gangmu). Although this tradition was transmitted through individuals and varied with them, it ultimately became plainly manifest and impossible to obscure. This is evidence of its efficacy.
To speak of historiographical conventions: Yang Xiong was a subject of the Han. In his day, no one equaled his literary renown. Yet he willingly served Wang Mang and even composed In Praise of the Xin and writings on auspicious mandates [?] to glorify him. Compared with Gong Sheng and Xue Fang, he surely had much to be ashamed of. Thus the Outline and Details records his end with the word “died” and further calls him “Wang Mang’s Grand Master.” Condemning Yang Xiong was a means of condemning Wang Mang. Yang Xiong had already become a Gentleman during Emperor Cheng’s reign; how could he then have entered Wang Mang’s service?
Xun Yu, too, was a subject of the Han. Despite Cao Cao’s treachery, he became his trusted confidant, laboring amid difficulties at Xu and devising ingenious strategies. He certainly was not ignorant of Cao Cao’s character; it was therefore Xun Yu who enabled Cao Cao’s usurpation. Yet, when the conferral of the Nine Bestowments was at hand, he sought to restrain him with principled arguments and thereby claim the righteousness of one who sacrifices his life. He was truly pitiable. Thus the Outline and Details uses the wording “killed himself,” while also attaching his official title, implying that it was Cao Cao who had appointed him. Xun Yu’s repentance came too late.

title: 嘉靖二十二年江西鄉試錄
text:
若雄者失身於其終而或者又失身於其
始君子不可不愼也陶潛博學不羣其令
彭澤也賦歸去來之辭而不爲折腰之辱
其高潔可知也然自以爲大尉侃之孫恥
屈身於劉宋至於書甲子以終其身嗟乎
晉亡矣而潛心乎晉故綱目以晉徵士書
之予其節也狄仁傑面折廷諍雖仕於周
而其母子姑姪孰親之譬足以感悟其心
其剛正可知也蒙恥奮忠卒取日於虞淵
===
嗟乎唐已周矣而仁傑又反而唐也故綱
目先書周以示臣法而卒繫之唐予其忠
也若潛之始終爲晉仁傑之始終爲唐是
以君子交予之也此非春秋之義乎蘇轍
所謂域中有三大而史之權與天與君竝
者此也以論法言之張良志本爲韓乃委
身於高祖運籌畫策輔成漢業是以有四
百年之安謂其有儒者氣象是矣論以文
成其誰曰不可然而黃石之惟君子或譏
punctuated:
若雄者，失身於其終，而或者又失身於其始，君子不可不愼也。陶潛博學不羣，其令彭澤也，賦《歸去來》之辭，而不爲折腰之辱，其高潔可知也。然自以爲大尉侃之孫，恥屈身於劉宋，至於書甲子以終其身。嗟乎！晉亡矣，而潛心乎晉，故《綱目》以晉徵士書之，予其節也。狄仁傑面折廷諍，雖仕於周，而其母子姑姪孰親之譬，足以感悟其心，其剛正可知也。蒙恥奮忠，卒取日於虞淵。嗟乎！唐已周矣，而仁傑又反而唐也，故《綱目》先書周，以示臣法，而卒繫之唐，予其忠也。若潛之始終爲晉，仁傑之始終爲唐，是以君子交予之也。此非《春秋》之義乎？蘇轍所謂「域中有三大，而史之權與天與君竝」者，此也。

以論法言之，張良志本爲韓，乃委身於高祖，運籌畫策，輔成漢業，是以有四百年之安。謂其有儒者氣象，是矣；論以文成，其誰曰不可？然而黃石之惟，君子或譏
translation_en:
Men like Yang Xiong compromised themselves at the end, while others compromised themselves at the beginning. A gentleman cannot be too cautious. Tao Qian was widely learned and stood apart from the crowd. When serving as magistrate of Pengze, he composed his Return Home! and refused the humiliation of bowing low; his lofty integrity is evident. Moreover, regarding himself as the grandson of Kan, the Grand Commandant, he felt ashamed to submit to the Liu Song dynasty, going so far as to date his writings by the sexagenary cycle for the rest of his life. Alas! Jin had fallen, yet Qian’s heart remained with Jin. Thus the Outline and Details (Gangmu) records him as a “summoned scholar of Jin,” acknowledging his integrity. Di Renjie openly challenged the ruler and remonstrated at court. Although he served Zhou, his comparison asking which bond was closer—that between mother and son or that between paternal aunt and nephew—was sufficient to awaken her understanding. His firmness and uprightness are evident. Enduring disgrace and exerting himself in loyalty, he ultimately retrieved the sun from the abyss of Yu, where it sets. Alas! Tang had already become Zhou, yet Renjie turned it back into Tang. Thus the Outline and Details first records him under Zhou to make clear the standard for a minister’s conduct, but ultimately associates him with Tang, acknowledging his loyalty. Since Qian remained devoted to Jin from beginning to end, and Renjie to Tang from beginning to end, the gentleman approves of them both. Is this not the meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals? This is what Su Zhe meant when he said, “Within the realm there are three great powers: the historian’s authority stands alongside Heaven and the ruler.”

Speaking of the principles of judgment, Zhang Liang’s original resolve was to serve Han, the former state. Yet he committed himself to Gaozu, devising strategies and plans and helping establish the Han dynasty’s enterprise, thereby bringing about four hundred years of peace. To say that he possessed the bearing of a Confucian scholar is correct. Who could object to judging him worthy of the posthumous title Wencheng, “Cultured and Accomplished” [?]? Yet as for his regard for Huangshi [?], some gentlemen criticize …

title: 嘉靖二十二年江西鄉試錄
text:
焉魏徵性本鯁直卒致身於太宗正色立
朝耻君不及堯舜是以有貞觀之盛謂其
直臣是矣謚以文貞以事太宗而言也忘
君事讐君子終耻焉就二子而言之子房
之功業元證之直言亦古人所難也賈充
蚤侯父爵不可謂不榮也主成濟之孛悖
以成司馬之篡處非其據徒有諂媚之容
蓋篡弑之賊也內外從亂曰荒君子猶不
能免於誅也而乃更之何哉許敬宗紉以
===
文名召用是亦可謂遭際矣揣高宗之昏
懦以助武昭儀之立謀殺忠良卒成唐室
之禍蓋姦佞之雄也名與實爽曰繆君子
猶以爲未盡也而亦更之又何邪就二子
而論之不更未足以誅惡更之亦反以彌
彰蓋後世不可掩也此非周公之法乎王
福疇所謂得失一朝榮辱千載者此也嗚
呼書法謚法之難又有不可得而輕重者
矣雖然謚法賜於君上太常得以定之而
punctuated:
焉。魏徵性本鯁直，卒致身於太宗，正色立朝，耻君不及堯舜，是以有貞觀之盛。謂其直臣，是矣；謚以文貞，以事太宗而言也。忘君事讐，君子終耻焉。就二子而言之，子房之功業、元證之直言，亦古人所難也。
賈充蚤侯父爵，不可謂不榮也。主成濟之孛悖，以成司馬之篡，處非其據，徒有諂媚之容，蓋篡弑之賊也。「內外從亂曰荒」，君子猶不能免於誅也，而乃更之，何哉？許敬宗紉以文名召用，是亦可謂遭際矣。揣高宗之昏懦，以助武昭儀之立，謀殺忠良，卒成唐室之禍，蓋姦佞之雄也。「名與實爽曰繆」，君子猶以爲未盡也，而亦更之，又何邪？就二子而論之，不更未足以誅惡，更之亦反以彌彰，蓋後世不可掩也。此非周公之法乎？王福疇所謂「得失一朝，榮辱千載」者，此也。
嗚呼！書法、謚法之難，又有不可得而輕重者矣。雖然，謚法賜於君上，太常得以定之，而
translation_en:
…in this regard. Wei Zheng was by nature forthright and unbending. He ultimately entered Taizong’s service, standing at court with a stern countenance and feeling ashamed if his ruler fell short of Yao and Shun. This brought about the flourishing rule of the Zhenguan era. To call him an upright minister is correct; to confer on him the posthumous title Wenzhen, “Cultured and Steadfast,” is to speak of his service to Taizong. Yet forgetting one’s ruler and serving his enemy remains shameful to the gentleman. Considering these two men, Zifang’s achievements and Yuanzheng’s [?] frank remonstrances were accomplishments difficult even for the ancients to attain.
Jia Chong early inherited his father’s rank as marquis: this could hardly be called lacking in honor. He directed Cheng Ji’s rebellious outrage to bring about the Sima clan’s usurpation. Occupying a position to which he had no rightful claim, he displayed only servile flattery; he was indeed a criminal guilty of usurpation and regicide. “To follow disorder both within and without is called Huang”—“Dissolute.” Even with this designation, the gentleman would not spare him condemnation. Why, then, was it changed? Xu Jingzong was summoned to office on account of his literary reputation [?]; this too may be called a fortunate opportunity. Gauging Gaozong’s benighted weakness, he helped bring about the elevation of Wu, Lady of Bright Deportment. He plotted the murder of loyal and worthy men, ultimately bringing calamity upon the Tang ruling house. He was a foremost practitioner of treachery and flattery. “When reputation and reality diverge, it is called Miu”—“False.” The gentleman would still consider this insufficient, yet this title too was changed. Why was that? Considering these two men, even leaving their titles unchanged would not have sufficed to condemn their wickedness; changing them, however, only made it still more conspicuous. It could not be concealed from later generations. Is this not the Duke of Zhou’s method? This is what Wang Fuchou meant by “Success and failure belong to a single day; honor and disgrace endure for a thousand years.”
Alas! The difficulties of historical writing and of assigning posthumous titles cannot simply be weighed as greater or lesser. Nevertheless, posthumous titles are bestowed by the sovereign, and the Court of Imperial Sacrifices is empowered to determine them, but…

title: 嘉靖二十二年江西鄉試錄
text:
權不可不謹書法雖後世之草茅亦得奮
筆以俟而論不可不公權有弗謹則請乞
風行而稱謂無稽如獨孤及之議呂諲梁
肅之議楊綰可愧也論有弗公則實錄微
而紀事不足信欲如趙盾不能改董狐之
筆崔氏不能奪南史之簡不可得也然則
欲復周公之法明孔子之旨使公道常明
於天下者豈無其要哉亦惟愼博采之至
公明臣工之實行祛好惡之私絶毀譽之
===
原由蘇洵以師周公之意使公論明於朝
著而後謚法可信也孜之以經史訪之於
衆議毋忌諱於簡牘毋出入於愛憎由朱
子以探孔子之旨使國是定於當時而後
書法有徵也如是則不必爵賞而人皆樂
爲善不必刑罰而人皆耻爲惡剛正之氣
可振而邪佞之風自息矣不然其能免於
踈濫之失乎此狂瞽之言也
第五問
punctuated:
權不可不謹。書法雖後世之草茅，亦得奮筆以俟，而論不可不公。權有弗謹，則請乞風行而稱謂無稽，如獨孤及之議呂諲、梁肅之議楊綰，可愧也。論有弗公，則實錄微而紀事不足信；欲如趙盾不能改董狐之筆、崔氏不能奪南史之簡，不可得也。然則欲復周公之法，明孔子之旨，使公道常明於天下者，豈無其要哉？亦惟愼博采之至公，明臣工之實行，祛好惡之私，絶毀譽之原，由蘇洵以師周公之意，使公論明於朝著，而後謚法可信也。孜之以經史，訪之於衆議，毋忌諱於簡牘，毋出入於愛憎，由朱子以探孔子之旨，使國是定於當時，而後書法有徵也。如是，則不必爵賞而人皆樂爲善，不必刑罰而人皆耻爲惡，剛正之氣可振，而邪佞之風自息矣。不然，其能免於踈濫之失乎？此狂瞽之言也。

第五問
translation_en:
…this authority must be exercised with care. As for the principles of historical writing, even men outside official service in later generations may take up the brush and await judgment, but their assessments must be impartial. If authority is exercised carelessly, requests and petitions become rampant, and the designations bestowed lack a sound basis. Such cases as Dugu Ji’s deliberation concerning Lü Yin and Liang Su’s concerning Yang Wan are shameful. If assessments are partial, truthful records decline and accounts of events become untrustworthy. It then becomes impossible to achieve what was seen when Zhao Dun could not alter Dong Hu’s writing and the Cui clan could not wrest away the bamboo slips of the Historian of the South.

Is there, then, no essential means of restoring the Duke of Zhou’s rules, elucidating Confucius’s intent, and keeping impartial justice ever manifest throughout the realm? One must carefully ensure the utmost impartiality in gathering information widely, ascertain officials’ actual conduct, dispel personal likes and dislikes, and cut off the sources of slander and flattery. By following Su Xun in taking the Duke of Zhou’s intent as a model, one can make impartial judgment manifest at court; only then can the rules for conferring posthumous names be trusted. One must diligently examine matters through the classics and histories [?], consult collective opinion, allow no fearful reticence in the written record, and neither add nor omit anything out of affection or hatred. By following Master Zhu in exploring Confucius’s intent, one can establish an authoritative public judgment in one’s own time; only then will historical writing have a sound basis.

If this is done, everyone will delight in doing good without needing the reward of rank, and everyone will be ashamed to do evil without needing punishment. The spirit of firmness and integrity can be revived, and the prevailing habits of wickedness and flattery will subside of themselves. Otherwise, how can errors of laxity and indiscriminate judgment be avoided? These are the words of a rash and unperceptive man.

Fifth Policy Question

title: 嘉靖二十二年江西鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭葉　批〔井田廢後世之法皆無可恃者〕
胡杰
義
國家立法最善然法久𡚁生存乎其人耳此作責成處最為得之故録
同考試官教諭廖　批〔明白詳盡時務策宜如此〕
同考試官學正黃　批〔責成守令更歸重於令甚〕
是
考試官教授葉　批〔詳明而切實〕
考試官教授翟　批〔撫𣪍之道盡矣〕
===
夫賦税之法與征輸之道此誠江西之民
憂而今時之急務也執事發策必欲操切
理要根極弊源嘉惠羣黎力追往哲此俊
傑之能辦而非樸樕之所明也雖然請毋
以空言相詡而以由衷自畢可乎先之以
作法之情次之以壞法之故求其影使之
因影以得形提其綱使之因綱以振目此
固承學區區之初而亦執事皇皇之臆也
蓋自井地之制大潰于秦均田之議不行
punctuated:
同考試官教諭葉批〔井田廢，後世之法皆無可恃者。〕
胡杰
義
國家立法最善，然法久𡚁生，存乎其人耳。此作責成處最為得之，故録。
同考試官教諭廖批〔明白詳盡，時務策宜如此。〕
同考試官學正黃批〔責成守令，更歸重於令，甚〕是。
考試官教授葉批〔詳明而切實。〕
考試官教授翟批〔撫𣪍之道盡矣。〕
夫賦税之法與征輸之道，此誠江西之民憂，而今時之急務也。執事發策，必欲操切理要，根極弊源，嘉惠羣黎，力追往哲。此俊傑之能辦，而非樸樕之所明也。雖然，請毋以空言相詡，而以由衷自畢，可乎？先之以作法之情，次之以壞法之故，求其影，使之因影以得形；提其綱，使之因綱以振目。此固承學區區之初，而亦執事皇皇之臆也。蓋自井地之制大潰于秦，均田之議不行
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Ye, Instructor: 〔Since the well-field system was abolished, none of the methods of later ages has been dependable.〕
Hu Jie
Exposition [yi]
The state's legislation is most excellent. Yet, as laws endure, abuses arise; everything depends upon the people who administer them. This composition is especially sound where it discusses assigning responsibility and demanding results; hence its inclusion.
Associate Examiner Liao, Instructor: 〔Clear and comprehensive: policy essays on current affairs should be like this.〕
Associate Examiner Huang, Instructor: 〔It holds prefects and county magistrates responsible, placing still greater weight upon the magistrates. Very〕 true.
Examiner Ye, Professor: 〔Detailed, clear, and practical.〕
Examiner Zhai, Professor: 〔The ways of caring for the people [?] are fully set forth.〕
Now, the system of taxation and the methods of collecting and delivering taxes are indeed a source of distress to the people of Jiangxi and an urgent concern of the present day. In setting this policy question, you surely intend to grasp the essentials of sound principle and probe the abuses to their very roots, generously to benefit the common people and strive to emulate the wise men of the past. This is something that outstanding talents can accomplish, but that an ordinary, unworthy person such as I cannot comprehend. Nevertheless, may I refrain from presenting empty words for your admiration and instead express fully what is in my heart? First I shall discuss the circumstances in which the laws were established, and then the reasons for their deterioration. I shall seek their shadows, so that through the shadows their forms may be discerned; I shall lift the net's main cord, so that by means of that cord all its meshes may be raised. This is indeed the humble original intention of one who has received instruction, and also the concern that so earnestly occupies your thoughts.
For, ever since the well-field system collapsed completely under the Qin, proposals for equalizing landholdings were not put into practice…

title: 嘉靖二十二年江西鄉試錄
text:
於漢唐人口分世業之法最爲近古矣安
史之亂海內雲擾版圖隳於避地賦法壞
於奉軍取之無定則徵之無定時誠如昔
人所論者我
國家以墾田定賦矣在地曰夏稅稅有差在
田曰秋粮粮有則所謂定法也因時起徵
矣稅始五月汔于秋粮始十月汔于冬所
謂定時也夫上之則壞而緣時所以宜民
而示之仁也下之力本以供賦所以急君
===
而示之義也上下相維仁義交至承學所
謂先之以作法之情者此也然民漓則偽
起法久則弊生偽起則日滋弊生則日壞
故變亂日興逋負日廣誠如執事所云者
夫變亂之故六一曰奇分二曰灑派三曰
擴飛四曰倒失五曰詭寓六曰懸虛奇分
者析子戶而無籍名灑派者愚小民而無
定數擴飛者過都越里而莫原其從倒失
者遞推轉收而莫見其止詭寓者先則於
punctuated:
於漢，唐人口分、世業之法最爲近古矣。安史之亂，海內雲擾，版圖隳於避地，賦法壞於奉軍，取之無定則，徵之無定時，誠如昔人所論者。我國家以墾田定賦矣，在地曰夏稅，稅有差；在田曰秋粮，粮有則，所謂定法也。因時起徵矣，稅始五月，汔于秋；粮始十月，汔于冬，所謂定時也。夫上之則壞而緣時，所以宜民而示之仁也；下之力本以供賦，所以急君而示之義也。上下相維，仁義交至，承學所謂先之以作法之情者，此也。
然民漓則偽起，法久則弊生；偽起則日滋，弊生則日壞。故變亂日興，逋負日廣，誠如執事所云者。夫變亂之故六：一曰奇分，二曰灑派，三曰擴飛，四曰倒失，五曰詭寓，六曰懸虛。奇分者，析子戶而無籍名；灑派者，愚小民而無定數；擴飛者，過都越里而莫原其從；倒失者，遞推轉收而莫見其止；詭寓者，先則於
translation_en:
…under the Han, the Tang system of per-capita allotments and hereditary holdings came closest to ancient practice. During the An Lushan and Shi Siming rebellion, turmoil spread throughout the realm. Flight to places of refuge disrupted the territorial and household registers, and provisioning armies undermined the taxation system. Exactions followed no fixed rules, and collection observed no fixed times, just as earlier writers have argued. Our dynasty has fixed tax assessments according to cultivated land. On land termed di, the levy is called the summer tax, with graded assessments; on fields termed tian, it is called autumn grain, with prescribed quotas. These are what we call fixed rules. Collection begins according to the season: the summer tax starts in the fifth month and runs into autumn; the grain levy starts in the tenth month and runs into winter. These are what we call fixed times. Those above adapt their rules to the times [?], thereby accommodating the people and showing them benevolence; those below devote their efforts to agriculture to supply taxes, thereby meeting their ruler’s urgent needs and showing righteousness. Above and below sustain one another, and benevolence and righteousness are both fully realized. This is what I, a student, meant by first examining the intentions behind the establishment of the laws.
Yet when the people become insincere, deception arises; when laws have long been in force, abuses develop. Once deception arises, it increases daily; once abuses develop, deterioration proceeds daily. Thus irregularities multiply day by day, and tax arrears grow ever greater, just as you have said. There are six causes of these irregularities: first, irregular subdivision (qifen); second, scattered apportionment (sapai); third, shifting assessments afar (kuofei) [?]; fourth, successive transfers and losses (daoshi) [?]; fifth, fictitious attachment (guiyu); and sixth, unsupported assessments (xuanxu). Irregular subdivision means splitting off subsidiary households without entering their names in the registers. Scattered apportionment means deceiving the common people and imposing no fixed amounts. Shifting assessments afar means carrying them across du and li administrative boundaries so that their origins cannot be traced. Successive transfers and losses means passing liabilities onward and transferring collection, with no discernible end. As for fictitious attachment, first …

title: 嘉靖二十二年江西鄉試錄
text:
絶貸𢦏數於流移托名於寄庄借頓於親
識附麗於權勢者是也懸虛者戶無考則
懸於戶爲戶虛里無考則懸於里爲里虛
都無考則懸於都爲都虛縣無考則懸於
縣爲縣虛者是也是六者里書之受賕而
豪強之爲害者也至於貧者採目前則減
畆自困愚民貪小利則抱納不推久漸湮
迷遂成逃絶豈獨豪強之罪哉逋負之故
五一曰予數緩二曰端緒繁三曰大戶持
===
四曰駔儈行五曰役累重吏胥恃賄而後
派故緩一糧十則以起徵故繁糧長圖覊
餘而大戶執本價故持孱弱者存畏難之
心壟斷者有泊制之術故駔儈行矣産廢
於賠虛而數不繼力分於借辦而用愈繁
故役累重矣此五者上下之因循而糧里
之交困者也至於積年敗役之營充貪官
汚吏之賄縱萬分僥倖一或蠲除豈獨侵
牟之罪哉承學所謂次之以壞法之故者
punctuated:
絶貸𢦏數於流移，托名於寄庄，借頓於親識，附麗於權勢者是也。懸虛者，戶無考則懸於戶，爲戶虛；里無考則懸於里，爲里虛；都無考則懸於都，爲都虛；縣無考則懸於縣，爲縣虛者是也。是六者，里書之受賕而豪強之爲害者也。至於貧者採目前，則減畆自困；愚民貪小利，則抱納不推，久漸湮迷，遂成逃絶。豈獨豪強之罪哉？

逋負之故五：一曰予數緩，二曰端緒繁，三曰大戶持，四曰駔儈行，五曰役累重。吏胥恃賄而後派，故緩；一糧十則以起徵，故繁；糧長圖覊餘，而大戶執本價，故持；孱弱者存畏難之心，壟斷者有泊制之術，故駔儈行矣；産廢於賠虛而數不繼，力分於借辦而用愈繁，故役累重矣。此五者，上下之因循而糧里之交困者也。至於積年敗役之營充，貪官汚吏之賄縱，萬分僥倖，一或蠲除，豈獨侵牟之罪哉？承學所謂次之以壞法之故者
translation_en:
…[opening words unclear: 絶貸𢦏數] assigning tax amounts to displaced persons [?], using names associated with outlying estates, lodging obligations with relatives and acquaintances, and attaching oneself to the powerful: these constitute fictitious registration. As for unsupported assessments: when an assessment cannot be verified against a household, it is left charged to that household, becoming a fictitious household assessment; when it cannot be verified within a li, it is left charged to that li, becoming a fictitious li assessment; when it cannot be verified within a du, it is left charged to that du, becoming a fictitious du assessment; and when it cannot be verified within a county, it is left charged to that county, becoming a fictitious county assessment. These six abuses arise from village clerks accepting bribes and powerful families doing harm. Yet poor people, looking only to their immediate circumstances, reduce their registered acreage and thereby bring hardship upon themselves. Ignorant commoners, coveting small gains, take on tax payments without transferring the registered liability. Over time the records become increasingly obscured and confused, and the households eventually become classified as absconded or extinct. Can the powerful families alone be blamed?

There are five causes of arrears: first, delays in issuing assessment figures; second, excessive procedural complexity; third, obstruction by substantial households; fourth, the activities of unscrupulous brokers; and fifth, heavy service burdens. Clerks wait for bribes before allocating assessments, hence the delays. A single grain-tax obligation is collected under ten assessment rates, hence the complexity. Tax captains seek to retain the surplus [?], while substantial households insist upon the base price, hence the obstruction. The weak fear the difficulties involved, while monopolists possess means of coercive control [?]; thus unscrupulous brokers flourish. Property is ruined by making good unsupported assessments, leaving insufficient resources to meet the amounts due; effort is diverted into borrowing to discharge obligations, while expenses grow ever more numerous. Thus service burdens become heavy. These five problems arise from habitual inaction at both higher and lower levels, bringing distress alike to tax captains and village communities. Moreover, men who have repeatedly defaulted in service scheme to secure appointments, while corrupt officials and clerks accept bribes and indulge them. They cling to the remotest hope that some remission might occur. Can the blame lie solely in embezzlement and exaction? What I, a student, referred to as ‘next, the causes by which the regulations are undermined’…

title: 嘉靖二十二年江西鄉試錄
text:
此也茲欲懸詭清而常賦不亂愚以爲丈
量之法可行也不可輕也歲造之法可舉
也不可據也天下之事無有盡利而無害
者計其分數則爲之故驗土膏均糧則使
貧富不至於甚偏清尺籍摘奸欺使繩墨
不至於大壞如此而已如欲盡利而無害
必復井田而後可而豈其時哉至欲逋侵
絕而常限不踰愚以爲遠年之逋可緩也
不可迫也近時之宄可懲也不可縱也蓋
===
天下之事未有盡法而無情者計其事勢
則爲之故任催年革端緒則事簡而民易
從治倉墨時派徵則法行而上可信如此
而已如欲盡法而無情必如桑孔而後可
而豈其道哉承學所謂求其影使之因影
以得形者凡此類也夫事至求影而不得
其形於乎執事之心亦困矣無已則愚請
以瞽說更其端可乎故夫探本之論三一
曰議差役二曰議法令三曰議責成何謂
punctuated:
此也。茲欲懸詭清而常賦不亂，愚以爲丈量之法可行也，不可輕也；歲造之法可舉也，不可據也。天下之事，無有盡利而無害者，計其分數則爲之。故驗土膏，均糧則，使貧富不至於甚偏；清尺籍，摘奸欺，使繩墨不至於大壞，如此而已。如欲盡利而無害，必復井田而後可，而豈其時哉？至欲逋侵絕而常限不踰，愚以爲遠年之逋可緩也，不可迫也；近時之宄可懲也，不可縱也。蓋天下之事，未有盡法而無情者，計其事勢則爲之。故任催年，革端緒，則事簡而民易從；治倉墨，時派徵，則法行而上可信，如此而已。如欲盡法而無情，必如桑孔而後可，而豈其道哉？承學所謂求其影，使之因影以得形者，凡此類也。
夫事至求影而不得其形，於乎，執事之心亦困矣！無已，則愚請以瞽說更其端，可乎？故夫探本之論三：一曰議差役，二曰議法令，三曰議責成。何謂
translation_en:
…this is what I mean. Now, if we wish to clear up fictitious and concealed tax registrations [?] without disrupting the regular taxes, I submit that land measurement may be implemented, but must not be undertaken lightly; annual compilation of the registers may be instituted, but must not be relied upon as conclusive. In the affairs of the world, nothing brings benefits alone without harm. One must weigh their relative proportions and then act. Thus, examine the fertility of the soil and equalize the grain-tax rates, so that the burden does not fall too unevenly upon rich and poor; put the land registers in order and expose fraud, so that established standards are not gravely undermined. That is all. If one desires benefits alone without harm, this would require restoring the well-field system. But is this the time for that?
As for wishing to eliminate arrears and embezzlement and ensure that regular deadlines are not exceeded, I submit that arrears from long ago may be dealt with leniently and must not be pressed for urgently; recent wrongdoing must be punished and must not be tolerated. In the affairs of the world, the law has never been applied to the utmost without regard for human circumstances. One must weigh the circumstances and then act. Thus, entrust collection to the annual collection officers [?] and eliminate procedural complications: affairs will become simpler and the people will find it easier to comply. Punish corruption in the granaries and apportion and collect taxes at the proper times: the law will then be enforced and the authorities will command trust. That is all. If one desires the utmost application of the law without regard for human circumstances, one would have to act like Sang and Kong. But is that the proper way? These are all instances of what I, a student, have called seeking the shadow so as to find the form through it.
When matters reach the point where one seeks the shadow yet cannot find the form, alas, your mind, honored sir, must also be sorely troubled! If we must pursue the matter further, may I offer my unenlightened views and approach it from a different starting point? There are three discussions that probe the root: first, a discussion of labor-service assignments; second, a discussion of laws and ordinances; third, a discussion of holding officials responsible for results. What is meant by…

title: 嘉靖二十二年江西鄉試錄
text:
