議差役夫爲弊者勢也非民之情也江西
之役稱最難者糧長也故凡樂爲糧長者
皆民之蠹也其次如聽解大戶驛傳頭戶
之類甚難也故凡樂爲是役者皆民之蠹
也斯役之來皆足以覆人故其爲弊之初
心以避役也非以避稅也及其久而不可
核則其流者也今擇糧長關合而領批使
里長催徵而均解附帶幇補聽其自便而
官寔親焉不可乎大戶頭戶之類凡其役
===
之難者皆量其體裁而寬其分數不可乎
治民者每求民之所不便而推移之以服
其心以平其情吾知驅之爲弊不爲也何
謂議法今欺隱有没入之法抗違有遷徙
之法稽越有遍謫之法貪贓有大刑之法
令則上下狥姑息而法之不盡行者固多
矣是惟服民之心平民之情而後盡我之
法焉斯不怨故法令次之何謂議責成今
之居官視爲傳舍而不顧者非意也責成
punctuated:
議差役？夫爲弊者勢也，非民之情也。江西之役稱最難者，糧長也。故凡樂爲糧長者，皆民之蠹也。其次，如聽解大戶、驛傳頭戶之類，甚難也。故凡樂爲是役者，皆民之蠹也。斯役之來，皆足以覆人，故其爲弊之初心，以避役也，非以避稅也。及其久而不可核，則其流者也。今擇糧長關合而領批，使里長催徵而均解，附帶幇補，聽其自便，而官寔親焉，不可乎？大戶、頭戶之類，凡其役之難者，皆量其體裁而寬其分數，不可乎？治民者每求民之所不便，而推移之，以服其心，以平其情，吾知驅之爲弊不爲也。
何謂議法？今欺隱有没入之法，抗違有遷徙之法，稽越有遍謫之法，貪贓有大刑之法。令則上下狥姑息，而法之不盡行者固多矣。是惟服民之心，平民之情，而後盡我之法焉，斯不怨，故法令次之。
何謂議責成？今之居官，視爲傳舍而不顧者，非意也，責成
translation_en:
…discussing labor-service assignments? Abuses arise from circumstances, not from the people's natural inclinations. Of the service duties in Jiangxi, that of grain chief is reputed to be the most burdensome. Thus, all who willingly become grain chiefs are parasites upon the people. Next come such duties as those of major households awaiting assignment to transport tax payments and head households responsible for postal-relay service; these too are very burdensome. Thus, all who willingly undertake these duties are parasites upon the people. Any of these assignments can ruin a person. Consequently, people's original intention in resorting to abuses is to escape service, not to evade taxes. When, after a long time, matters can no longer be verified, that is a subsequent development.
Could we not now select grain chiefs to coordinate their responsibilities and receive the official warrants [?], have the village headmen press for collection and share the work of remittance equally, allow them to arrange supplementary assistance as they find convenient, and have the officials themselves actually oversee the work? For major households, head households, and the like, wherever their duties are burdensome, could we not assess the nature of those duties and reduce their allotted shares? If those who govern the people continually identify what causes them hardship and adjust arrangements accordingly, thereby winning their willing acceptance and settling their feelings, I know that even if driven to commit abuses, they would not do so.
What is meant by discussing the laws? At present, there are laws of confiscation for fraudulent concealment, laws of forced relocation for defiance and disobedience, laws of banishment [?] for delays and transgressions, and laws imposing severe punishment for corruption and illicit gains. Yet [?] superiors and subordinates alike indulge in undue leniency, and there are indeed many laws that are not fully enforced. Only after winning the people's willing acceptance and settling their feelings should we fully enforce our laws; then there will be no resentment. This is why laws and ordinances come second.
What is meant by discussing accountability for results? That officials today regard their offices as posting stations and give them no care is not a matter of intention; the means of holding them accountable…

title: 嘉靖二十二年江西鄉試錄
text:
之術不專且不至也然其急者在守令而
令之視守尤切爲何則其地近其分親也
地近則易知分親則易洽故爲令者苟加
志於民何民弗濟苟存心於事何事弗成
自定賦言之由戶總以核里總里總核都
總都總核縣總而縣之實徵可知矣由縣
虛以求都虛都虛求里虛里虛求戶虛而
縣之虛數可知矣自起徵言之給戶由立
約劑凡折直皆入於官帑而不入於糧里
===
之手則輸直者無負矣脩倉庾信期會凡
本粟皆入於官廥而不入於駔儈之手則
輸粟者無負矣近固有行之而甚效者在
賢令一加之意耳愚請著爲甲凡縣令之
至者毋束以期會薄書之煩而以清糧專
責之計其縣虛三分之以斃吏治每歲縣
登其清出之數以上之府府有要府以上
之司司有成司以上之撫按撫按有會會
則計其清出之通以下上其考大要察其
punctuated:
之術不專且不至也。然其急者在守令，而令之視守尤切。爲何？則其地近，其分親也。地近則易知，分親則易洽。故爲令者，苟加志於民，何民弗濟？苟存心於事，何事弗成？

自定賦言之，由戶總以核里總，里總核都總，都總核縣總，而縣之實徵可知矣。由縣虛以求都虛，都虛求里虛，里虛求戶虛，而縣之虛數可知矣。自起徵言之，給戶由，立約劑，凡折直皆入於官帑，而不入於糧里之手，則輸直者無負矣。脩倉庾，信期會，凡本粟皆入於官廥，而不入於駔儈之手，則輸粟者無負矣。近固有行之而甚效者，在賢令一加之意耳。

愚請著爲甲，凡縣令之至者，毋束以期會薄書之煩，而以清糧專責之。計其縣虛，三分之，以斃吏治。每歲縣登其清出之數，以上之府，府有要；府以上之司，司有成；司以上之撫按，撫按有會。會則計其清出之通，以下上其考。大要察其
translation_en:
…the methods for holding officials accountable are neither focused nor thorough. The most urgent need concerns prefects and district magistrates, and among these it is especially pressing for magistrates. Why? Because they are close to the locality and their responsibilities bring them into intimate contact with its people. Proximity makes understanding easier; close relations make harmony easier. Thus, if a magistrate devotes his attention to the people, who among them will not receive relief? If he applies himself to administrative affairs, what business will remain unfinished?

As for fixing tax assessments, use household totals to verify village totals, village totals to verify township totals, and township totals to verify the district total: the district’s actual collectible revenue can then be known. Starting from the district’s unsupported assessments, trace those of the townships; from the townships, trace those of the villages; and from the villages, trace those of individual households. The amount of unsupported assessments in the district can then be known. As for initiating collection, issue tax notices to households and establish written agreements. Let all payments commuted into money enter the public treasury, rather than pass through the hands of grain-tax and village headmen; then those paying in money will suffer no loss. Repair the granaries and keep faithfully to the appointed collection dates. Let all grain paid in kind enter the public granaries, rather than pass through the hands of brokers; then those delivering grain will suffer no loss. Recently there have indeed been cases in which these measures were implemented with excellent results. It requires only that a worthy magistrate give the matter his attention.

I humbly request that this be established as a regulation [?]. Whenever a district magistrate takes office, do not bind him with the burdens of deadlines and paperwork, but assign him specific responsibility for clearing up the grain-tax accounts. Calculate his district’s unsupported assessments and divide them into three portions, using this to judge his administration [?]. Each year the district should record the amount it has cleared up and submit it to the prefecture, which should compile a summary. The prefecture should submit this to the Provincial Administration Commission, which should compile a completed account. The commission should submit it to the Grand Coordinator and Regional Inspector, who should compile a consolidated account. On consolidation, calculate the total amount cleared up and use it to lower or raise the magistrate’s performance rating. The essential point is to examine his…

title: 嘉靖二十二年江西鄉試錄
text:
觔法者先去之而半登者爲稱格至於一
歲起徵之數雖升斗不盡亦懲焉積之以
三年之通而縣虛絕歲輸無奇者聽其代
否則叙詰之此則地官螽嘗一行而遽輟
者夫使上之人內則堅執競之心外則嚴
淑慝之令吾知數年之間必有可觀者出
焉而丈量歲造之法或不戒而畢行矣承
學所謂操其綱使之循綱以振目者此類
也故夫緣情以作法法勝則傷仁立法以
===
制情情勝則害義由仁義以立政則政行
矣酌情法以宜民則民化矣此固草茅之
所談也若夫宗本前哲之規模參考歷代
之利害如陸贄所稱放名田而爲之限
不驚民不動衆不用井田之制而獲井田
之利如蘇軾所論此則執事之責也固非
承學所逮也幸與進而明教之
punctuated: 觔法者，先去之，而半登者爲稱格。至於一歲起徵之數，雖升斗不盡，亦懲焉。積之以三年之通，而縣虛絕、歲輸無奇者，聽其代；否則叙詰之。此則地官螽嘗一行而遽輟者。夫使上之人內則堅執競之心，外則嚴淑慝之令，吾知數年之間必有可觀者出焉，而丈量歲造之法或不戒而畢行矣。承學所謂操其綱，使之循綱以振目者，此類也。故夫緣情以作法，法勝則傷仁；立法以制情，情勝則害義。由仁義以立政，則政行矣；酌情法以宜民，則民化矣。此固草茅之所談也。若夫宗本前哲之規模，參考歷代之利害，如陸贄所稱放名田而爲之限，不驚民，不動衆，不用井田之制而獲井田之利，如蘇軾所論，此則執事之責也，固非承學所逮也。幸與進而明教之。
translation_en:
…those who violate the law [?] should first be removed, while those who recover half should be deemed to meet the standard. As for the amount assessed for collection in a given year, punishment should follow even if a sheng or a dou remains unpaid. Taking the aggregate over three years, if a county’s shortfall has been eliminated and its annual remittances leave no balance outstanding, its magistrate should be permitted to leave office upon replacement; otherwise, he should be questioned according to a graded procedure. This is a measure that the fiscal authorities [?] once implemented but abruptly discontinued.

If those above inwardly maintain a firm resolve to exert themselves [?] and outwardly enforce strict orders distinguishing the good from the wicked, I know that within a few years results worth seeing will emerge. The procedures for surveying land and compiling annual registers might then be fully carried out even without further injunctions. This is the sort of thing that I, a student, mean by grasping the main cord and having people follow it to draw the meshes of the net into order. Thus, when laws are framed in accordance with human circumstances, allowing law to prevail excessively injures benevolence; when laws are established to regulate human circumstances, allowing those circumstances to prevail excessively harms righteousness. Establish government through benevolence and righteousness, and its measures will take effect; weigh circumstances against law to suit the people’s needs, and the people will be transformed. These, admittedly, are the views of one outside official life.

As for taking the designs of earlier worthies as one’s foundation and examining the benefits and harms of successive dynasties—for example, permitting private landholding while setting limits upon it, as Lu Zhi advocated, and obtaining the benefits of the well-field system without alarming the people, mobilizing the populace, or employing that system itself, as Su Shi discussed—this is your responsibility, gentlemen. It is certainly beyond the reach of a student such as myself. I hope you will allow me to advance further and give me your illuminating instruction.

title: 嘉靖二十二年江西鄉試錄
text:
江西鄉試錄後序
嘉靖癸卯江西鄉試錄成教
授翟表序之備矣御史揖〔天〕
〔榮〕使申告曰
聖天子嗣大歷服惟今二十有二
載此邦盖凡八賔興矣得人
之盛爲天下稱首豈直山川
===
產才之良實惟
文明弘賁覃布其耿光休烈以又
寧區宇多士用是遭際
昌期罔不含英茹華負鳴世之志
始〔天〕〔榮〕之入院校籌也觀於
初試見其根據經傳不鑿不
浮嘆曰懿哉斯其有得聖賢
punctuated:
江西鄉試錄後序

嘉靖癸卯江西鄉試錄成，教授翟表序之備矣。御史揖〔天〕〔榮〕，使申告曰：

「聖天子嗣大歷服，惟今二十有二載。此邦盖凡八賔興矣，得人之盛，爲天下稱首。豈直山川產才之良？實惟文明弘賁，覃布其耿光休烈，以又寧區宇。多士用是遭際昌期，罔不含英茹華，負鳴世之志。始〔天〕〔榮〕之入院校籌也，觀於初試，見其根據經傳，不鑿不浮，嘆曰：『懿哉！斯其有得聖賢
translation_en:
Afterword to the Record of the Jiangxi Provincial Examination

The Record of the Jiangxi Provincial Examination for the guimao year of Jiajing (1543) was completed, and Instructor Zhai Biao had supplied a comprehensive preface. The censor bowed to me, Tianrong, and asked me to add this further statement:

“The sagely Son of Heaven succeeded to the great imperial mandate twenty-two years ago. This province has now held eight examinations to honor and advance worthy men. Its abundant recruitment of talent is acclaimed as foremost in the realm. Can this be due merely to the excellence of the talent nurtured by its mountains and rivers? It is truly because imperial cultural brilliance has splendidly adorned the land, spreading its radiant light and glorious achievements far and wide to bless [?] and pacify the realm. Thus the many scholars have encountered a flourishing age. All have imbibed the finest cultural nourishment and cherish the ambition to make their voices heard in the world.

“When I, Tianrong, first entered the examination compound to assess the submissions [?], I examined the work from the first session and saw that it was grounded in the classics and their commentaries, neither forced nor superficial. I exclaimed: ‘How admirable! Surely they have grasped the sages’ and worthies’ …

title: 嘉靖二十二年江西鄉試錄
text:
之訓乎再試之見其雄深典
雅動閑矩度嘆曰富哉文乎
其兼尚世之體裁乎三試之
則見其鋪敘今古陳説世務
出入乎百家子史之言根極
理要愈叩之而愈不匱則又
嘆曰渢渢乎美矣至矣通儒
===
之義備矣豈三代之遺乎旣
乃仰而思之則又作而嘆曰
夫文安從生哉言者心之聲
也文言之粹也聖人之道藴
之爲德行發之爲事業今多
士之文郁郁乎盛矣抑不知
其中所藴果皆光明俊偉以

translation_en:
…the teachings of the sages and worthies?” On examining them a second time, they found their writing powerful, profound, classically elegant, and at every turn observant of proper standards. They exclaimed: “How rich this writing is! Does it also encompass the literary forms esteemed through the ages[?]?” On examining them a third time, they found that the candidates set forth matters ancient and modern, discussed contemporary affairs, and ranged freely through the writings of the various schools, philosophers, and historians, probing principles to their roots and essentials. The more deeply they questioned them, the more inexhaustible their resources proved. They exclaimed again: “How richly resonant! How fine, how consummate! All the understanding of a thoroughly learned Confucian scholar is present here. Could this be a legacy of the Three Dynasties?”
Then they looked upward in reflection, rose, and sighed once more: “Where does literary composition come from? Speech is the voice of the heart; literary composition is the essence of speech. The Way of the sages, when stored within, constitutes virtuous conduct; when expressed outwardly, it becomes practical achievement. title: 嘉靖二十二年江西鄉試錄
text:
毋浮于爾言者乎夫主司校
閱惟其文焉爾其人固不可
得而知也
國家取士亦非徒以其藝焉爾
蓋將欲得夫所謂賢人君子
登進勵翼輔理承化以共成
正大光明之治爾多士榮膺
===
茲選行將策名
天府入對
大廷布列在位則夫慎飭辭令宣
布忠誠敷求輔世之勲以恢
張
帝王之業亦皆爾多士之責也其
尚懋昭明德精白迺心庶幾
punctuated:
毋浮于爾言者乎？夫主司校閱，惟其文焉爾，其人固不可得而知也。

國家取士，亦非徒以其藝焉爾，蓋將欲得夫所謂賢人君子，登進勵翼，輔理承化，以共成正大光明之治。爾多士榮膺茲選，行將策名天府，入對大廷，布列在位，則夫慎飭辭令，宣布忠誠，敷求輔世之勲，以恢張帝王之業，亦皆爾多士之責也。其尚懋昭明德，精白迺心，庶幾
translation_en:
…so that your words do not exceed what is within you? Those presiding over the examination assess only the candidates’ writings; they cannot truly know the men themselves.

In selecting men for office, the state likewise does not look merely to their literary skill. Its purpose is to find those whom we call worthy men and gentlemen, advance them to office, and have them exert themselves in support, assist in governance, and carry forward its transforming influence, together bringing about upright and enlightened rule. You scholars have been honored with selection in this examination. Soon you will have your names inscribed in the imperial registers, present your answers at the great court, and take your places in office. Then, to be circumspect in your official utterances, give expression to your loyal sincerity, and seek far and wide opportunities for meritorious service to the realm, thereby extending the imperial enterprise—all these will be your responsibilities. title: 嘉靖二十二年江西鄉試錄
text:
上不負
天子下不負所學俾永有辭于世
是
國家之楨也非〔天榮〕之幸也御
史與諸大夫之幸也其或非
然也御史與諸大夫亦既勞
止矣是〔天榮〕之罪也夫是〔天
榮〕之罪也夫於乎爾多士其
慎之哉
山東東昌府儒學教授葉〔天
榮〕謹序
punctuated:
上不負天子，下不負所學，俾永有辭于世。是國家之楨也，非〔天榮〕之幸也，御史與諸大夫之幸也。其或非然也，御史與諸大夫亦既勞止矣，是〔天榮〕之罪也夫！是〔天榮〕之罪也夫！於乎，爾多士其慎之哉！
山東東昌府儒學教授葉〔天榮〕謹序。
translation_en:
…above, you will not fail the Son of Heaven, and below, you will not betray what you have learned, so that you may forever have an honorable account to give before the world. You will thus be pillars of the state. This is good fortune not for Tianrong alone, but for the Censor and the other officials. If, however, it should prove otherwise, the Censor and the other officials will have labored in vain, and the fault will be Tianrong’s! The fault will be Tianrong’s! Ah, you scholars, take heed!
Respectfully prefaced by Ye Tianrong 葉天榮, Instructor at the Confucian School of Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong.
